glosses.meaningKo: 잠에서 깨다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop sleeping and become awake
glosses.sourceDescription: same as wake
examples: I wake up when sunlight reaches my room.
Mina woke up a few minutes before her alarm.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 어떤 것에 동의하도록 설득하는 데 성공하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in persuading someone to agree to something
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in persuading someone to agree to something
examples: I'll try to talk him round.
We haven't managed to talk him round.

glosses.meaningKo: 정기적으로 가는 곳에서 자주 사람을 발견하기
glosses.englishDescription: to notice someone often in places that you go to regularly
glosses.sourceDescription: to notice someone often in places that you go to regularly
examples: We hardly ever see you around here.
I haven't seen her around here.

glosses.meaningKo: 쳐서 넘어뜨리다
glosses.englishDescription: to hit or push something so that it falls
glosses.sourceDescription: same as knock down
examples: I accidentally knocked over the vase.
Tom knocked over the vase.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 위해 많은 돈을 쓰기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to spend a lot of money on something
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend a lot of money on something
examples: Since they wouldn’t share, I ended up shelling out for two hotel rooms.
Tara was not a jewellery person, which was just as well because Finn certainly didn't have the money to shell out on chunky gold stuff.

glosses.meaningKo: 형태를 갖추며 진행되어 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to develop
glosses.sourceDescription: to develop
examples: The class project is shaping up nicely.
Our weekend plans shaped up better than expected.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 원하지 않을 때 상황에 휘말리게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone become involved in a situation when they do not want to
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone become involved in a situation when they do not want to
examples: Last night it was the turn of the evangelical Christians to be dragged in.
More worrying still were signs that France, too, was being dragged in.

glosses.meaningKo: 갑자기 특정 상태나 상황에 빠지기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly get into a particular state or situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly get into a particular state or situation
examples: The city was plunged into total darkness when the entire electrical system failed.
The country is plunging into recession once more.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가 그만하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to stop doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop doing something
examples: Give over making that noise!
‘You know how fond I am of you.’ ‘Oh, give over, will you?’

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 곳으로 가거나 여행하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to go or travel to different places
glosses.sourceDescription: to go or travel to different places
examples: At the age of 85 Milly still gets around quite well.
He said: 'I can't get around my flat without the wheelchair.'

glosses.meaningKo: 더 큰 조각에서 무언가를 자르고 제거하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to remove something from a larger piece by cutting
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove something from a larger piece by cutting
examples: I cut this article out of a magazine for you.
Using the 5cm cutter, cut out six circles from the rectangular cake.

glosses.meaningKo: 여기저기 이동하다
glosses.englishDescription: to travel or move from place to place
glosses.sourceDescription: same as get around
examples: In Copenhagen it's just a pleasant way of getting about.
You really need a car to get about here.

glosses.meaningKo: 법이나 규정을 피해 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to avoid a law or rule by finding a way around it
glosses.sourceDescription: same as get around
examples: But his promise to try to get round human rights laws was undermined by his own Immigration Minister.
It got round the law and alerted us to what is going on in our neighbourhood.

glosses.meaningKo: 사업장이나 시설의 운영을 중단하다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop a business or facility from operating
glosses.sourceDescription: same as close
examples: Hotels are closing down all over the country.
Their intention is to close down the factory.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 혼란스러운 상황을 대처하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to deal with a problem or a confused situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal with a problem or a confused situation
examples: A team of accountants was brought in to straighten out the firm’s finances.
He had still not had time to straighten out his own thoughts.

glosses.meaningKo: 여행을 계속하지 않고 당신이 온 것과 같은 방식으로 돌아가거나, 누군가가 이것을 하도록 만들기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to return the same way that you came instead of continuing on your journey, or to make someone do this
glosses.sourceDescription: to return the same way that you came instead of continuing on your journey, or to make someone do this
examples: Bad weather forced them to turn back.
I got up and walked and followed the river a long way and then turned back again.

glosses.meaningKo: 상황을 대처하기 어려울 때 도움을 받기 위해 누군가에게 가는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to go to someone for help when you are having difficulty dealing with a situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to someone for help when you are having difficulty dealing with a situation
examples: I’m sorry, but I had no one else to turn to.
There are plenty of people you can turn to for advice.

glosses.meaningKo: 필요 없는 것을 버리다
glosses.englishDescription: to get rid of something that is no longer wanted
glosses.sourceDescription: same as throw away
examples: I’ve thrown out my old boots.
She hadn't seen him throw out a perfectly good egg cup because it had got a little chip on the rim.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람을 내려 주거나 물건을 갖다 놓다
glosses.englishDescription: to take someone or something to a place and leave them there
glosses.sourceDescription: same as drop
examples: Can you drop the kids off at school this morning?
Is it ok if I drop the documents off later?

glosses.meaningKo: 특별한 일 없이 머물거나 지체하다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend time somewhere without doing much, or to delay leaving
glosses.sourceDescription: same as hang
examples: We hung about near the library after class.
Do not hang about, or we will miss the bus.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 일을 거친 끝에 특정 장소나 상황에 이르다
glosses.englishDescription: to be in a particular place or situation at the end of a long series of events
glosses.sourceDescription: to be in a particular place or situation at the end of a long series of events
examples: We finished up back at school after the field trip.
After several stops, we finished up at the station.

glosses.meaningKo: 실수를 하거나, 누군가를 실수하게 하기 위해서요
glosses.englishDescription: to make a mistake, or to cause someone to make a mistake
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a mistake, or to cause someone to make a mistake
examples: I tripped up on a couple of questions.
The tests are designed to trip you up.

glosses.meaningKo: 식혀 온도를 낮추다; 식다
glosses.englishDescription: to become cooler or to make something cooler
glosses.sourceDescription: same as cool
examples: The rain had cooled everything down.
We had to wait until the engine had cooled down before restarting the car.

glosses.meaningKo: 건물 문과 창문을 모두 잠그고 아무도 들어갈 수 없도록 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to lock all the doors and windows of a building so that no one can get in
glosses.sourceDescription: to lock all the doors and windows of a building so that no one can get in
examples: I locked up and went to bed.
It took me just a couple of minutes to retrieve the disc and lock up again.

glosses.meaningKo: 동전을 던져 결정하다
glosses.englishDescription: to throw a coin into the air, often to make a decision
glosses.sourceDescription: same as toss
examples: Let’s toss up to decide who drives.
Neil tossed the penny up; she called ‘heads’ and won.

glosses.meaningKo: 개인적인 감정과 경험에 대해 더 많이 이야기하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to talk more about your personal feelings and experiences
glosses.sourceDescription: to talk more about your personal feelings and experiences
examples: It’s taken a few months, but Katy is finally starting to open up to me.
She concentrated her attention on getting Richard to open up about himself.

glosses.meaningKo: 육지의 가장자리를 도는 대신 육지의 한 지역을 가로질러 가는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to go across an area of land instead of going around the edge of it
glosses.sourceDescription: to go across an area of land instead of going around the edge of it
examples: He left his car up the road and cut across the fields on foot.
We cut across the field to save time.

glosses.meaningKo: 일련의 사건들 후에 마침내 장소나 상황에 도달하기
glosses.englishDescription: to finally arrive at a place or situation after a series of events
glosses.sourceDescription: to finally arrive at a place or situation after a series of events
examples: We finally landed up at Tom’s house.
We happened to land up just at the wrong party spot," said Gareth.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 당신이 지불하지 않기를 원할 때, 무언가를 지불하기 위해 돈을 주는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to give money to pay for something, especially when you would prefer not to
glosses.sourceDescription: to give money to pay for something, especially when you would prefer not to
examples: Come on, cough up, it’s your turn to pay.
I had to cough up for the medical bills.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 돈을 지불해서 협박하거나 협박하는 것을 멈추도록 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to pay someone to stop threatening you or blackmailing you
glosses.sourceDescription: to pay someone to stop threatening you or blackmailing you
examples: By the time the public discovers that a product is defective, the company has made so much money it can afford to buy off the victims.
Efforts to buy her off have failed.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 줄이기 위해, 특히 당신이 쓰는 돈을 줄이기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce the amount of something, especially money that you spend
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce the amount of something, especially money that you spend
examples: If you cut back on fat and sugar, you’ll lose weight.
We’re trying to cut back on the amount we spend on food.

glosses.meaningKo: 공문서의 빈 공간에 이름이나 주소 등의 정보를 추가하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to add information such as your name or address in the empty spaces on an official document
glosses.sourceDescription: to add information such as your name or address in the empty spaces on an official document
examples: I spent over two hours filling in the application form.
Please fill in your name and address in the space provided.

glosses.meaningKo: 텐트나 다른 쉼터가 있거나 없는 밖에서 잠을 자기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to sleep outside, with or without a tent or other shelter
glosses.sourceDescription: to sleep outside, with or without a tent or other shelter
examples: He planned to camp out in the wild.
They camped out on the pavement in front of his office.

glosses.meaningKo: 자기 주위에 싸여 있는 것을 평평하게 만들기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make something that is wrapped around itself become flat
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something that is wrapped around itself become flat
examples: Roll out the pizza dough on a well-floured surface.
She rolled out the document on the table.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 가지 또는 여러 장소를 함께하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to join several things or places together
glosses.sourceDescription: to join several things or places together
examples: I’ve connected the modem up to the phone line.
The plumber came and connected up the dishwasher.

glosses.meaningKo: 선, 울타리, 밧줄 등을 사용하여 영역의 한계를 표시합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to mark the limits of an area using a line, fence, rope etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to mark the limits of an area using a line, fence, rope etc
examples: The crime scene was marked off with official police tape.
The various Moties used the lines to mark off their territories.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 속도를 늦추거나 무언가가 속도를 늦추면, 그들은 덜 활동적이거나 효과적이 된다
glosses.englishDescription: if someone slows down, or if something slows them down, they become less active or effective
glosses.sourceDescription: if someone slows down, or if something slows them down, they become less active or effective
examples: For me, holidays are a time to slow down and relax.
This cold is really slowing me down.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 찾기 위해 지역을 둘러보는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to look around an area in order to find something
glosses.sourceDescription: to look around an area in order to find something
examples: He quickly spied out the waiter.
I’m going to spy out a suitable place to meet.

glosses.meaningKo: 자동차, 비행기 등에서 안전벨트를 매기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to fasten your seat belt in a car, plane etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to fasten your seat belt in a car, plane etc
examples: Buckle up, it's going to be a bumpy ride.
Get ready, buckle up, and keep your arms and legs inside the vehicle at all times.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 결정을 신중하게 고려하기
glosses.englishDescription: to consider a problem or decision carefully
glosses.sourceDescription: to consider a problem or decision carefully
examples: I began to pace about and think over my options.
Let’s think over his proposal before we see him again.

glosses.meaningKo: 음식, 오락, 서비스 등을 특히 무료로 제공하다
glosses.englishDescription: to provide something such as food, entertainment, or a service, especially without charging for it
glosses.sourceDescription: to provide something such as food, entertainment, or a service, especially without charging for it
examples: The school laid on a bus for the class trip.
They lay on free snacks for every club meeting.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 다루거나 정리하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to deal with or organize something
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal with or organize something
examples: Can you see about getting us a lift home?
We must see about a teacher for you right away.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 매우 피곤하게 만들기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone feel very tired
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone feel very tired
examples: It was climbing that last hill that really did them in.
I’m completely done in after all that running around.

glosses.meaningKo: 공식적 합의 또는 계약의 일부가 되도록 합의하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to agree to be part of an official agreement or contract
glosses.sourceDescription: to agree to be part of an official agreement or contract
examples: Borrowers must be clear about the agreement they are entering into.
In 1986, the organization entered into an agreement with a private firm to operate the security system.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 유형의 직업이나 비즈니스에서 일하기 시작하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to start working in a particular type of job or business
glosses.sourceDescription: to start working in a particular type of job or business
examples: Alex has decided to go into nursing.
Eric went into the army right after school.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 빨리 읽기 위해서, 특히 필요한 정보를 찾기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to read something quickly, especially to find the information you need
glosses.sourceDescription: to read something quickly, especially to find the information you need
examples: But I looked through the book yesterday and found a huge number of favourite dishes in it.
I’ve just been looking through your cookery books for inspiration.

glosses.meaningKo: 하룻밤 다른 사람의 집에서 자려고
glosses.englishDescription: to sleep at someone else’s house for one night
glosses.sourceDescription: to sleep at someone else’s house for one night
examples: Let him have friends to sleep over as a reward for staying in his own room.
Mum, can Billy sleep over on Saturday?

glosses.meaningKo: 이해하기 쉽게 또는 상상하기 쉽게 하기 위해 무언가에 대해 더 자세한 내용을 추가합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to add more details about something in order to make it easier to understand or imagine
glosses.sourceDescription: to add more details about something in order to make it easier to understand or imagine
examples: After lunch we started to flesh out our campaign strategy, in his office.
Time to flesh out the few terse facts he'd told me about his home.

glosses.meaningKo: 잠깐 어디를 방문하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make a short visit somewhere
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a short visit somewhere
examples: Maybe she'd drop in on Annie Cabbot, the only decent copper among them.
My next unedifying conclusion was that in order to make this informality credible I had to drop in without warning at the Deanery.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 곳으로 가는 길에 정차하는 것은 보통 무언가를 할 수 있도록 하기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop at a place on your way to another place, usually so that you can do something
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop at a place on your way to another place, usually so that you can do something
examples: Can you call at the shop on your way home and get some milk?
This train calls at Hagley and all stations to Birmingham.

glosses.meaningKo: 갑자기 또는 예상치 못하게 일어날 수 있습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to happen suddenly or unexpectedly
glosses.sourceDescription: to happen suddenly or unexpectedly
examples: Ben had to go back to work – a problem’s cropped up.
It is only in the last few years that it has cropped up for sale in the UK.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 또는 무언가의 진행을 지연시키기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to delay the progress of someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to delay the progress of someone or something
examples: Four years ago he took a knock that could have set back many a weaker character.
The spending cuts have set the research project back several years.

glosses.meaningKo: 에너지나 결단을 보여주는 방식으로 특정 방향으로 가는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to go in a particular direction in a way that shows energy or determination
glosses.sourceDescription: to go in a particular direction in a way that shows energy or determination
examples: Startled by the noise, he had struck off through the woods.
They struck off across the desert without supplies.

glosses.meaningKo: 나중에 특정 목적으로 사용하기 위해 더 많은 양이나 공급으로부터 무언가를 보관하거나 저장하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to keep or save something from a larger amount or supply in order to use it later for a particular purpose
glosses.sourceDescription: to keep or save something from a larger amount or supply in order to use it later for a particular purpose
examples: Have you set aside some money for your child’s education?
Set aside a few hours for this task and be prepared to ask yourself some hard questions.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가를 검사하기 위해, 보통 빨리
glosses.englishDescription: to examine something, usually quickly
glosses.sourceDescription: to examine something, usually quickly
examples: An American inspection team had looked over sites in January.
He’d been looking over the leaflets he’d picked up earlier.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가가 존재한다고 생각하는 것은
glosses.englishDescription: to think that someone or something exists
glosses.sourceDescription: to think that someone or something exists
examples: I don’t believe in miracles.
I’m beginning to think you actually believe in ghosts!

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 많은 시간이나 노력이 필요한 일을 하기 위해, 편안한 장소에서 자신을 만들기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a place, especially in order to do something that will take a lot of time or effort
glosses.sourceDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a place, especially in order to do something that will take a lot of time or effort
examples: I settled down in front of the television for the evening.
She took a seat and settled down to wait.

glosses.meaningKo: 양이나 수준이 줄어들다
glosses.englishDescription: to become less
glosses.sourceDescription: to become less
examples: The noise level went down after the door closed.
Ticket prices may go down next month.

glosses.meaningKo: 매우 빠르게 성공하거나 인기 있게 되기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to become successful or popular very fast
glosses.sourceDescription: to become successful or popular very fast
examples: Her business has really taken off.
Our plan was to design and sell software for the computer industry which was beginning to really take off then.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 위해 무언가를 하도록 함으로써 누군가에게 문제나 어려움을 일으키게 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to cause problems or difficulties for someone by making them do something for you
glosses.sourceDescription: to cause problems or difficulties for someone by making them do something for you
examples: I don’t see why I should put myself out for him.
It would be lovely to stay with you, but I don’t want to put you out.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 그들과 비슷하기 때문에 집단에 의해 받아들여진다
glosses.englishDescription: to be accepted by a group of people because you are similar to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to be accepted by a group of people because you are similar to them
examples: Here Lee's lonely, he doesn't fit in; there he's ostracized.
She fitted in with her new colleagues straight away.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신의 팀의 다른 구성원을 교체하기 위해 스포츠 필드에 도착해야 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive on a sports field in order to replace another member of your team
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive on a sports field in order to replace another member of your team
examples: He came on as a substitute.
Miller came on for Thompson in the 75th minute of the game.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 비판하는 것, 특히 부당한 방법으로 비판하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to criticize someone, especially in an unfair way
glosses.sourceDescription: to criticize someone, especially in an unfair way
examples: You’re a brilliant mother. Why do you run yourself down?
You’re always running me down!

glosses.meaningKo: 사람, 장소, 주제 또는 활동으로 돌아가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to return to a person, place, subject, or activity
glosses.sourceDescription: to return to a person, place, subject, or activity
examples: I’d like to go back to what Abby was saying just a minute ago.
The computer breaks down and you go back to writing things down on pieces of paper.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 깊은 인상을 주거나 매우 흥분하게 만들기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to impress someone very much or make them very excited
glosses.sourceDescription: to impress someone very much or make them very excited
examples: But we were absolutely blown away by just how effective the combination of ingredients was.
When I heard that song for the first time it just blew me away.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신을 비난한 누군가, 또는 당신을 해친 무언가를 막으려고 노력합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to stop someone who has criticized you, or something that has harmed you
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to stop someone who has criticized you, or something that has harmed you
examples: The concert organizers have fought back against their critics.
But we are going to fight back, make our voices heard and rebut these accusations, which very often have no evidence to support them.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람에게 권력이나 통제권을 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give power or control to someone else
glosses.sourceDescription: to give power or control to someone else
examples: They formally hand power over to the new government next week.
Once the new operation is up and running, responsibility is handed over to a local team.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 체결하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to fasten something
glosses.sourceDescription: to fasten something
examples: Annie walked away, but not in a hurry, she stopped to do up the six buttons of her coat.
The dress does up at the back.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭘 다 먹기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to eat all of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to eat all of something
examples: Come on, eat up your broccoli.
You can have some more tomorrow, if you're a good boy and eat up all your dinner.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 당신이 그들을 믿지 않는다거나 그들이 말하는 것이 멍청하다고 말하는 데 사용됩니다
glosses.englishDescription: used for telling someone that you do not believe them or that what they are saying is stupid
glosses.sourceDescription: used for telling someone that you do not believe them or that what they are saying is stupid
examples: Come off it now – she was only trying to help.
Come off it, I know lots of men who do housework.

glosses.meaningKo: 듣기도 읽고 읽는 것을 이해하고 기억하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to understand and remember something that you hear or read
glosses.sourceDescription: to understand and remember something that you hear or read
examples: I’m not sure how much of his explanation she took in.
Livy was too excited and tired to take in much of what was said.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 많이 늘리기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to increase
glosses.sourceDescription: to increase
examples: The price of oil has gone up by over 50 per cent in less than a year.
We’d like to see the baby’s weight going steadily up.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가 나오면 알려지게 됩니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something comes out, it becomes known
glosses.sourceDescription: if something comes out, it becomes known
examples: He said it’ll all come out in court.
It eventually came out that she was already married.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 직업이나 직위에 대해 고려되어야 한다는 것을 공식적으로 제안하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to officially suggest that someone should be considered for a particular job or position
glosses.sourceDescription: to officially suggest that someone should be considered for a particular job or position
examples: I’ve thought about putting myself forward to chair the meeting.
Your name was put forward as a possible team leader.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 매우 피곤하게 만들기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone feel very tired
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone feel very tired
examples: She was worn out from looking after her elderly mother.
You need a holiday or you’ll wear yourself out.

glosses.meaningKo: 매우 슬프거나 어려운 상황에서 용감한 행동을 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to behave in a brave way in a very sad or difficult situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to behave in a brave way in a very sad or difficult situation
examples: Asked how he was bearing up under the mounting questions about his economic competence, he was dismissive of the sceptics.
Let’s see how he bears up under the pressure.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람이 하도록 하기 위해 일을 중단하도록 하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to stop doing something in order to let someone else do it
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop doing something in order to let someone else do it
examples: Some of their players have had fantastic careers but it's time to move over and let some youngsters come through.
They seem to expect older musicians to move over so that the younger ones can get a chance.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 짧은 기간 동안 무언가를 하거나 사용하는 것을 중단하도록 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop doing or using something, especially for a short period of time
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop doing or using something, especially for a short period of time
examples: I had to lay off the medication for a while to see if that was causing my headaches.
Just lay off complaining for a minute!

glosses.meaningKo: 차량이나 운전자가 출차하면 도로로 이동하거나 교통이 더 빠르게 움직이는 도로의 일부로 이동한다
glosses.englishDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls out, they move onto a road or onto a part of a road where the traffic is moving faster
glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls out, they move onto a road or onto a part of a road where the traffic is moving faster
examples: A plume of exhaust trailed from the Opel, probably getting ready to pull out.
She just pulled out in front of me without indicating!

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 집단이나 사람의 기술을 사용하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to use the skills of a particular group or person
glosses.sourceDescription: to use the skills of a particular group or person
examples: An independent investigator will be brought in to look at the allegations.
This is an opportunity to bring in new talent.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 꼼꼼히 확인하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to check something carefully
glosses.sourceDescription: to check something carefully
examples: Could you go over this report and correct any mistakes?
Go over the figures carefully before you commit.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들과 잘 지내다
glosses.englishDescription: to have a friendly relationship with someone
glosses.sourceDescription: same as get along
examples: My parents and I don’t get on.
She seems to get on with everybody.

glosses.meaningKo: 현금 등록부의 버튼을 눌러 금액을 기록합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to record an amount of money by pressing buttons on a cash register
glosses.sourceDescription: to record an amount of money by pressing buttons on a cash register
examples: She rang up our purchases quickly and we left.
Then she carried the photograph to the front to ring up the purchase.

glosses.meaningKo: 생각이나 주의를 무언가에 향하게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to direct your thoughts or attention to something
glosses.sourceDescription: to direct your thoughts or attention to something
examples: The party needs to look to the future and forget its past problems.
This is the moment to look to the future and take that step.

glosses.meaningKo: 누워 있거나 자고 있을 때 몸의 위치를 반대 방향을 향하도록 바꿔준다
glosses.englishDescription: to change the position of your body when you are lying or sleeping so that you face the opposite direction
glosses.sourceDescription: to change the position of your body when you are lying or sleeping so that you face the opposite direction
examples: I turned over in bed and groaned.
She turned over and went back to sleep.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 방문하기 위해 누군가가 있는 곳, 특히 그들의 집에 가기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to go to a place where someone is, especially their house, in order to visit them
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to a place where someone is, especially their house, in order to visit them
examples: I must've wanted to talk, because some friends at school got together and came round to see me.
I suggested he come round for dinner one night.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 잠을 자려고 하지 않을 때, 잠에 자려고
glosses.englishDescription: to go to sleep, especially when you do not intend to
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to sleep, especially when you do not intend to
examples: He even kept a camp bed there for the nights when he was so exhausted he would begin to nod off as he worked.
I drank it - I was feeling sleepy now, and it wouldn't do to nod off in Florence's drawing room.

glosses.meaningKo: 실수하거나 일을 잘못하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a mistake, or to do something badly
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a mistake, or to do something badly
examples: I messed up one answer on the worksheet.
Do not worry if you mess up the first try.

glosses.meaningKo: 돈이나 지식 같은 것을 충분히 가지고 있어야 할 일을 할 수 있습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to have just enough of something such as money or knowledge so that you can do what you need to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to have just enough of something such as money or knowledge so that you can do what you need to do
examples: As long as she could get by on her bank loan, she didn't see any point in giving up her independence.
My arithmetic isn’t very good, but I get by.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 포함하지 않도록
glosses.englishDescription: to not include someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to not include someone or something
examples: We decided to leave the chapter out of the book altogether.
Maybe while they're at it they could leave out the mosquitoes and the ticks as well.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신을 비판한 사람에게 맞서 비판하다
glosses.englishDescription: to criticize someone who has criticized you
glosses.sourceDescription: to criticize someone who has criticized you
examples: The coach hit back at the unfair criticism.
She hit back at the rude review with a calm reply.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가에 많은 노력, 돈, 도움을 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give a lot of effort, money, or help to someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to give a lot of effort, money, or help to someone or something
examples: How much money have you poured into Crystal Palace?
The business has been valued at about 8m prior to any new money being poured into the venture.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가에서 더 멀리 나가기 위해 뒤로 이동하기
glosses.englishDescription: to move backwards in order to get further away from something
glosses.sourceDescription: to move backwards in order to get further away from something
examples: Tell those people to back off so that the helicopter can land.
The policeman asked people to back off.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 차를 다른 곳으로 옮기는 것을 막기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to stop someone from moving their car out of a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop someone from moving their car out of a place
examples: William's car was completely blocked in.
I couldn't get out of the parking space because I was blocked in.

glosses.meaningKo: 경기나 물가 같은 게 바닥을 치면 다시 개선되기 전에 최저 수준에 도달한다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as an economy or price bottoms out, it reaches its lowest level before starting to improve again
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as an economy or price bottoms out, it reaches its lowest level before starting to improve again
examples: The deterioration of corporate earnings has yet to bottom out.
The Dow plunged 35 points and then bottomed out.

glosses.meaningKo: 빛이나 소리가 표면에서 튀어나오면, 그것에 부딪힌 다음 다시 그로부터 멀어진다
glosses.englishDescription: if light or sound bounces off a surface, it hits it and then moves away from it again
glosses.sourceDescription: if light or sound bounces off a surface, it hits it and then moves away from it again
examples: The sound bounces right off the walls.
If an object is in the path of the sound pulse, the sound bounces off the object and returns an “echo” to the sonar transducer.

glosses.meaningKo: 서비스를 제공하는 사람이나 단체에 와서 무언가를 처리하도록 요청합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to ask a person or organization that provides a service to come and deal with something
glosses.sourceDescription: to ask a person or organization that provides a service to come and deal with something
examples: A doctor was called in right away.
They called in a doctor because the child was ill.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 불쾌하거나 어려운 상황에 놓게 하는 것은 자신이 준비되지 않은 상황일 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to put someone in an unpleasant or difficult situation that they are not prepared for
glosses.sourceDescription: to put someone in an unpleasant or difficult situation that they are not prepared for
examples: I was caught out by the bad weather.
Ziri didn't want to be caught out in the woods after dark.

glosses.meaningKo: 투숙을 결정한 호텔이나 개인병원에 도착하고 접수처에서 일하는 사람에게 개인 정보를 알려주기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive at a hotel or a private hospital where you have arranged to stay and give your personal details to the person working at the reception desk
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive at a hotel or a private hospital where you have arranged to stay and give your personal details to the person working at the reception desk
examples: Tom checked into the hotel.
We checked into our hotel and then went out to do some sightseeing.

glosses.meaningKo: 땅을 파서 물건을 밖으로 나가거나 땅에서 밖으로 나가게 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to get something out of a place or out of the ground by digging
glosses.sourceDescription: to get something out of a place or out of the ground by digging
examples: We need to dig the truck out of the mud.
Tom had to dig his car out of the snow.

glosses.meaningKo: 지붕이나 벽이 떨어지면 땅으로 떨어진다
glosses.englishDescription: if a roof or wall falls in, it falls to the ground
glosses.sourceDescription: if a roof or wall falls in, it falls to the ground
examples: The roof of the house has fallen in.
The roof is going to fall in one of these days.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것의 양, 수준, 가치가 떨어지면 더 작아진다
glosses.englishDescription: if the amount, level, or value of something falls off, it gets smaller
glosses.sourceDescription: if the amount, level, or value of something falls off, it gets smaller
examples: Theater attendance usually falls off in summer.
Sales fell off in the third quarter.

glosses.meaningKo: 거래나 계획, 정리와 같은 일이 무산되면, 그것은 일어나지 않는다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as a deal, plan, or arrangement falls through, it fails to happen
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as a deal, plan, or arrangement falls through, it fails to happen
examples: Our plans fell through.
The project to build a new sports center has fallen through for lack of adequate funds.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 매우 열정적으로 느끼게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone feel very enthusiastic
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone feel very enthusiastic
examples: I'm really fired up about this.
The cheerleaders worked hard to fire up the crowd before the players took the court for the final game of the Delaware high school basketball playoffs.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가와 결합하여 좋고, 자연스러우거나, 매력적으로 보이도록
glosses.englishDescription: to seem good, natural, or attractive in combination with something
glosses.sourceDescription: to seem good, natural, or attractive in combination with something
examples: Those shoes don't go with the suit.
This tie goes with your shirt.

glosses.meaningKo: 친구들과 어울려 시간을 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend time relaxing or socializing with other people
glosses.sourceDescription: same as hang
examples: Children like to hang out with friends after school.
We hung out in the park on Saturday.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 일어나거나 반드시 이루어져야 한다는 것을 매우 단호하게 말하는 것은
glosses.englishDescription: to say very firmly that something must happen or must be done
glosses.sourceDescription: to say very firmly that something must happen or must be done
examples: I can't understand why you always insist on inviting her.
If you insist on doing it that way, I'm not going to help you.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 무언가를 하지 못하게 하거나, 무언가가 일어나지 않도록 하기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to prevent someone from doing something or prevent something from happening
glosses.sourceDescription: to prevent someone from doing something or prevent something from happening
examples: Urgent business kept me from going shopping with you.
That noise keeps me from sleeping.

glosses.meaningKo: 키보드로 입력하다
glosses.englishDescription: to enter information using a keyboard or keypad
glosses.sourceDescription: same as key
examples: Has the data been keyed in yet?
You cannot key in numbers because the NumLock LED is off.

glosses.meaningKo: 병이나 부상으로 누워 지내다
glosses.englishDescription: if an illness lays you up, it makes you stay in bed and stop your usual activities
glosses.sourceDescription: same as lay
examples: I've been laid up with flu for the last week.
Jim has been laid up with flu for three days.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 일어나게 하는 과정을 시작하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to begin a process that causes something to happen
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin a process that causes something to happen
examples: Globalisation has led to 24-hour trading.
Bad thoughts lead to bad actions.

glosses.meaningKo: 직장이나 공부가 있는 곳에서 살기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to live at the place where you work or study
glosses.sourceDescription: to live at the place where you work or study
examples: Only international students live in the new dormitory.
Three Canadian students live in this dormitory.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 사고가 날 가능성이 높기 때문에 누군가에게 주의를 당부하는 데 사용됩니다
glosses.englishDescription: used for warning someone to be careful, especially because they are likely to have an accident
glosses.sourceDescription: used for warning someone to be careful, especially because they are likely to have an accident
examples: "Look out!" someone cried.
Look out, there's a shark!

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가의 외모를 변화시키거나 개선하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to change or improve the appearance of someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to change or improve the appearance of someone or something
examples: I want to have this old coat made over.
He made over the interior of his house.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 심각하게 화나게 하거나 혼란을 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to seriously upset someone or make them confused
glosses.sourceDescription: to seriously upset someone or make them confused
examples: Boston messes with my head.
Too much cocoa can mess with your head.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 원하는 것을 얻거나 논쟁을 피하기 위해, 누군가나 무언가에 동의하는 척하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to pretend to agree with someone or something, especially in order to get what you want or avoid an argument
glosses.sourceDescription: to pretend to agree with someone or something, especially in order to get what you want or avoid an argument
examples: Ziri decided he was going to play along with Rima's lies.
You should play along with him for the time being.

glosses.meaningKo: 결정하기 전에 여러 가지 방법을 시험해 보다
glosses.englishDescription: to think about all the different possible ways of doing something before you make a decision
glosses.sourceDescription: to think about all the different possible ways of doing something before you make a decision
examples: We played around with several colors before choosing blue.
Mina played around with different layouts for the poster.

glosses.meaningKo: 다 먹을 때까지 먹거나 마시려고
glosses.englishDescription: to eat or drink something until it is finished
glosses.sourceDescription: to eat or drink something until it is finished
examples: The cake had been polished off before I got home.
"I'm afraid we've already polished off the soup."

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 사실이 아닌 것을 믿도록 속이기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to trick someone into believing something that is not true
glosses.sourceDescription: to trick someone into believing something that is not true
examples: Nobody can put anything over on the bureau chief.
You can't put anything over on Tom.

glosses.meaningKo: 많은 수 또는 양으로 도달하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive in large numbers or amounts
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive in large numbers or amounts
examples: Fog rolled in from the sea.
Dark clouds are rolling in.

glosses.meaningKo: 공식적인 직군이나 직위에 선출되도록 노력하기
glosses.englishDescription: to try to be elected to an official job or position
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to be elected to an official job or position
examples: I wanted to run for class president.
I'm running for mayor.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 어려움에 부딪히다
glosses.englishDescription: to start to have trouble/difficulty/problems etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to start to have trouble/difficulty/problems etc
examples: We ran into a small problem with the printer.
The project ran into difficulty near the end.

glosses.meaningKo: 왜 한 사람이 다른 사람을 매력적으로 찾거나 좋아하는지 이해할 수 없다는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to not understand why one person finds another person attractive or likes them
glosses.sourceDescription: to not understand why one person finds another person attractive or likes them
examples: I never understood what you saw in that boy.
You say you love him, but I can't for the life of me understand what you see in him.

glosses.meaningKo: 그들이 떠날 때 누군가와 함께 문 앞에 가서 작별 인사를 하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to go with someone to the door when they are leaving in order to say goodbye to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to go with someone to the door when they are leaving in order to say goodbye to them
examples: Can I see Tom out?
Come and see this girl out.

glosses.meaningKo: 조직에 편지나 문서를 보내기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to send a letter or document to an organization
glosses.sourceDescription: to send a letter or document to an organization
examples: He sent in his application to the office.
Have you sent in your report?

glosses.meaningKo: 공식적으로 일을 중단할 수 있을 때까지 계속 일을 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to continue doing something until you are officially allowed to stop doing it
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue doing something until you are officially allowed to stop doing it
examples: He vowed that he would serve out his five-year term as chairperson.
Sami served out his entire sentence.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 너무 많이 먹거나 마신 후 잠을 자면서 불쾌하거나 불편한 느낌을 없애기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to get rid of an unpleasant or uncomfortable feeling by sleeping, especially after eating or drinking too much
glosses.sourceDescription: to get rid of an unpleasant or uncomfortable feeling by sleeping, especially after eating or drinking too much
examples: Tom will be all right once he sleeps it off.
She slept it off.

glosses.meaningKo: 장소의 분위기나 느낌을 경험하고 즐기는 시간을 보내기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend time experiencing and enjoying the mood or feeling in a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend time experiencing and enjoying the mood or feeling in a place
examples: I was in a coffee bar soaking in the atmosphere.
I wish I could return to Paris and order a dozen oysters at an outdoor cafe while soaking in the sun.

glosses.meaningKo: 발을 세게 내려서 타는 것을 멈추게 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make a fire stop burning by putting your feet down hard on it
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a fire stop burning by putting your feet down hard on it
examples: He stamped out a fire.
Tom stamped out the fire.

glosses.meaningKo: 앞으로 나아가지 않거나, 또는 무언가, 일반적으로 위험하거나 불쾌한 것을 향해 움직이지 않기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to not move forwards, or to not move towards something, usually something dangerous or unpleasant
glosses.sourceDescription: to not move forwards, or to not move towards something, usually something dangerous or unpleasant
examples: Tom told us to stay back.
You should stay back.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 늘리기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to increase something
glosses.sourceDescription: to increase something
examples: The Indonesian government has stepped up fire prevention and enforcement of existing forest laws.
Chinese banks began to prohibit the use of digital currencies in 2013 and stepped up regulations after 2016.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려운 일이나 불쾌한 일을 계속 결심한 방식으로 계속 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to continue to work at something difficult or unpleasant in a determined way
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue to work at something difficult or unpleasant in a determined way
examples: "Stick at it!"
Stick at it, and you'll pass the exam.

glosses.meaningKo: 나중에 쓸 수 있도록 많은 것을 보관하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to keep a lot of something so that you can use it later
glosses.sourceDescription: to keep a lot of something so that you can use it later
examples: Birds and mammals store up food for the winter.
Squirrels store up food for the winter.

glosses.meaningKo: 조명이나 기계 같은 것을 켜거나 켜면 작동을 시작하게 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if you switch on something such as a light or a machine, or if it switches on, you make it start working
glosses.sourceDescription: if you switch on something such as a light or a machine, or if it switches on, you make it start working
examples: Could you switch the light on, please?
Tom switched on the lights.

glosses.meaningKo: 습관으로 무언가를 하기 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to start doing something as a habit
glosses.sourceDescription: to start doing something as a habit
examples: He's taken to gardening.
I took to reading.

glosses.meaningKo: 대화에서 발언, 질문 등을 추가하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to add a remark, question etc in a conversation
glosses.sourceDescription: to add a remark, question etc in a conversation
examples: Tom likes to throw in some French words when he's speaking English.
Holmes listened attentively to everything, throwing in a question from time to time.

glosses.meaningKo: 정리하다; 말끔히 다듬다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a place clean and organized
glosses.sourceDescription: same as tidy
examples: Tom tidied up his bedroom.
We tidied up our classroom after school.

glosses.meaningKo: 보통 사람들이 떠날 거라고 말하지 않고 어디론가 떠나세요
glosses.englishDescription: to leave somewhere, usually without telling people that you are going to leave
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave somewhere, usually without telling people that you are going to leave
examples: I was mid-sentence when the girl simply walked off.
Ziri turned around and walked off.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신에게 편지를 보낸 사람에게 답장을 보내기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to send a reply to someone who has sent you a letter
glosses.sourceDescription: to send a reply to someone who has sent you a letter
examples: Write back to me as soon as you get this letter.
I wrote to my uncle, who wrote back to me soon.

glosses.meaningKo: 날씨가 밝아지면 더 밝아진다
glosses.englishDescription: if the weather brightens up, it becomes sunnier
glosses.sourceDescription: if the weather brightens up, it becomes sunnier
examples: The sky has brightened up.
It would be nice if it brightened up tomorrow.

glosses.meaningKo: 결심하거나 열정적인 방법으로 무언가를 시작하기 시작하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to start doing something in a determined or enthusiastic way
glosses.sourceDescription: to start doing something in a determined or enthusiastic way
examples: As soon as their meeting was over, they set to work.
He took his coat off and set to work.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 즐기고 더 많은 것을 얻기 위해 열심입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to enjoy something and be keen to get more of it
glosses.sourceDescription: to enjoy something and be keen to get more of it
examples: Her fellow holidaymakers lapped up the glorious view.
The jokes were crude but the audience were lapping them up.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 제공하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to provide something
glosses.sourceDescription: to provide something
examples: Aunt Edie served up a lovely roast leg of lamb for dinner.
The teams served up some highly entertaining football this afternoon.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 펼치거나 표면이나 영역에 넓게 벌려 놓다
glosses.englishDescription: to open, extend, or separate things across a surface or area
glosses.sourceDescription: to separate things that were together and put them separately on a surface
examples: Spread out the map so we can all see it.
We spread our papers out on the table.

glosses.meaningKo: 누우기, 보통 긴장을 풀기 위해 또는 잠을 잘 때
glosses.englishDescription: to lie down, usually in order to relax or to sleep
glosses.sourceDescription: to lie down, usually in order to relax or to sleep
examples: Porter stretched out on his bunk, hands clasped behind his head.
She stretched herself out on the sofa.

glosses.meaningKo: 일어서거나 위로 올라가다
glosses.englishDescription: to stand or move upwards
glosses.sourceDescription: same as rise
examples: Everyone rose up to greet the guest.
Warm air rises up from the sunny ground.

glosses.meaningKo: 식당에서 음식을 주문하고 배달을 요청하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to order food from a restaurant and ask for it to be delivered to you
glosses.sourceDescription: to order food from a restaurant and ask for it to be delivered to you
examples: I ordered in pizza for dinner.
We were too tired to cook, so we ordered in.

glosses.meaningKo: 계속 일어나거나 하던 일을 이어 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue happening or doing something as before
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue happening or doing something as before
examples: Please go on reading while I open the window.
The music went on until the class ended.

glosses.meaningKo: 말다툼 끝에 다시 친해지기
glosses.englishDescription: to become friendly with someone again after an argument
glosses.sourceDescription: to become friendly with someone again after an argument
examples: They argue a lot, but they always kiss and make up.
Why don’t you two forget your differences and make up?

glosses.meaningKo: 일이나 책임을 맡다
glosses.englishDescription: to accept some work or responsibility
glosses.sourceDescription: to accept some work or responsibility
examples: I can take on one more task this week.
Mina took on responsibility for the class garden.

glosses.meaningKo: 취미나 일로 무언가를 정기적으로 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start doing something regularly as a habit, job, or interest
glosses.sourceDescription: to start doing something regularly as a habit, job, or interest
examples: Leo took up painting during the summer.
She wants to take up tennis after school.

glosses.meaningKo: 생각이나 기억이 떠오르다
glosses.englishDescription: if something comes to you, you think of it or remember it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something comes to you, you think of it or remember it
examples: A simple solution came to me during lunch.
The answer may come to you after a short break.

glosses.meaningKo: 사실이나 정보를 알아내다
glosses.englishDescription: to discover a fact or piece of information
glosses.sourceDescription: to discover a fact or piece of information
examples: We found out when the library opens.
Please find out which bus goes downtown.

glosses.meaningKo: 애써 하던 일을 포기하다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop doing something that you are trying hard to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop doing something that you are trying hard to do
examples: Do not give up when the puzzle feels difficult.
She nearly gave up, but one small hint helped.

glosses.meaningKo: 장비 등을 설치해 사용할 수 있게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to fix something such as equipment in the place where it will be used and make it ready to use
glosses.sourceDescription: to fix something such as equipment in the place where it will be used and make it ready to use
examples: They put in a new sink beside the window.
We plan to put in brighter lights next week.

glosses.meaningKo: 옷이나 장신구를 착용하다
glosses.englishDescription: to cover a part of your body with a piece of clothing or jewellery so that you are wearing it
glosses.sourceDescription: to cover a part of your body with a piece of clothing or jewellery so that you are wearing it
examples: Put on your blue jacket before we leave.
Leo put his warm hat on for the walk.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 무언가를 말하려면
glosses.englishDescription: to tell someone something
glosses.sourceDescription: to tell someone something
examples: He pointed out that we had two hours of free time before dinner.
`Correction, you told me not to leave the club," Whitlock was quick to point out.

glosses.meaningKo: 좋지 않은 상태가 시작되어 오래 영향을 미치다
glosses.englishDescription: if something unpleasant sets in, it starts to happen and have an effect, and is not likely to stop for a long time
glosses.sourceDescription: if something unpleasant sets in, it starts to happen and have an effect, and is not likely to stop for a long time
examples: A long spell of rainy weather set in.
By evening, the cold had set in across the town.

glosses.meaningKo: 여행이나 길을 떠나다
glosses.englishDescription: to start a journey
glosses.sourceDescription: to start a journey
examples: We set out early for the science museum.
The hikers set out after a good breakfast.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 하겠다고 말했거나 하라는 대로 하는 것을 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to do something that you have said you will do or that you have been told to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to do something that you have said you will do or that you have been told to do
examples: But of course she would take a message, and he could rely on someone from the Agence to carry out his wishes.
Only Sethos could be so bold; only he could carry out such a daring plot.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 하기 위해 행동을 취하는 것, 특히 문제를 해결하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to take action to do something, especially to solve a problem
glosses.sourceDescription: to take action to do something, especially to solve a problem
examples: The government must now deal with the problem of high unemployment.
We’ll deal with the question of poverty in a moment.

glosses.meaningKo: 사용했는지, 사용하려고 하는지, 특히 당신의 직업에서 지출할 책임이 있는 금액을 말하려면
glosses.englishDescription: to say how you have used, or how you will use, an amount of money that you are responsible for spending, especially in your job
glosses.sourceDescription: to say how you have used, or how you will use, an amount of money that you are responsible for spending, especially in your job
examples: He said: 'Every single transaction has been properly accounted for.'
This was fully and properly accounted for and audited.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가 없이 살거나 일을 성공시키기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in living or working without someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in living or working without someone or something
examples: We all must do without something, child.
Whether it may come or not, one should try and prepare one 's self to do without it.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제, 상황 또는 직업을 특정한 방식으로 다루기 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to start dealing with a problem, situation, or job in a particular way
glosses.sourceDescription: to start dealing with a problem, situation, or job in a particular way
examples: Or you don't know how to go about solving issues and asking for what you need.
The problem is no one wants to go about it directly.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람과 함께 어디론가 여행하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to travel somewhere with someone else
glosses.sourceDescription: to travel somewhere with someone else
examples: And what better reason to go along and look?
Which has me thinking that going along just to look couldn't hurt, could it?

glosses.meaningKo: 사람 또는 장소에서 이동하거나 멀리 이동하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to move or travel away from a person or place
glosses.sourceDescription: to move or travel away from a person or place
examples: I must have done something very unkind to make him go away and leave me.
I put him in his place and he went away.

glosses.meaningKo: 여행 중에 장소를 지나거나 짧은 시간 동안 그곳에 멈추기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to move past a place or stop there for a short time during a journey
glosses.sourceDescription: to move past a place or stop there for a short time during a journey
examples: Not in a cloud of dust, but creeping up until I had to slacken speed or go by.
We passed a house back from the road, and in the garden a woman stopped to watch us go by.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 것을 선택하다
glosses.englishDescription: to choose a particular thing
glosses.sourceDescription: to choose a particular thing
examples: I will go for the blue notebook.
Mina went for the simpler design.

glosses.meaningKo: 정보가 이해되어 머리에 들어오다
glosses.englishDescription: if information goes in, you understand it
glosses.sourceDescription: if information goes in, you understand it
examples: I explained the rule twice before it finally went in.
The lesson went in once the teacher used a clear example.

glosses.meaningKo: 신호나 경고음이 울리기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start making a noise as a signal or warning
glosses.sourceDescription: to start making a noise as a signal or warning
examples: My alarm went off at seven this morning.
The timer goes off when the bread is ready.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 시간에 유행하는 것을 멈추기
glosses.englishDescription: to stop being fashionable at a particular time
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop being fashionable at a particular time
examples: Classic jewellery like this will never go out of fashion.
That hairstyle went out about ten years ago.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 매우 꼼꼼히 살펴보다
glosses.englishDescription: to examine or search something very carefully
glosses.sourceDescription: to examine or search something very carefully
examples: Let us go through the checklist one more time.
Mina went through every page of her notes.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가에 손이 닿거나 접근할 수 있다
glosses.englishDescription: to manage to reach or touch something
glosses.sourceDescription: to manage to reach or touch something
examples: I cannot get at the box behind the chair.
Move the bag so we can get at the shelf.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람 또는 장소에서 벗어나기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to escape from a person or place
glosses.sourceDescription: to escape from a person or place
examples: Somewhere to get away from the darkness.
There is something to be got away from and something to be got back to.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 장소로 돌아오다
glosses.englishDescription: to return to a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to return to a place
examples: We got back home before dinner.
What time did you get back from the library?

glosses.meaningKo: 집이나 직장에 도착하다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive at home or at work
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive at home or at work
examples: I got in from school at four.
What time will you get in tonight?

glosses.meaningKo: 학교에서 공부하거나 팀 소속으로 뛰도록 선택받습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to be accepted to study at a school or chosen to play for a team etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to be accepted to study at a school or chosen to play for a team etc
examples: And they were more than six times as likely to get into Oxford or Cambridge.
Just over a fifth of pupils who applied from comprehensive schools got into Cambridge, compared with more than a third of applicants at independent schools.

glosses.meaningKo: 하루의 마지막을 일할 장소를 떠나기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to leave the place where you work at the end of the day
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave the place where you work at the end of the day
examples: We get off early on Fridays.
What time do you get off work?

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람을 떠나게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make another person leave
glosses.sourceDescription: to make another person leave
examples: Get out of my house!
Get that man out of my bedroom!

glosses.meaningKo: 당신에게 나쁜 일이 일어난 후 다시 행복하거나 잘 느끼기 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to start to feel happy or well again after something bad has happened to you
glosses.sourceDescription: to start to feel happy or well again after something bad has happened to you
examples: I'm now getting over that illness.
It can take weeks to get over an illness like that.

glosses.meaningKo: 일이나 과제를 끝내다
glosses.englishDescription: to finish dealing with some work, a subject etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to finish dealing with some work, a subject etc
examples: Mina got through all her homework before dinner.
We got through the whole list this morning.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 장소를 향해 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to move towards a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to move towards a place
examples: We made for the exit after the show.
The ducks made for the pond at once.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 특정한 방식으로 이해하다
glosses.englishDescription: to understand someone or the meaning of something in a particular way
glosses.sourceDescription: to understand someone or the meaning of something in a particular way
examples: What do you make of this unusual clue?
I do not know what to make of his short note.

glosses.meaningKo: 어렵게 보거나 듣거나 이해하다
glosses.englishDescription: to see, hear, or understand someone or something with difficulty
glosses.sourceDescription: to see, hear, or understand someone or something with difficulty
examples: I could barely make out the sign in the fog.
Can you make out what the speaker is saying?

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가의 긍정적인 효과나 성공을 줄이기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce the positive effect or success of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce the positive effect or success of something
examples: A few hooligans couldn’t take away from the team’s success.
We are using ethanol from corn, but it is not taking away from our food.

glosses.meaningKo: 주머니, 가방 등에서 무언가를 제거하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to remove something from a pocket, bag etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove something from a pocket, bag etc
examples: He reached into his coat to take out his wallet, intending to give the Father a hundred dollars for his troubles.
Henry took out his wallet.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 장악하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to take control of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to take control of something
examples: Are you calling me in to take over my old job?
I’ll take over from you for a moment.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 우연히 일어날 수 있습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to happen, especially by chance
glosses.sourceDescription: to happen, especially by chance
examples: Indeed, he doesn't say how it comes about at all.
Which came about, he says, purely by accident.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가가 특정한 방식으로 만나게 되면, 그들을 만나거나 볼 때, 당신은 그들에 대한 특정한 의견을 갖게 된다
glosses.englishDescription: if someone or something comes across in a particular way, you have a particular opinion of them when you meet them or see them
glosses.sourceDescription: if someone or something comes across in a particular way, you have a particular opinion of them when you meet them or see them
examples: But steely though she can be, she comes across in person as perfectly pleasant.
She comes across as very self-confident.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가, 특히 구하기 힘든 것을 얻기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to get something, especially something that is hard to get
glosses.sourceDescription: to get something, especially something that is hard to get
examples: Accommodation for men without money is harder to come by in this great city of ours.
At that time, teaching jobs abroad were hard to come by.

glosses.meaningKo: 느낌이 오면 갑자기 강한 영향을 미치거든요
glosses.englishDescription: if a feeling comes over you, it suddenly affects you in a strong way
glosses.sourceDescription: if a feeling comes over you, it suddenly affects you in a strong way
examples: A wave of anger came over him.
I came over all emotional when I saw him.

glosses.meaningKo: 신호나 메시지가 전달되어 오다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as a signal or a message comes through, you receive it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as a signal or a message comes through, you receive it
examples: Your message came through clearly this morning.
The call came through just before lunch.

glosses.meaningKo: 곧 일어날 것입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to be about to happen soon
glosses.sourceDescription: to be about to happen soon
examples: We’ve got a busy period coming up in a couple of weeks.
Our flight hasn’t come up yet.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 돌보다
glosses.englishDescription: to take care of someone or something and make certain that they have everything they need
glosses.sourceDescription: to take care of someone or something and make certain that they have everything they need
examples: Can you look after my cat this afternoon?
Leo looked after the class plants during the break.

glosses.meaningKo: 과거 어떤 시간이나 사건을 생각해 보는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to think about a time or event in the past
glosses.sourceDescription: to think about a time or event in the past
examples: Most people look back on their school days with fondness.
Those are the nights and days you look back on fondly.

glosses.meaningKo: 활동에 참여하지 않고 지켜보다
glosses.englishDescription: to watch an activity or event without taking part in it
glosses.sourceDescription: to watch an activity or event without taking part in it
examples: We looked on as the model train crossed the bridge.
Mina looked on while her friends arranged the display.

glosses.meaningKo: 책이나 목록, 컴퓨터에서 정보를 찾아보다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to find a particular piece of information by looking in a book or on a list, or by using a computer
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to find a particular piece of information by looking in a book or on a list, or by using a computer
examples: Look up the word in your dictionary.
She looked the train time up on the computer.

glosses.meaningKo: 맞서기를 그만두고 받아들이다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop competing or arguing and accept that you cannot win
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop competing or arguing and accept that you cannot win
examples: We asked again, and Dad finally gave in.
I gave in and let my friend choose the game.

glosses.meaningKo: 많은 사람들이 당신을 반대하기 때문에 뭔가를 요구하는 것을 멈추거나 무언가를 할 것이라고 말하는 것을 멈추십시오
glosses.englishDescription: to stop asking for something, or to stop saying that you will do something, because a lot of people oppose you
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop asking for something, or to stop saying that you will do something, because a lot of people oppose you
examples: Neither side is willing to back down.
We will not back down on the decision to strike.

glosses.meaningKo: 교통이 다시 막히거나, 막히면 차량이 긴 줄을 서서 계속 이동하길 기다리고 있다
glosses.englishDescription: if traffic backs up, or if it is backed up, the vehicles are in a long line and waiting to continue moving
glosses.sourceDescription: if traffic backs up, or if it is backed up, the vehicles are in a long line and waiting to continue moving
examples: Cars were backed up for miles.
Traffic is backing up on all out-of-town routes.

glosses.meaningKo: 사실을 따져 문제를 해결하다
glosses.englishDescription: to solve a problem by considering the facts
glosses.sourceDescription: to solve a problem by considering the facts
examples: We worked out why the door would not close.
Can you work out the answer from these clues?

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 테스트하여 그들이 어떤지 또는 그들이 적합한지 효과적인지 여부를 확인하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to test someone or something to see what they are like or whether they are suitable or effective
glosses.sourceDescription: to test someone or something to see what they are like or whether they are suitable or effective
examples: She was even ready to try out side A of the first of the commercial cassettes.
The other music Orfe was working on... That, she finally allowed the band to try out.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가와 통화가 끝난 후 전화기 수신기를 다시 베이스에 넣기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to put the telephone receiver back onto its base after you have finished talking to someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to put the telephone receiver back onto its base after you have finished talking to someone
examples: How dare he put the phone down on me!
She put the phone down and turned to me with a worried expression.

glosses.meaningKo: 예정된 일의 시간이나 날짜를 뒤로 미루다
glosses.englishDescription: to change the time or date of something so that it happens later than originally planned, especially because of a problem
glosses.sourceDescription: to change the time or date of something so that it happens later than originally planned, especially because of a problem
examples: The picnic was put off until Saturday.
We put off the meeting because the room was busy.

glosses.meaningKo: 집도 아닌 곳에서 잠깐 머무르기
glosses.englishDescription: to stay for a short time in a place that is not your home
glosses.sourceDescription: to stay for a short time in a place that is not your home
examples: Could you put me up for the night when I come to London?
We put up at a cheap hotel.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 계속하다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue doing something
examples: Keep on practicing the song each day.
The rain kept on falling through the afternoon.

glosses.meaningKo: 양이나 수가 한도를 넘지 않도록 하기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to prevent an amount or number from passing a limit
glosses.sourceDescription: to prevent an amount or number from passing a limit
examples: Always keep to the speed limit.
If people don't want to get fined for speeding, they should get to grips with keeping to the speed limit.

glosses.meaningKo: 하던 일을 계속하다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue to do something
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue to do something
examples: Keep up the good work on your project.
She kept up her daily reading during vacation.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 장소에 들어오지 못하게 돌려보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to refuse to let someone come into a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to refuse to let someone come into a place
examples: The full cafe had to turn a few customers away.
The hall had no seats left and turned us away.

glosses.meaningKo: 버튼이나 스위치로 기기를 켜다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a piece of equipment start working by pressing a button or moving a switch
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a piece of equipment start working by pressing a button or moving a switch
examples: Please turn on the lamp beside the desk.
Leo turned the small fan on after lunch.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 예고 없이 어떤 곳에 나타나다
glosses.englishDescription: to come somewhere, especially unexpectedly or without making a firm arrangement
glosses.sourceDescription: to come somewhere, especially unexpectedly or without making a firm arrangement
examples: Mina turned up early for the art class.
An old friend turned up at our picnic.

glosses.meaningKo: 권위 있는 사람에게 무언가를 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give something to a person in authority
glosses.sourceDescription: to give something to a person in authority
examples: All essays must be handed in by Tuesday.
He’s going on Friday. He’s already handed in his notice.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 눈에 보이게 나타나다
glosses.englishDescription: if something shows up, people can see it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something shows up, people can see it
examples: A pencil mark shows up clearly on white paper.
The stars showed up after the clouds moved away.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 머물 곳이 마음에 들지 않기 때문에, 당신이 머물 곳을 몰래 떠나는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to secretly leave a place where you should stay, because you are not happy there
glosses.sourceDescription: to secretly leave a place where you should stay, because you are not happy there
examples: She had grown up in a care home and run away.
She loved the acting, but was always running away.

glosses.meaningKo: 만약 물건이 다 떨어지면, 당신은 더 이상 남아 있지 않다
glosses.englishDescription: if something runs out, you do not have any more of it left
glosses.sourceDescription: if something runs out, you do not have any more of it left
examples: Luck which could continue indefinitely, or run out at any time.
Nevertheless, the money wouldn't last for ever, and then his luck would run out.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 빠르게 설명하거나 읽어 보다
glosses.englishDescription: to explain or to read something quickly
glosses.sourceDescription: to explain or to read something quickly
examples: Let us run through the steps before we begin.
The teacher ran through the schedule with us.

glosses.meaningKo: 분량이나 수량이 특정한 정도에 이르다
glosses.englishDescription: to reach a particular amount, especially a large amount
glosses.sourceDescription: to reach a particular amount, especially a large amount
examples: The final cost could run to one hundred dollars.
The series runs to ten short episodes.

glosses.meaningKo: 하던 이야기나 일을 멈추고 다음 것으로 넘어가다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop discussing or doing something and begin discussing or doing something different
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop discussing or doing something and begin discussing or doing something different
examples: Let us move on to the next question.
After the warm-up, the class moved on to a new song.

glosses.meaningKo: 살던 집이나 사업장을 완전히 떠나다
glosses.englishDescription: permanently to leave the house or flat where you live or the place where you have your business
glosses.sourceDescription: permanently to leave the house or flat where you live or the place where you have your business
examples: Our family will move out at the end of May.
The shop moved out of the old building last week.

glosses.meaningKo: 감정을 겉으로 드러내지 않고 참다
glosses.englishDescription: to not allow your feelings to show
glosses.sourceDescription: to not allow your feelings to show
examples: She tried to hold in her laughter during the game.
I could not hold my excitement in any longer.

glosses.meaningKo: 기다리기
glosses.englishDescription: to wait
glosses.sourceDescription: to wait
examples: Can you hurry up in the bathroom – I can’t hold on much longer.
We’ll hold on another minute, then we’ll have to go.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 물건이 쓰러지지 않도록 받치다
glosses.englishDescription: to support someone or something so that they do not fall down
glosses.sourceDescription: to support someone or something so that they do not fall down
examples: These four legs hold up the table.
Two strong posts held the sign up.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 일으키기 위해서, 특히 상황에 변화를 일으키기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make something happen, especially to cause changes in a situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something happen, especially to cause changes in a situation
examples: It is only a beginning for others to consider, follow and use to bring about change.
What is going to change its course and how do we bring about something better than that?

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 주제를 꺼내 이야기하기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start discussing a subject
glosses.sourceDescription: to start discussing a subject
examples: Mina brought up the class trip during lunch.
Please bring up your idea at the next meeting.

glosses.meaningKo: 종이에 무언가를 쓰기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to write something on a piece of paper
glosses.sourceDescription: to write something on a piece of paper
examples: As soon as I have an idea, I write it down.
Write down seven words that describe how you feel.

glosses.meaningKo: 빠진 단어나 숫자를 써넣다
glosses.englishDescription: to add words or numbers that are missing from something
glosses.sourceDescription: to add words or numbers that are missing from something
examples: Please write in the missing word below.
Leo wrote the correct date in at the top.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신이나 다른 사람이 숙박하도록 예약하다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange for yourself or someone else to stay at a hotel, hospital etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrange for yourself or someone else to stay at a hotel, hospital etc
examples: Dad booked us in at a quiet hotel for Friday.
The guide booked the group in at a nearby guesthouse.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일을 거쳐 결국 특정 장소나 상태에 이르다
glosses.englishDescription: to be in a particular place or state after doing something or because of doing it
glosses.sourceDescription: to be in a particular place or state after doing something or because of doing it
examples: We took a wrong turn and ended up at the park.
The extra paper ended up in the recycling box.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 직책이나 특정 기관의 구성원으로 선거 때 뽑히려고 노력합니다. 미국 영어에서는 누가 선거에 출마한다고 말합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to get chosen in an election for a particular position or as a member of a particular institution. In American English, you say that someone runs for office
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to get chosen in an election for a particular position or as a member of a particular institution. In American English, you say that someone runs for office
examples: He could stand for Prime Minister and be voted in.
She is intending to stand for parliament.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람의 일을 할 수 없는 동안 일시적으로 다른 사람의 일을 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to do someone else’s job temporarily while they are not available to do it
glosses.sourceDescription: to do someone else’s job temporarily while they are not available to do it
examples: Lorraine was ready to stand in if Helen got sick.
She really ought to be going - she'd promised to stand in for Daphne.

glosses.meaningKo: 달라서 쉽게 눈에 띄다
glosses.englishDescription: to be easy to see or notice because of being different
glosses.sourceDescription: to be easy to see or notice because of being different
examples: The yellow door stands out against the gray wall.
Her clear poster stood out in the busy hallway.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 가지를 다른 것과 비교하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to compare one thing with another
glosses.sourceDescription: to compare one thing with another
examples: They will conclude the existence of the disparity between their successful and enterprising form set against Wales 's failure and uninspiring play.
This season’s results have been disappointing set against last year’s.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가에 대해 더 많이 알아보려고 노력하거나, 그것에 대처하기 위해 더 많은 것을 하기 위해 노력합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to find out more about something, or to do something more to deal with it
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to find out more about something, or to do something more to deal with it
examples: Meanwhile, I'll follow up all the leads I can think of here.
The police are now following up some new leads.

glosses.meaningKo: 읽고 있는 말을 사람들이 들을 수 있도록 말하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to say the words that you are reading so that people can hear them
glosses.sourceDescription: to say the words that you are reading so that people can hear them
examples: The King held his child, who had grown so since their last meeting, and read out aloud the note he carried.
The two addresses Liz had just read out were identical with the ones Rachel Lieberman had already given me.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 수나 금액을 더해 합계를 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to calculate the total of several numbers or amounts
glosses.sourceDescription: to calculate the total of several numbers or amounts
examples: Add up the three numbers in the first row.
Mina added the points up after the game.

glosses.meaningKo: 아기나 어린 아이에서 나이 든 아이나 성인이 되는 것으로 변화한다
glosses.englishDescription: to change from being a baby or young child to being an older child or adult
glosses.sourceDescription: to change from being a baby or young child to being an older child or adult
examples: It wasn’t until my marriage ended that I really started to grow up.
She’s really starting to grow up now.

glosses.meaningKo: 뒤쪽으로 처지거나 물러나다
