glosses.englishDescription: to move so that you are behind someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to move so that you are behind someone or something
examples: The tired runner fell back behind the group.
Leo fell back a few steps to walk with me.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일이 누구의 책임으로 돌아가다
glosses.englishDescription: if something falls on someone, it is their responsibility to do it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something falls on someone, it is their responsibility to do it
examples: The task of choosing a date fell on Mina.
It fell on me to water the class plants.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가의 양을 줄이다
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce an amount of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce an amount of something
examples: We need to cut down on paper waste.
We cut down our screen time by an hour.

glosses.meaningKo: 말하는 사람에게 끼어들다
glosses.englishDescription: to interrupt someone who is speaking
glosses.sourceDescription: to interrupt someone who is speaking
examples: Please do not cut in while Leo is speaking.
You may cut in if an important detail is missing.

glosses.meaningKo: 통화 중 전화 연결이 끊기게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: if someone or something cuts you off when you are talking on the telephone, they make the telephone line stop working
glosses.sourceDescription: if someone or something cuts you off when you are talking on the telephone, they make the telephone line stop working
examples: Our call was cut off during the storm.
We were cut off again before the call ended.

glosses.meaningKo: 계속 뭔가를 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to continue doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue doing something
examples: Carry on. You’re doing fine.
Just carry on with what you were doing.

glosses.meaningKo: 기계나 차량이 고장 나 작동을 멈추다
glosses.englishDescription: if a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working
glosses.sourceDescription: if a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working
examples: Our old printer broke down this morning.
The school bus may break down without regular care.

glosses.meaningKo: 해가 구름 사이로 나타나다
glosses.englishDescription: if the sun breaks through the clouds, it appears from behind them
glosses.sourceDescription: if the sun breaks through the clouds, it appears from behind them
examples: The sun broke through the clouds after lunch.
Warm sunlight is breaking through the thin clouds.

glosses.meaningKo: 여럿 가운데 하나를 고르다
glosses.englishDescription: to choose one thing or person from a group
glosses.sourceDescription: to choose one thing or person from a group
examples: Pick out one book to read this weekend.
Mina picked a bright scarf out from the basket.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 들어 올려서 빼앗아가려고
glosses.englishDescription: to lift something up and take it away
glosses.sourceDescription: to lift something up and take it away
examples: I am constantly picking up the things the children leave lying around.
I’ve already asked them to pick their toys up.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 이해할 수 있거나 문제를 해결할 수 있기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to be able to understand something or to solve a problem
glosses.sourceDescription: to be able to understand something or to solve a problem
examples: Bob meanwhile was wracking his brains trying to figure out what could have happened.
Incredibly competent yet doubted from many sides, for reasons Brad couldn't quite figure out.

glosses.meaningKo: 오랜만에 만나 서로의 근황을 이야기하다
glosses.englishDescription: to talk to someone you have not seen for some time and find out what they have been doing
glosses.sourceDescription: to talk to someone you have not seen for some time and find out what they have been doing
examples: We met after class to catch up.
I called my cousin so we could catch up.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 토론이나 논쟁에 관여하기 위해, 특히 그것을 멈추게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to become involved in a discussion or argument, especially in order to make it stop
glosses.sourceDescription: to become involved in a discussion or argument, especially in order to make it stop
examples: It is time for the government to step in.
It reached a point where one of her Very Important fellow panellists decided to step in.

glosses.meaningKo: 수표를 써서 은행 계좌에서 돈을 가져가는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to take money from a bank account by writing a cheque
glosses.sourceDescription: to take money from a bank account by writing a cheque
examples: He paid with a cheque drawn on his company’s account.
She went into the branch and asked for a 4,000 cheque to be drawn on her savings account.

glosses.meaningKo: 문서나 계획서 같은 것을 준비하고 작성하기
glosses.englishDescription: to prepare and write something such as a document or plan
glosses.sourceDescription: to prepare and write something such as a document or plan
examples: Guidelines have been drawn up for dealing with emergencies.
The security regime is detailed in a set of regulations that was drawn up in 2002.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 가능성을 더는 고려하지 않다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop considering something as a possibility
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop considering something as a possibility
examples: The forecast does not rule out sunshine later.
Mina ruled out the red design after comparing both.

glosses.meaningKo: 밤이나 어둠이 다가와 점점 어두워지다
glosses.englishDescription: if night or darkness closes in, it becomes night, or it gets darker
glosses.sourceDescription: if night or darkness closes in, it becomes night, or it gets darker
examples: We headed home as darkness closed in.
Night closed in over the quiet village.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 사람, 어떤 것을 찾아내기 위해, 그들은 어떤 사람을 찾아내기 위해, 그들의 결심이 있는 방법으로 찾고 있다
glosses.englishDescription: to find someone or something by looking for them in a determined way
glosses.sourceDescription: to find someone or something by looking for them in a determined way
examples: Corbett resolved to seek out the truth.
Sometimes as he fussed around her, his eyes would suddenly seek out Laura's.

glosses.meaningKo: 눕다
glosses.englishDescription: to put your body in a flat position in order to rest
glosses.sourceDescription: same as lie
examples: I’m going to go and lie down for a while.
Lie down and relax.

glosses.meaningKo: 오래된 것을 새로운 것에 대한 지불의 일부로 주기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to give something old as part of the payment for something new
glosses.sourceDescription: to give something old as part of the payment for something new
examples: She traded in her old Ford for a new Honda.
When they left the snow behind Cazaril reluctantly permitted Ferda to trade in their excellent mules for swifter horses.

glosses.meaningKo: 지켜야 할 규칙이나 방식을 공식적으로 정하다
glosses.englishDescription: to state officially what someone must do or how they must do it
glosses.sourceDescription: to state officially what someone must do or how they must do it
examples: The club laid down simple rules for every member.
The guide lays down clear steps for the activity.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 의견 불일치, 어려운 상황을 성공적으로 처리하기 위해 필요한 일을 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to do what is necessary to deal with a problem, disagreement, or difficult situation successfully
glosses.sourceDescription: to do what is necessary to deal with a problem, disagreement, or difficult situation successfully
examples: He found the unfortunate Frampton in the lobby trying to sort out disputed items on his bill.
I've been asked a couple of times to sort out problems he's had.

glosses.meaningKo: 잠깐 기다리거나 참다
glosses.englishDescription: to wait or be patient
glosses.sourceDescription: to wait or be patient
examples: Hang on a moment while I find the map.
We hung on for five minutes until the doors opened.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 한 가지 일을 계속하거나 사용하며, 어떤 기간 동안 변경하거나 중단하지 않도록 한다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue to do or use one particular thing and not change it or stop it for any period of time
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue to do or use one particular thing and not change it or stop it for any period of time
examples: And this time he must stick to it.
Now he must stick to it.

glosses.meaningKo: 오래 머물기 때문에 편안한 곳에서 지내기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a place because you are going to stay there for a long time
glosses.sourceDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a place because you are going to stay there for a long time
examples: It took the young men half an hour to settle in, unpack, make a few telephone calls.
We found our seats and settled in for the journey.

glosses.meaningKo: 원하는 것을 하거나 그들이 당신을 위해 할 것으로 기대하는 것을 누군가에 의지해야 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to depend on someone to do what you want or expect them to do for you
glosses.sourceDescription: to depend on someone to do what you want or expect them to do for you
examples: I knew I could count on you to be on time.
The whole team was counting on me, and I let them down.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 빨리 움직이거나 더 빨리 일어나기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to move or happen faster
glosses.sourceDescription: to move or happen faster
examples: He savoured the phrase as the traffic began to speed up a little.
You see drivers speeding up when they should be slowing down.

glosses.meaningKo: 법관이 사건을 요약하면, 주어진 모든 증거의 요약을 제공합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a judge sums up a case, they give a summary of all the evidence that has been given
glosses.sourceDescription: if a judge sums up a case, they give a summary of all the evidence that has been given
examples: Summing up, Mr Justice Kay directed the jury to consider whether the accused had acted intentionally.
The judge will sum up the evidence tomorrow.

glosses.meaningKo: 결정이나 판결과 같은 것이 자신에게 불리하게 되면, 자신이 원했던 결정이나 판결을 받지 못한다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as a decision or judgment goes against you, you do not get the decision or judgment that you wanted
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as a decision or judgment goes against you, you do not get the decision or judgment that you wanted
examples: Or did it no longer matter once the vote had gone against?
The vote went against him, by some distance.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 장소를 방문하다
glosses.englishDescription: to visit a person or a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to visit a person or a place
examples: We went around to Mina's house after lunch.
Leo goes around to the library every Saturday.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람 또는 장소를 방문하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to visit a person or a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to visit a person or a place
examples: And my friend Mark has a large garden so sometimes I go round there.
We usually sit in her kitchen when I go round, so I'd never seen them before.

glosses.meaningKo: 둘 이상의 것이 함께 가면 자주 함께 존재한다
glosses.englishDescription: if two or more things go together, they frequently exist together
glosses.sourceDescription: if two or more things go together, they frequently exist together
examples: Some things inevitably go together.
There are some things that just go together.

glosses.meaningKo: 사업 같은 게 안 되면 완전히 실패해서 영업을 중단합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as a business goes under, it fails completely and stops operating
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as a business goes under, it fails completely and stops operating
examples: She lost her parents and we've struggled to keep our business from going under.
She said it was important to take responsibility for the fact that the business had gone under.

glosses.meaningKo: 필요하거나 원하는 것 없이 지내다
glosses.englishDescription: to live without something that you need or would like to have
glosses.sourceDescription: to live without something that you need or would like to have
examples: I can go without my phone for one afternoon.
We had to go without the printer for a day.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 무언가를 이해하도록 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make people understand something
glosses.sourceDescription: to make people understand something
examples: That is the message to get across.
The message is not getting across because they don't really know what the message is.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 잘 지내면 서로 좋아하고 친하게 지내요
glosses.englishDescription: if people get along, they like each other and are friendly to each other
glosses.sourceDescription: if people get along, they like each other and are friendly to each other
examples: It is the core idea that people who want different things can still get along.
You may get along as individuals but if you want different things you will be holding one another back from finding the right person.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 글로 적어 두다
glosses.englishDescription: to write something somewhere
glosses.sourceDescription: to write something somewhere
examples: Please get the main points down in your notebook.
Mina got every new word down on paper.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 모이면 만나서 뭔가 하거나 같이 시간을 보내기 위해서 만난다
glosses.englishDescription: if people get together, they meet in order to do something or to spend time together
glosses.sourceDescription: if people get together, they meet in order to do something or to spend time together
examples: He got together with some friends to plan a party for her.
He said they could earn money if they got together.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일을 결정하거나 하기 전에 어떤 상황에서 중요한 사실을 모두 고려하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to consider all the important facts in a situation before deciding or doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to consider all the important facts in a situation before deciding or doing something
examples: Think it out properly before you make a decision.
Tomorrow she must listen again to the instructions and think out more clearly all the implications.

glosses.meaningKo: 발명하거나 상상하기 위해서, 특히 변명
glosses.englishDescription: to invent or to imagine something, especially an excuse
glosses.sourceDescription: to invent or to imagine something, especially an excuse
examples: She would have to be on her guard against all the dirty tricks he might ever have heard of - or be able to think up on his own.
She’d have to think up a good reason for being late.

glosses.meaningKo: 고장 났거나 맞지 않는 물건을 가게에 반품하다
glosses.englishDescription: to take something that you have bought back to the shops because it is broken or not suitable
glosses.sourceDescription: to take something that you have bought back to the shops because it is broken or not suitable
examples: I took the shirt back because it was too large.
We need to take back this lamp and choose another.

glosses.meaningKo: 큰 구조물을 해체하다
glosses.englishDescription: to separate a large structure into pieces
glosses.sourceDescription: to separate a large structure into pieces
examples: We took down the tent after breakfast.
The helpers took the small stage down carefully.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 무언가, 특히 불쾌하거나 어려운 무언가의 끝까지 계속 할 수 있도록 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make it possible for someone to continue to the end of something, especially something unpleasant or difficult
glosses.sourceDescription: to make it possible for someone to continue to the end of something, especially something unpleasant or difficult
examples: Having come this far, she was determined to see things through.
It was a long and tough fight, which she planned meticulously and saw through to the end.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가와 함께 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to go somewhere with someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to go somewhere with someone
examples: Would you like to come along to the museum?
Mina came along with us for the afternoon walk.

glosses.meaningKo: 상황이나 관계를 떠나 더 이상 관계 속에 관여하지 않기를 원한다
glosses.englishDescription: to wish to leave a situation or relationship and no longer be involved in it
glosses.sourceDescription: to wish to leave a situation or relationship and no longer be involved in it
examples: She wanted out of the jail cell so badly she started to scream.
Stephanie is fed up with her husband. She just wants out of the marriage.

glosses.meaningKo: 열, 빛 또는 냄새와 같은 것을 생산하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to produce something such as heat, light, or a smell
glosses.sourceDescription: to produce something such as heat, light, or a smell
examples: They give off a very white light, and sound as if they're liable to explode any minute.
`Some of the others had real torches, so they never noticed that his one didn't give off any light.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 사람에게 무언가를 나누어 주다
glosses.englishDescription: to give something to several people
glosses.sourceDescription: to give something to several people
examples: The teacher gave out a worksheet to each student.
Volunteers gave the maps out near the entrance.

glosses.meaningKo: 변화나 차이가 줄어들어 고르게 되다
glosses.englishDescription: if things even out, or if you even them out, they show fewer or smaller changes or differences
glosses.sourceDescription: if things even out, or if you even them out, they show fewer or smaller changes or differences
examples: The workload should even out by next week.
These changes will even out the daily schedule.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 동의한 행동을 하지 않기로 결정하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to decide not to do something you agreed to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to decide not to do something you agreed to do
examples: I promised to help and I’m not backing out now.
We’re hoping that no one will back out of the deal.

glosses.meaningKo: 기분이나 체중과 같은 것을 발산하면 신체 활동을 많이 하는 일을 함으로써 그것을 제거한다
glosses.englishDescription: if you work off something such as a feeling or some of your weight, you get rid of it by doing something that involves a lot of physical activity
glosses.sourceDescription: if you work off something such as a feeling or some of your weight, you get rid of it by doing something that involves a lot of physical activity
examples: I knew I wouldn't get to sleep if I didn't work off some of my excess energy.
I needed to work off some of that Mediterranean Stew before I got in the pool.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신을 속상하게 하거나 흥분시키거나 긴장하게 만들기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make yourself feel upset, excited, or nervous
glosses.sourceDescription: to make yourself feel upset, excited, or nervous
examples: I just can’t work up any enthusiasm for this trip.
`I must say I can't work up any great enthusiasm for the cause," I said.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가의 주의를 끌려고 큰 소리로 부르다
glosses.englishDescription: to shout something, especially when you are trying to get someone’s attention
glosses.sourceDescription: to shout something, especially when you are trying to get someone’s attention
examples: Mina called out my name from across the playground.
He called out to ask us to wait.

glosses.meaningKo: 전화하기
glosses.englishDescription: to telephone someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to telephone someone
examples: I called him up and told him.
When I call up and ask for information, people get weird with me,' he said.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 당신이 정말 어떤 사람인지 볼 수 있도록 당신의 아이디어를 명확하고 효과적으로 표현합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to express your ideas clearly and effectively so that people can see what you are really like
glosses.sourceDescription: to express your ideas clearly and effectively so that people can see what you are really like
examples: He just wanted to put across his opinion.
Today you can be your true self and put across your ideas well, instead of compromising to please other people.

glosses.meaningKo: 돈을 절약해서 미래에 뭔가를 사거나 지불할 수 있도록
glosses.englishDescription: to save an amount of money so that you can buy or pay for something in the future
glosses.sourceDescription: to save an amount of money so that you can buy or pay for something in the future
examples: And how much money should he put aside each month?
How much money should he put aside?

glosses.meaningKo: 돈을 절약하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to save an amount of money
glosses.sourceDescription: to save an amount of money
examples: Loyal savers who have been putting away money towards their retirement have been suffering from a barrage of hidden fees and dire returns for many years.
Savers who have diligently put away money all their lives are unlikely to spend it in one go.

glosses.meaningKo: 옮기기 전에 있던 자리에 무언가를 넣기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to put something in the place where it was before it was moved
glosses.sourceDescription: to put something in the place where it was before it was moved
examples: He was rushed to hospital in the German capital where his shoulder was put back in place.
The shoulder blade was put back into place in hospital, but the longer-term damage is difficult to assess.

glosses.meaningKo: 돈을 따로 모아 두다
glosses.englishDescription: to save money for future use
glosses.sourceDescription: same as put aside
examples: She had put by the money for them secretly, buying less food for the week and doing without when Nick was out of the house.
`I suppose I've got enough money put by to last him some time: after all, I'd heard his wife's decision to leave him.

glosses.meaningKo: 아이디어, 의견, 계획 등을 진술하거나 제안하기 위한 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to state or offer an idea, opinion, plan etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to state or offer an idea, opinion, plan etc
examples: The government has put forth a modest plan to streamline the whole system.
We had to think of the publicity there would be if this new theory was put forth, and it was by no means conclusive.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 일이 없을 때 여유 있게 시간을 보내는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to spend time in a relaxed way when you have nothing else to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend time in a relaxed way when you have nothing else to do
examples: The purpose of life is to while away the intervening time as pleasantly as possible.
This sort of thing may be all very good in its way: one has to while away the time somehow.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 제어하고 크기가 증가하거나 숫자가 증가하는 것을 방지하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to control something and prevent it from increasing in size or number
glosses.sourceDescription: to control something and prevent it from increasing in size or number
examples: Like so many paper mills, the economics of scale keep increasing so as to keep down production costs.
We have to try and keep costs down.

glosses.meaningKo: 기대한 일을 하지 않아 누군가를 실망시키다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone disappointed by not doing something that they are expecting you to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone disappointed by not doing something that they are expecting you to do
examples: I promised not to let my partner down.
The team worked hard because it did not want to let us down.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 집이나 방 등에 들어오게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to allow someone to enter a house, room etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to allow someone to enter a house, room etc
examples: Please let the cat in before dinner.
Mina let us in when we reached the classroom.

glosses.meaningKo: 비밀을 알려 주다
glosses.englishDescription: to allow someone to know a secret
glosses.sourceDescription: same as let
examples: It is as if you had been let into a secret.
Then he was let into the secret.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 해야 할 것으로 기대했던 일을 하지 않도록 하기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to allow someone not to do something that they were expecting to have to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to allow someone not to do something that they were expecting to have to do
examples: I was pulled over for speeding, but I was let off with a warning.
When we were in port, he let me off work and allowed me to go ashore.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 인정하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to admit something
glosses.sourceDescription: to admit something
examples: He knows more than he lets on.
`You've more courage than you like to let on about," Robina said.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람 또는 동물이 장소를 떠날 수 있도록 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to allow a person or animal to leave a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to allow a person or animal to leave a place
examples: Would you let the dog out, please?
`Do you realise, Comrade Didenko, the nature of the animal you propose to let out of its cage?

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 돕기 위해, 특히 특정 일을 하거나 돈을 주는 것으로,
glosses.englishDescription: to help someone, especially by doing a particular job or by giving them money
glosses.sourceDescription: to help someone, especially by doing a particular job or by giving them money
examples: He always helped out with the housework.
My family has always helped me out.

glosses.meaningKo: 계획이나 상황을 구체적으로 논의하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to discuss a plan or a situation in a detailed way
glosses.sourceDescription: to discuss a plan or a situation in a detailed way
examples: Here problems are talked through and a consensus emerges.
We discuss how the team is working and talk through any problems that they may have.

glosses.meaningKo: 분노나 반대를 누군가에게 돌리거나, 지지를 멈추고 반대하기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to direct anger or opposition toward someone, or to stop supporting them and begin opposing them
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop liking or supporting someone or something and to start opposing them
examples: Some of the people 's anger is turned against themselves.
The rival factions turned against each other in a bitter struggle for power.

glosses.meaningKo: 제안이나 요청을 거절하다
glosses.englishDescription: to not accept an offer or request
glosses.sourceDescription: to not accept an offer or request
examples: Mina turned down the offer to lead the group.
I had to turn down the invitation this time.

glosses.meaningKo: 이동을 시작하거나 여행을 시작하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to begin moving, or to begin a journey
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin moving, or to begin a journey
examples: He started off for the station at a brisk pace.
She started off well, but slowed down halfway through the race.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 시작해 작업하거나 처리하다
glosses.englishDescription: to begin working on something or dealing with something
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin working on something or dealing with something
examples: Let us start on the first part of the project.
She started on her homework after a short break.

glosses.meaningKo: 하나의 것으로 시작하여 다른 것으로 발전하기
glosses.englishDescription: to begin as one thing and develop into something else
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin as one thing and develop into something else
examples: He started out as a salesperson before turning to poetry.
Some businesses start out as hobbies.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 이상 쓰지 않는 옷이나 장난감을 어린아이에게 물려주다
glosses.englishDescription: to give clothes, toys etc to a younger child when an older child no longer needs them
glosses.sourceDescription: to give clothes, toys etc to a younger child when an older child no longer needs them
examples: We hand down our storybooks to younger cousins.
The jacket was handed down to her little sister.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 사물을 눈에 띄거나 돋보이게 드러내다
glosses.englishDescription: to display someone or something so that they are noticed or admired, or to make their attractive qualities easy to see
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something look very impressive or attractive
examples: She couldn't wait to start walking around in full hedgehog gear so she could show off the whole outfit.
The trousers were very tight-fitting, showing off her slim figure.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 사건이나 상황이 특정한 방식으로 전개되면 그런 방식으로 일어난다
glosses.englishDescription: if an event or situation is played out in a particular way, it happens in that way
glosses.sourceDescription: if an event or situation is played out in a particular way, it happens in that way
examples: She had come this far, she decided, so she might as well play out the drama to the end.
She was moving at her old, leisurely pace, as though they had all the time in the world to play out the last reel of this tragedy.

glosses.meaningKo: 아이들이 장난스럽게 말썽을 부리다
glosses.englishDescription: if children play up or play someone up, they behave badly in a way that they think is funny
glosses.sourceDescription: if children play up or play someone up, they behave badly in a way that they think is funny
examples: The children played up during the long wait.
The class sometimes plays up before lunch.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 쫓기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to chase someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to chase someone or something
examples: She should spend more time studying and less time running after boys.
She's usually seen running after boys in Hollyoaks.

glosses.meaningKo: 액체가 표면이나 용기에서 흘러나가다
glosses.englishDescription: if a liquid runs off, or if you run it off, it flows away from or out of something
glosses.sourceDescription: if a liquid runs off, or if you run it off, it flows away from or out of something
examples: Rainwater runs off the roof into a barrel.
Rainwater can run off the leaves after a shower.

glosses.meaningKo: 이해할 수 있도록 다시 설명하다
glosses.englishDescription: to explain something again so that someone understands
glosses.sourceDescription: to explain something again so that someone understands
examples: Let us run over the instructions once more.
The teacher ran over the last step with Mina.

glosses.meaningKo: 일부러 무언가를 미루기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to deliberately delay doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to deliberately delay doing something
examples: How much longer can they hold off on political reform?
They can hold off the vote until the election.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람이 받을 수 있도록 무언가를 내밀다
glosses.englishDescription: to hold something where someone else can reach it
glosses.sourceDescription: to hold something where someone else can reach it
examples: Mina held out the map for me to take.
Please hold the basket out so Leo can reach it.

glosses.meaningKo: 일을 나중 시간이나 날짜로 미루다
glosses.englishDescription: to do something or deal with something at a later time or date
glosses.sourceDescription: to do something or deal with something at a later time or date
examples: We held the final discussion over until Monday.
The last question was held over for the next class.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려운 상황에서 함께 있으면서 좋은 관계를 계속 이어나가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to stay together and continue to have a good relationship in a difficult situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to stay together and continue to have a good relationship in a difficult situation
examples: I was trying to hold my marriage together.
We had acted as if we could still be a couple and as if we could still hold together a family.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가가 움직이거나 땅으로 떨어지게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone or something move or fall to the ground
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone or something move or fall to the ground
examples: Chavasse raised his right arm to bring down the edge of his hand.
Johnson was brought down by an aggressive tackle just a few feet from the goal.

glosses.meaningKo: 이벤트의 날짜나 시간을 변경하여 더 일찍 이루어지도록 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to change the date or time of an event so that it happens earlier
glosses.sourceDescription: to change the date or time of an event so that it happens earlier
examples: She left a message with her father's secretary on the off chance that he could bring forward his flight home and come along, too.
The match has been brought forward to 1.00 pm.

glosses.meaningKo: 글이나 발언의 강도나 세부 내용을 약하게 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something such as a statement or newspaper article less offensive, powerful, or detailed
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something such as a statement or newspaper article less offensive, powerful, or detailed
examples: The editor watered down the strongest sentence.
Do not water down the main point of your report.

glosses.meaningKo: 성공하지 못할 것이라 단정하고 더는 관심을 두지 않다
glosses.englishDescription: to decide that someone or something will not succeed and so to stop giving them your attention and energy
glosses.sourceDescription: to decide that someone or something will not succeed and so to stop giving them your attention and energy
examples: Do not write off the small team before the match.
She refused to write the new idea off too soon.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것을 다시 쓰기 위해, 보통 더 완전한 형태로
glosses.englishDescription: to write something again, usually in a more complete form
glosses.sourceDescription: to write something again, usually in a more complete form
examples: Could you write out exactly what you need me to do?
`If I did my duty, I'd make you write out your own version of every story you've read this morning, but I'm too soft-hearted.

glosses.meaningKo: 앞서 작성한 노트를 이용하여 보고서, 기사 등을 작성하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to write a report, article etc using notes that you wrote earlier
glosses.sourceDescription: to write a report, article etc using notes that you wrote earlier
examples: Give her a chance to write up her project on her own first, if that's what she wants.
She fully intended to write up a report for the file on Jennifer Spencer.

glosses.meaningKo: 긴장을 풀고 무언가를 하려는 노력을 멈추는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to relax and stop making the effort to do something
glosses.sourceDescription: to relax and stop making the effort to do something
examples: So perhaps we ought just to sit back and enjoy it.
You should just sit back and enjoy it.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 활동에 잠시 참여하지 않다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop doing something for a period of time
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop doing something for a period of time
examples: I will sit out the next round and rest.
Mina sat the final practice out this morning.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 것과 관련하여 어떤 것을 올바른 위치로 이동시키고, 특히 그것에 대해 수준이 되도록 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to move something into the correct position in relation to something else, especially so that it is level with it
glosses.sourceDescription: to move something into the correct position in relation to something else, especially so that it is level with it
examples: Broker tried to line up Sommer's green parka with the end of the point that appeared, then disappeared, playing peek-a-boo.
He lined the ball up and kicked it straight into the net.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람이 얻는 이익이나 기회를 얻지 못하다
glosses.englishDescription: to not get a benefit that someone else is getting
glosses.sourceDescription: to not get a benefit that someone else is getting
examples: Hurry, or you may lose out on a place in the team.
She lost out because she sent the form too late.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 당신이 그들로부터 빌린 것과 같은 돈을 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give someone the same amount of money that you borrowed from them
glosses.sourceDescription: to give someone the same amount of money that you borrowed from them
examples: Borrowers can also pay back the equity loan early to increase their share in the property.
We borrowed from the bank to improve the property, with the intention of remortgaging to pay back the loan.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 일이 좋은 결과나 이익을 가져오다
glosses.englishDescription: if something that you do pays off, it brings you some benefit
glosses.sourceDescription: if something that you do pays off, it brings you some benefit
examples: Your daily practice will pay off soon.
The extra planning paid off on the day of the event.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 많은 돈을 지출하다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend or pay money, especially a lot of money
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend or pay money, especially a lot of money
examples: The club paid out fifty dollars for new art supplies.
We paid out more than expected for the repairs.

glosses.meaningKo: 빚을 진 돈을 지불하기 위해서, 특히 지불하기를 원하지 않을 때
glosses.englishDescription: to pay money that you owe, especially when you are unwilling to pay
glosses.sourceDescription: to pay money that you owe, especially when you are unwilling to pay
examples: If she didn't think she'd done something wicked, she wouldn't pay up.
We’re waiting for the insurance company to pay up.

glosses.meaningKo: 조심하라고
glosses.englishDescription: to be careful
glosses.sourceDescription: to be careful
examples: You could have a nasty accident if you don’t watch out.
You're gonna get yourself in trouble, girl, if you don't watch out.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 곳으로 가기 전에 어딘가를 방문하기
glosses.englishDescription: to visit somewhere before continuing to another place
glosses.sourceDescription: to visit somewhere before continuing to another place
examples: I'd been working and I was wide awake, so rather than go home and bounce off the walls I thought I'd stop off for a coffee.
We stopped off in town on the way to Jenni’s house.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것에 대해 확고한 공개적으로 의견을 진술하기 위해서, 특히 어떤 것에 대해 항의하거나 방어하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to state your opinion firmly and publicly about something, especially in order to protest against or defend something
glosses.sourceDescription: to state your opinion firmly and publicly about something, especially in order to protest against or defend something
examples: Somebody in the crowd began to speak out at this, but was hushed as the Jaff looked in their direction.
This time I will speak out in a voice so loud it fills the skies like thunder and my words fall like rain.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 크게 이야기하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to talk louder
glosses.sourceDescription: to talk louder
examples: You have to speak up. The people in the back can’t hear you.
`It's somewhat better, but I'll still need you to speak up for me to hear you clearly.

glosses.meaningKo: 말이나 행동에서 실제로 없거나 분명하지 않은 의미를 지나치게 찾아내다
glosses.englishDescription: to find an extra meaning in someone’s words or actions that is not obvious or does not exist
glosses.sourceDescription: to find an extra meaning in someone’s words or actions that is not obvious or does not exist
examples: You should not read too much into that small pause.
Leah read a hidden promise into the friendly message.

glosses.meaningKo: 성장하거나 발전하여 특정한 사람이나 것이 되다
glosses.englishDescription: to develop and become a particular thing or person
glosses.sourceDescription: to develop and become a particular thing or person
examples: The small club grew into a busy community group.
With practice, Mina grew into a confident speaker.

glosses.meaningKo: 처음보다 점점 더 좋아지다
glosses.englishDescription: if something or someone grows on you, you start to like them more
glosses.sourceDescription: if something or someone grows on you, you start to like them more
examples: The new song grew on me after a few listens.
That unusual color is starting to grow on Leo.

glosses.meaningKo: 걷다가 실수로 몸의 일부를 무언가에 부딪히다
glosses.englishDescription: to accidentally hit a part of your body against something when you are walking
glosses.sourceDescription: to accidentally hit a part of your body against something when you are walking
examples: I walked into the low shelf while looking away.
Ben nearly walked into the open cupboard door.

glosses.meaningKo: 큰 어려움 끝에 성공하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed after great difficulty
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed after great difficulty
examples: If she did not arrive soon, hunger was likely to win out over curiosity.
It was a struggle, but truth won out in the end.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 당신과 동의하도록 설득하거나 당신에게 친절하도록 설득하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to persuade someone to agree with you or to be friendly to you
glosses.sourceDescription: to persuade someone to agree with you or to be friendly to you
examples: Cole, though, is convinced he can still win over his many doubters.
We’ve finally won him over to our point of view.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 비즈니스의 일부를 구매하기 위해, 특히 비즈니스를 통제하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to buy part of a business, especially in order to get control of it
glosses.sourceDescription: to buy part of a business, especially in order to get control of it
examples: Buying into a company under new management can often backfire.
Moves to buy into other companies have failed.

glosses.meaningKo: 이전에 함께 소유했던 모든 사업을 통제할 수 있도록 비즈니스 파트너에게 돈을 지불하는 것입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to pay money to your business partner so that you can control all of a business you previously owned together
glosses.sourceDescription: to pay money to your business partner so that you can control all of a business you previously owned together
examples: The other directors have offered to buy me out.
Would you be interested at all in letting me buy out your share of the business?

glosses.meaningKo: 많은 양의 물건 또는 사용할 수 있는 모든 것을 구입하기
glosses.englishDescription: to buy large amounts of something or all of it that is available
glosses.sourceDescription: to buy large amounts of something or all of it that is available
examples: For even if he managed to buy up all the shares on the open market, it would still amount to a stand-off.
Or perhaps buy up the outstanding outside holdings to prevent any attempt at a stand-off.

glosses.meaningKo: 식당에서 손님에게 음식을 내고 시중들다
glosses.englishDescription: to serve people in a restaurant
glosses.sourceDescription: to serve people in a restaurant
examples: Nora waits on customers at the family cafe.
One server waited on our table during lunch.

glosses.meaningKo: 말투나 행동을 흉내 내어 우스꽝스럽게 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone seem silly by pretending to speak or behave like them
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone seem silly by pretending to speak or behave like them
examples: The school play sent up old cooking shows.
That cartoon gently sends up famous fairy tales.

glosses.meaningKo: 일정 시간 동안 집 밖에 머물다
glosses.englishDescription: to remain out of your home for a period of time
glosses.sourceDescription: to remain out of your home for a period of time
examples: We stayed out until sunset during the neighborhood fair.
Mia may stay out a little later on Saturday.

glosses.meaningKo: 조직, 합의, 관계와 같은 것이 무너지면 더 이상 계속되지 않는다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as an organization, agreement, or relationship falls apart, it no longer continues
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as an organization, agreement, or relationship falls apart, it no longer continues
examples: I guess it was like that for you when your company started to fall apart.
The NATO alliance was in danger of falling apart.

glosses.meaningKo: 무엇이 떨어져 나가면 고정되어 있던 것에서 떨어져 나가게 된다
glosses.englishDescription: if something falls away, it breaks off from the thing it was fixed to
glosses.sourceDescription: if something falls away, it breaks off from the thing it was fixed to
examples: Plaster was falling away from the walls.
She beat on the rock floor with her fist and felt a chunk crumble off and fall away below.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 해야 할 시간에 무언가를 하지 못하거나 무언가를 지불하지 못하게 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to fail to do something or pay something at the time that you should
glosses.sourceDescription: to fail to do something or pay something at the time that you should
examples: And she won't fall behind, because if she does, she'll be taught how to keep up!
My daughter is falling behind with her school work.

glosses.meaningKo: 입고 있는 것이 다리 아래로 흘러내리다
glosses.englishDescription: if something you are wearing is falling down, it is slipping down your legs
glosses.sourceDescription: if something you are wearing is falling down, it is slipping down your legs
examples: These loose socks keep falling down around my ankles.
His oversized trousers started to fall down.

glosses.meaningKo: 속임수나 농담이 진실이라고 믿는 것은
glosses.englishDescription: to believe that a trick or a joke is true
glosses.sourceDescription: to believe that a trick or a joke is true
examples: Fortunately I am old enough and wise enough not to fall for that trick.
How could you fall for such an obvious trick?

glosses.meaningKo: 물건이 옆으로 넘어지다
glosses.englishDescription: if something falls over, it falls so that its side is on the ground
glosses.sourceDescription: if something falls over, it falls so that its side is on the ground
examples: The tall stack of blocks fell over on the rug.
That empty chair may fall over if you bump the table.

glosses.meaningKo: 곁을 지나가다
glosses.englishDescription: to go past
glosses.sourceDescription: to go past
examples: We passed by the bakery on our walk.
A bright bus passed by the school gate.

glosses.meaningKo: 행사가 특정한 방식으로 진행되다
glosses.englishDescription: if an event passes off in a particular way, it happens in that way
glosses.sourceDescription: if an event passes off in a particular way, it happens in that way
examples: The picnic passed off without any problems.
Our class show passed off better than we expected.

glosses.meaningKo: 예를 들어, 당신이 너무 더워서 갑자기 의식이 없게 되는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly become unconscious, for example because you are too hot
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly become unconscious, for example because you are too hot
examples: I swear to God my heart was beating so hard, I thought I was going to pass out.
People everywhere were passing out from the heat.

glosses.meaningKo: 기회를 이용하지 않기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to not take advantage of an opportunity
glosses.sourceDescription: to not take advantage of an opportunity
examples: I can’t believe you passed up the chance to do a parachute jump.
Possibly the fact that they both knew she was too good for Cyberdyne to pass up.

glosses.meaningKo: 상점이 물건을 팔면, 더 이상 구할 수 없도록 가지고 있는 모든 것을 판매합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a shop sells out of something, it sells all that it has so that there is no more available
glosses.sourceDescription: if a shop sells out of something, it sells all that it has so that there is no more available
examples: I went to get some bread, but the shop had sold out.
The tickets had sold out within a few short hours.

glosses.meaningKo: 불이 켜지면 빛을 내기 시작합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a light lights up, it starts to shine
glosses.sourceDescription: if a light lights up, it starts to shine
examples: Fireworks were lighting up the night sky.
In the blacked-out city far below a few fires set in trash cans now light up small patches of street.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 금액의 돈을 벌다
glosses.englishDescription: to earn a particular amount of money
glosses.sourceDescription: to earn a particular amount of money
examples: The small shop pulls down a steady income each month.
Her craft stall pulled down enough to buy new tools.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 옷을 빨리 벗으려면
glosses.englishDescription: to take off clothes, especially quickly
glosses.sourceDescription: to take off clothes, especially quickly
examples: He grunted, slung his helmet from a strap on the saddle, and began to pull off his gauntlets.
She pulled the dress off over her head.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 힘을 합치면 힘을 합쳐 뭔가를 성취한다
glosses.englishDescription: if people pull together, they work together to achieve something
glosses.sourceDescription: if people pull together, they work together to achieve something
examples: But if we pull together, work together, we will get through this together.
Let's pull together, work together.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량이나 운전자가 멈춰 서다
glosses.englishDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls up, they stop
glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls up, they stop
examples: The bus pulled up beside the school gate.
A taxi pulled up just as the rain began.

glosses.meaningKo: 대수롭지 않은 일처럼 설명해 넘기다
glosses.englishDescription: to tell someone about something in a way that makes them think it is unimportant, so that they do not ask questions about it
glosses.sourceDescription: to tell someone about something in a way that makes them think it is unimportant, so that they do not ask questions about it
examples: He tried to explain away the missing homework page.
You cannot explain the odd result away so easily.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려운 일을 성공적으로 처리하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to deal successfully with something difficult
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal successfully with something difficult
examples: Both actors have the stylish self-confidence needed to carry off these roles.
Luckily, that was enough to allow them to behave sufficiently intimately to carry off their charade.

glosses.meaningKo: 1년 또는 기간 동안 벌거나 받은 것을 다음 1년 동안 가져가기
glosses.englishDescription: to take something that you earn or are given in one year or period of time into the next one
glosses.sourceDescription: to take something that you earn or are given in one year or period of time into the next one
examples: If you haven't used this annual exemption during the previous tax year, it can be carried over into the next tax year.
You are not allowed to carry over holiday entitlement from one year into the next.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려움이 있어도 계획을 끝까지 실행하다
glosses.englishDescription: to complete something that was planned, often despite difficulties or opposition
glosses.sourceDescription: to complete something that was planned, often despite difficulties or opposition
examples: The team carried the recycling plan through.
We carried through our idea for a class garden.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량을 타고 출발해 떠나다
glosses.englishDescription: if a vehicle or driver drives off, the vehicle starts moving and leaves
glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver drives off, the vehicle starts moving and leaves
examples: The van drove off after the boxes were loaded.
We waved as the little bus drove off.

glosses.meaningKo: 갑자기 어떤 행동을 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to start doing something
examples: The audience broke into applause at the end.
Our group broke into song during the walk.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것의 일부가 끊어지면, 그것은 주된 부분과 분리된다
glosses.englishDescription: if a part of something breaks off, it becomes separated from the main part
glosses.sourceDescription: if a part of something breaks off, it becomes separated from the main part
examples: Each child broke off a piece of bread.
Part of the chimney broke off and fell to the ground.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 계속 부당하게 대하거나 흠잡다
glosses.englishDescription: to keep treating someone badly or unfairly, especially by criticizing them
glosses.sourceDescription: to keep treating someone badly or unfairly, especially by criticizing them
examples: Some classmates picked on Leo for his unusual backpack.
It is unfair to pick on someone for a small mistake.

glosses.meaningKo: 느낌이 서서히 사라지다
glosses.englishDescription: if a feeling wears off, it gradually disappears
glosses.sourceDescription: if a feeling wears off, it gradually disappears
examples: The excitement will wear off after a while.
Her nervousness began to wear off during rehearsal.

glosses.meaningKo: 갑자기 아이디어를 떠올리다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly have an idea
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly have an idea
examples: Mina hit on a clever way to sort the cards.
We finally hit on the perfect name for our team.

glosses.meaningKo: 직장에 전화해 메시지를 전하다
glosses.englishDescription: to telephone the place where you work in order to give a message
glosses.sourceDescription: to telephone the place where you work in order to give a message
examples: Leo phoned in a message before his work shift.
The manager phoned in to say she would arrive late.

glosses.meaningKo: 아는 것을 말하지 않거나 다른 사람이 아는 것을 말하지 못하게 함으로써 무언가에 대한 진실을 숨기기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to hide the truth about something by not telling what you know or by preventing other people from telling what they know
glosses.sourceDescription: to hide the truth about something by not telling what you know or by preventing other people from telling what they know
examples: He got his powerful friends to cover up for him.
It was a real scandal, but the school tried to cover the whole thing up.

glosses.meaningKo: 장소를 깔끔하게 만들기 위해 사용 완료했거나 더 이상 원하지 않는 것을 제거합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove something that you have finished using or no longer want in order to make a place tidy
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove something that you have finished using or no longer want in order to make a place tidy
examples: A young woman cleared away their empty cups.
You sit down – I’ll clear away.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 미스터리를 해결하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to solve a problem or a mystery
glosses.sourceDescription: to solve a problem or a mystery
examples: You can clear up misunderstandings, soothe emotions and ensure jealousy plays no part in family relationships.
Your skill in clearing up the misunderstandings that shadow a family relationship are important.

glosses.meaningKo: 이해하다
glosses.englishDescription: to understand
glosses.sourceDescription: to understand
examples: Sam caught on after the second example.
You will catch on quickly with a little practice.

glosses.meaningKo: 직위에서 물러나다
glosses.englishDescription: to leave an important job or position
glosses.sourceDescription: same as step
examples: And if that is the case, I'd rather step down than jeopardize this operation.
The chairman was forced to step down due to ill health.

glosses.meaningKo: 잠시 자리를 비우다
glosses.englishDescription: to leave a place for a short time
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave a place for a short time
examples: The teacher stepped out for a minute.
I need to step out and return this library book.

glosses.meaningKo: 공기와 같은 것을 몸에 넣기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to take something such as air into your body
glosses.sourceDescription: to take something such as air into your body
examples: She paused to draw in a slow breath.
Noah opened the window and drew in the cool morning air.

glosses.meaningKo: 편안하고 자신 있게 느끼게 하여 말을 더 하도록 이끌다
glosses.englishDescription: to encourage someone to talk more by making them feel more relaxed and confident
glosses.sourceDescription: to encourage someone to talk more by making them feel more relaxed and confident
examples: The friendly host drew the shy guest out.
A simple question helped draw Mina out.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 말하는 것을 몰래 듣기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to secretly listen to what someone says
glosses.sourceDescription: to secretly listen to what someone says
examples: Carter nodded and indicated to turn the volume up on the speaker so they could listen in.
Rachel was listening in on our conversation.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일이 일어나고 있거나 누군가 어떤 일을 하고 있는지에 의존해야 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to depend on something happening or on someone doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to depend on something happening or on someone doing something
examples: They are banking on the future being good.
They’re banking on him to save the match.

glosses.meaningKo: 옷 한 벌을 재빨리 벗다
glosses.englishDescription: to quickly remove a piece of clothing
glosses.sourceDescription: to quickly remove a piece of clothing
examples: Leo threw off his wet jacket at the door.
She quickly threw her heavy scarf off indoors.

glosses.meaningKo: 새롭거나 뜻밖의 것을 내놓다
glosses.englishDescription: to produce something new or unexpected
glosses.sourceDescription: to produce something new or unexpected
examples: The survey threw up two useful ideas.
Our simple test threw up an unexpected result.

glosses.meaningKo: 공문서의 빈 공간에 이름이나 주소 등의 정보를 추가하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to add information such as your name or address in the empty spaces on an official document
glosses.sourceDescription: to add information such as your name or address in the empty spaces on an official document
examples: Gus gave me a form to fill out which signed over ten per cent to the IRS.
It took me several hours to fill out the application form.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 시간이 많지 않을 때 무언가를 계속하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to continue doing something, especially when you do not have much time
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue doing something, especially when you do not have much time
examples: I’ve pushed on with the work because I want to finish it today.
There’s a lot to do, so let’s push on.

glosses.meaningKo: 어렵거나 불쾌한 상황을 잘 이겨 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to deal well with a difficult or unpleasant situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal well with a difficult or unpleasant situation
examples: She rose above a disappointing first practice.
Our group rose above the early confusion and finished well.

glosses.meaningKo: 신중하게 생각하고 사람 또는 상황에 대한 의견을 형성한다
glosses.englishDescription: to think carefully and form an opinion about a person or a situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to think carefully and form an opinion about a person or a situation
examples: And Janet respected Kay's ability to size up a situation squarely and feel, so it seemed to Janet, undivided.
He sized up the situation and immediately decided what to do.

glosses.meaningKo: 장소에 도착해 공식 명단에 이름을 적다
glosses.englishDescription: to write your name on an official list when you arrive at a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to write your name on an official list when you arrive at a place
examples: Every visitor must sign in at the front desk.
We signed in when we reached the activity center.

glosses.meaningKo: 편지를 끝맺다
glosses.englishDescription: to end a letter
glosses.sourceDescription: to end a letter
examples: I signed off the letter with my full name.
She always signs off with a cheerful message.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일을 하기로 동의하거나 과정이나 조직에 참여하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to agree to do something, or to join a course or organization
glosses.sourceDescription: to agree to do something, or to join a course or organization
examples: She’s decided to sign up for evening classes.
`And I'll bet she wants me to sign up for a whole course of treatment to defuse me.

glosses.meaningKo: 윗사람에게 버릇없이 대꾸하다
glosses.englishDescription: to reply rudely to someone who has more authority than you
glosses.sourceDescription: to reply rudely to someone who has more authority than you
examples: Ben apologized for answering back to his teacher.
Do not answer back when someone calmly corrects you.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 활용하여 이득을 얻기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to get an advantage by making use of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to get an advantage by making use of something
examples: But Fusionists knew they had the talent and there was never one that didn't trade on that.
They are trading on their reputation.

glosses.meaningKo: 각 부분이 잘 보이도록 무언가를 계획적으로 배치하거나 펼치다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange or spread something in a planned way so that its parts can be seen clearly
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrange something according to a detailed plan, for example rooms in a building, roads in a town, or areas on a piece of land
examples: A display of local history material was laid out on the table.
The brochure is beautifully laid out and illustrated.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 하거나 가질 기회를 놓치다
glosses.englishDescription: to lose an opportunity to do or have something
glosses.sourceDescription: to lose an opportunity to do or have something
examples: Join the game now so you do not miss out.
Mina missed out on the last seat in the workshop.

glosses.meaningKo: 상황이나 사건을 행동으로 재연하다
glosses.englishDescription: to show the events that happened in a situation by doing them again or by doing the same things as the people involved
glosses.sourceDescription: to show the events that happened in a situation by doing them again or by doing the same things as the people involved
examples: The class acted out a scene from the story.
We acted out the bus-stop conversation in pairs.

glosses.meaningKo: 투숙을 결정한 호텔이나 개인병원에 도착하고 접수처에서 일하는 사람에게 개인 정보를 알려주기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive at a hotel or a private hospital where you have arranged to stay and give your personal details to the person working at the reception desk
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive at a hotel or a private hospital where you have arranged to stay and give your personal details to the person working at the reception desk
examples: Graham paid the taxi driver, who had helped to carry the suitcases into the foyer, then crossed to the reception desk to check in.
The receptionist checked us in.

glosses.meaningKo: 도서관에서 책을 대출하다
glosses.englishDescription: to borrow a book from a library
glosses.sourceDescription: to borrow a book from a library
examples: I checked out two science books today.
You may check this novel out for three weeks.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 부분이 잘 어우러져 짜임새가 있다
glosses.englishDescription: if something hangs together, the different parts of it combine well so that it seems well planned and organized
glosses.sourceDescription: if something hangs together, the different parts of it combine well so that it seems well planned and organized
examples: The story hangs together from beginning to end.
The parts began to hang together after one more edit.

glosses.meaningKo: 대화가 끝날 때 전화 사용을 중단해야 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop using a telephone at the end of a conversation
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop using a telephone at the end of a conversation
examples: Finally, he was able to hang up, drained from the experience.
Starting to hang up, he was halted by the sudden, startling change in the quality of the voice.

glosses.meaningKo: 기대하거나 필요한 수준에 이르다
glosses.englishDescription: to be good enough
glosses.sourceDescription: to be good enough
examples: The new glue measured up in our craft test.
I practiced hard because I wanted to measure up.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신을 따라오거나 쫓아오는 누군가로부터 벗어나기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to escape from someone who is following or chasing you
glosses.sourceDescription: to escape from someone who is following or chasing you
examples: Flew up to Ireland to shake off the watchers, then on to Antwerp.
They ran into the alley, hoping to shake off their pursuers.

glosses.meaningKo: 가방이나 용기에서 물건을 찾아 꺼내다
glosses.englishDescription: to pull something out of a bag or other container
glosses.sourceDescription: to pull something out of a bag or other container
examples: She fished a blue pencil out of her bag.
I fished out the last coin from my pocket.

glosses.meaningKo: 햇볕이 강하게 내리쬐다
glosses.englishDescription: if the sun beats down, it shines very brightly making the weather very hot
glosses.sourceDescription: if the sun beats down, it shines very brightly making the weather very hot
examples: The sun can beat down brightly at noon.
At midday, the sun will beat down on the field.

glosses.meaningKo: 흥분하거나 걱정한 뒤 긴장을 풀다
glosses.englishDescription: to relax after a period of excitement or worry
glosses.sourceDescription: to relax after a period of excitement or worry
examples: I read a quiet story to wind down before bed.
We wound down with soft music after the busy fair.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일을 끝내다
glosses.englishDescription: to end something
glosses.sourceDescription: to end something
examples: We wound up the meeting with a short quiz.
The teacher will wind up the lesson at three.

glosses.meaningKo: 오랜 수색 끝에 누군가나 무언가를 찾기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to find someone or something after a long search
glosses.sourceDescription: to find someone or something after a long search
examples: I finally managed to track him down in Manchester.
I'll go and have a quick word, then we'll track down Mr Derringer.

glosses.meaningKo: 법원이 법을 공식적으로 무효화하다
glosses.englishDescription: if a judge or court strikes down a law, they officially end it
glosses.sourceDescription: if a judge or court strikes down a law, they officially end it
examples: The court struck down the outdated law.
A judge struck the outdated law down after review.

glosses.meaningKo: 문서의 단어 위에 선을 그어 지우다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove words from a document, for example by drawing a line through them
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove words from a document, for example by drawing a line through them
examples: Please strike out the repeated word.
Mina struck the extra sentence out with a pencil.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 앞으로 밀어넣거나, 멀리, 특히 몸의 일부를 밀어넣거나 스트레칭하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to push or stretch something forwards or away from you, especially a part of your body
glosses.sourceDescription: to push or stretch something forwards or away from you, especially a part of your body
examples: He had only to stick out his thumb and a car squealed to a halt.
She stuck her arm out of the car window and waved.

glosses.meaningKo: 서로 가까이 지내며 돕다
glosses.englishDescription: if people stick together, they remain close together and support one another
glosses.sourceDescription: if people stick together, they remain close together and support one another
examples: Our group stuck together during the long project.
Friends should stick together when work gets tricky.

glosses.meaningKo: 바꾸지 않고 계속 사용하거나 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue to do or use something, and not change it
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue to do or use something, and not change it
examples: I will stick with the study plan for one month.
We stuck with our first color choice.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려운 시기나 상황을 큰 문제 없이 견뎌 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to get to the end of a difficult or dangerous period or situation without any serious problems
glosses.sourceDescription: to get to the end of a difficult or dangerous period or situation without any serious problems
examples: Our team can ride out a difficult first week together.
The little shop managed to ride out a slow month.

glosses.meaningKo: 빛이나 소리가 무언가에 도달하는 것을 멈추기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to stop light or sound from reaching something
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop light or sound from reaching something
examples: Previous experience had taught him that having the Fat Man in the background tended to block out the light.
That tree in the neighbour’s garden blocks out a lot of light.

glosses.meaningKo: 사기 전에 여러 가게를 둘러보다
glosses.englishDescription: to go to several shops before you decide what particular thing to buy
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to several shops before you decide what particular thing to buy
examples: We shopped around before choosing a new lamp.
It helps to shop around for the right backpack.

glosses.meaningKo: 놀라거나 걱정될 때 큰 소리로 외치다
glosses.englishDescription: to shout something, especially when you are surprised or worried
glosses.sourceDescription: to shout something, especially when you are surprised or worried
examples: Mina cried out, "Look at the rainbow!"
"We found it!" Leo cried out.

glosses.meaningKo: 공기나 가스를 넣어 부풀리다
glosses.englishDescription: to fill something with air or gas
glosses.sourceDescription: to fill something with air or gas
examples: We blew up five balloons for the class party.
Can you help me blow this beach ball up?

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람처럼 보이도록 옷을 입히는 재미
glosses.englishDescription: to put clothes on someone so that they look like someone else, for fun
glosses.sourceDescription: to put clothes on someone so that they look like someone else, for fun
examples: For her birthday party, they had dressed her up as a fairy.
They had dressed up as princes and princesses.

glosses.meaningKo: 일을 끝내기 전에 남은 몇 가지를 처리하다
glosses.englishDescription: to deal with the last few things that have to be done before you can finish something
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal with the last few things that have to be done before you can finish something
examples: We tied up the last details before the class show.
Let us tie the loose ends up and finish the poster.

glosses.meaningKo: 필요 없는 물건과 먼지를 치워 장소나 용기를 깨끗이 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a place or container clean or tidy by removing objects that are not wanted and getting rid of any dirt or dust in it
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a place or container clean or tidy by removing objects that are not wanted and getting rid of any dirt or dust in it
examples: We cleaned out the art cupboard on Friday.
Please clean your desk drawer out before the term ends.

glosses.meaningKo: 장소를 완전히 깨끗하고 정돈되게 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a place completely clean and tidy
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a place completely clean and tidy
examples: We cleaned up the classroom after the activity.
Please help me clean the kitchen up.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일이 일어날지 자세히 계획하기
glosses.englishDescription: to plan in detail how something will happen
glosses.sourceDescription: to plan in detail how something will happen
examples: Her own future had been mapped out for her by her parents.
She'd ask me to wait outside while she made phone calls, and once there I began to map out my future alone.

glosses.meaningKo: 물기가 빠져 마르다
glosses.englishDescription: if something dries out or is dried out, some or all the water comes out of it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something dries out or is dried out, some or all the water comes out of it
examples: Leave the wet clay outside to dry out.
The towels dried out quickly in the warm sun.

glosses.meaningKo: 물기가 모두 빠져 완전히 마르다
glosses.englishDescription: if something dries up or is dried up, all the water comes out of it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something dries up or is dried up, all the water comes out of it
examples: The small puddle dried up in the afternoon sun.
The stream dried up after many sunny weeks.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 진실이라는 것을 보여주거나 누군가가 진실을 말하고 있다는 것을 보여주기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to show that something is true or that someone is telling the truth
glosses.sourceDescription: to show that something is true or that someone is telling the truth
examples: I always said – and Rick will bear me out – that this wouldn’t work.
Now, that could bear out what I've always thought -- that Alec was set up, that he knew too much, and now he wants to blow it sky high.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 하거나 마치는 동안 누군가에게 인내심을 가져 달라고 요청하는 예의 바른 방법으로 사용됩니다
glosses.englishDescription: used as a polite way of asking someone to be patient while you do or finish something
glosses.sourceDescription: used as a polite way of asking someone to be patient while you do or finish something
examples: I know it's boring, but bear with me for a bit.
If you just bear with me for a few more minutes, we’ll have all the paperwork finished.

glosses.meaningKo: 새해의 시작을 축하하며 종을 울리다
glosses.englishDescription: to ring bells to celebrate the beginning of a new year
glosses.sourceDescription: to ring bells to celebrate the beginning of a new year
examples: People rang in the new year with cheerful bells.
The town will ring the new year in at midnight.

glosses.meaningKo: 큰 선명한 사운드를 생성하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to produce a loud clear sound
glosses.sourceDescription: to produce a loud clear sound
examples: As Mike reached two glasses down from the shelf and uncorked the bottle they heard Piers's voice ring out round the kitchen.
Rob’s laughter rang out in the large room.

glosses.meaningKo: 기회를 이용해 이익이나 이점을 얻다
glosses.englishDescription: to use an opportunity to make a profit or gain an advantage
glosses.sourceDescription: to use an opportunity to make a profit or gain an advantage
examples: The shop cashed in on the sudden demand for notebooks.
Small cafes can cash in on the festival crowds.

glosses.meaningKo: 나쁜 것, 불법적인 것을 찾아서 없애기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to find something bad or illegal and get rid of it
glosses.sourceDescription: to find something bad or illegal and get rid of it
examples: The president vowed to root out corruption.
`However sincere, the chap had a good incentive to root out anyone even remotely qualifying for his detection methods.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 사람이나 사물을 다른 사람이나 사물로 착각하다
glosses.englishDescription: to think that one person or thing is another person or thing
glosses.sourceDescription: to think that one person or thing is another person or thing
examples: I mixed up the two similar folders.
Do not mix Sam up with his twin brother.

glosses.meaningKo: 새로운 것 또는 다른 것을 시작하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to start doing something new or different
glosses.sourceDescription: to start doing something new or different
examples: In the longer term, the company wants to branch out into providing investment advice.
Quinn wanted to leave the company and branch out on his own.

glosses.meaningKo: 효과가 나타나기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start to have an effect
glosses.sourceDescription: to start to have an effect
examples: The room heater kicked in after a short delay.
The new study routine began to kick in after a week.

glosses.meaningKo: 발을 흔들어서 신발이 벗겨지도록
glosses.englishDescription: to make your shoes come off by shaking your feet
glosses.sourceDescription: to make your shoes come off by shaking your feet
examples: Autumn wiggled her toes and wished she could kick off her boots.
Phyllis kicked off her sandals.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 장소나 단체에서 나가게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to force someone to leave a place or organization
glosses.sourceDescription: to force someone to leave a place or organization
examples: The staff kicked everyone out when the museum closed.
The club kicked Ben out for repeatedly ignoring its rules.

glosses.meaningKo: 감정이나 관심을 불러일으키다
glosses.englishDescription: to cause feelings or memories to become active
glosses.sourceDescription: same as stir
examples: So there was Felicity to stir up my apprehension; and of course, Milton Hemming.
The sight of the school stirred up a lot of memories.

glosses.meaningKo: 구조물 또는 구조물의 일부를 파괴하거나 제거하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to destroy or remove a structure or part of a structure
glosses.sourceDescription: to destroy or remove a structure or part of a structure
examples: That old house should have been torn down years ago.
going to tear down the house and build some modern houses on the grounds.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가의 강도나 두드러짐, 심각성, 불쾌감을 줄이다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something less strong, noticeable, severe, or offensive
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something less severe, shocking, or offensive
examples: She checked her complexion, feathering in the edges of her eye make-up and dabbing her lips on a tissue to tone down the gloss.
Somebody needed some plastic surgery to tone down their facial features.

glosses.meaningKo: 가격이나 양을 낮추다
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce a price or amount
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce a price or amount
examples: The shop knocked down the price of the lamp.
A coupon knocked the total cost down by five dollars.

glosses.meaningKo: 따뜻하게 유지하기 위해 옷을 충분히 입기
glosses.englishDescription: to wear enough clothes to keep you warm
glosses.sourceDescription: to wear enough clothes to keep you warm
examples: I could hear my mother telling me to wrap up warm.
Now I must excuse myself for a moment and go and wrap up warmly.

glosses.meaningKo: 천에서 물질이 씻겨지면 세탁으로 제거할 수 있습니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a substance washes out of cloth, it can be removed by washing
glosses.sourceDescription: if a substance washes out of cloth, it can be removed by washing
examples: All the colour has washed out of these old curtains.
Permanent dyes won’t wash out.

glosses.meaningKo: 식사 뒤에 접시나 컵 등을 설거지하다
glosses.englishDescription: to wash plates, cups, spoons etc after a meal
glosses.sourceDescription: to wash plates, cups, spoons etc after a meal
examples: I washed up while my sister dried the plates.
We always wash up together after dinner.

glosses.meaningKo: 여럿이 비용을 조금씩 보태다
glosses.englishDescription: if people chip in, they each give some money to help pay for something
glosses.sourceDescription: if people chip in, they each give some money to help pay for something
examples: We all chipped in for a class thank-you gift.
Each cousin chipped in one dollar for the flowers.

glosses.meaningKo: 프린터에서 컴퓨터 문서 사본을 생산하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to produce a copy of a computer document from a printer
glosses.sourceDescription: to produce a copy of a computer document from a printer
examples: I'll go and ask one of my colleagues to print out the appropriate data.
Should I print out that graph now?

glosses.meaningKo: 방을 두고 문을 잠그고 아무도 나갈 수 없도록 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to put someone in a room and lock the door so they cannot leave
glosses.sourceDescription: to put someone in a room and lock the door so they cannot leave
examples: She went to her hotel room and locked herself in.
You can’t keep me locked in.

glosses.meaningKo: 작업이나 장비를 멀리 두고 하루의 작업을 마무리하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to finish work for the day by putting work or equipment away
glosses.sourceDescription: to finish work for the day by putting work or equipment away
examples: The last scene of the day was finally in the can and everyone could pack up and go home, albeit an hour later than usual.
The workmen have already packed up and left.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 마지막 남은 어려움을 제거함으로써 의견 불일치나 문제를 성공적으로 처리합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to deal successfully with a disagreement or problem, especially by removing the last remaining difficulties
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal successfully with a disagreement or problem, especially by removing the last remaining difficulties
examples: They started rehearsing the Christmas concert well in advance in order to iron out the kinks by December 20.
They’re meeting in Berlin to iron out the final details of the contract.

glosses.meaningKo: 만족스러운 방법으로 무언가를 끝내기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to end something in a satisfactory way
glosses.sourceDescription: to end something in a satisfactory way
examples: Coffin wondered if he would say something memorable or profound to round off the moment, but he didn't do so.
If there is something that he feels he has to round off, I don't begrudge it him.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 갑자기 화를 내며 맞서다
glosses.englishDescription: to react angrily towards someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to react angrily towards someone
examples: Mia rounded on her brother for moving her books.
The speaker rounded on the person who interrupted.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 목적을 위해 사람이나 동물을 한곳에 모으다
glosses.englishDescription: to bring animals or people together in one place for a particular purpose
glosses.sourceDescription: to bring animals or people together in one place for a particular purpose
examples: The guide rounded up the campers before lunch.
We rounded the puppies up for their checkup.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제를 덜 심각해 보이게 만드는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make a problem seem less serious
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a problem seem less serious
examples: He’s trying to smooth over differences between the two leaders.
Usually he is asking his brother to have a word with one duke or another, to smooth over some political difference.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가의 말을 듣지 않거나, 무언가에 대한 생각을 멈추도록 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop listening to someone, or to stop thinking about something
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop listening to someone, or to stop thinking about something
examples: He allowed the professional part of himself to run finally down and switch off.
Now stop agonising, stop thinking about wretched Desmond and switch off.

glosses.meaningKo: 천으로 물건의 안쪽을 닦다
glosses.englishDescription: to clean the inside of something with a cloth
glosses.sourceDescription: to clean the inside of something with a cloth
examples: I wiped out the lunch box with a clean cloth.
Please wipe the empty drawer out before using it.

glosses.meaningKo: 완전히 이해되다
glosses.englishDescription: to become completely understood
glosses.sourceDescription: to become completely understood
examples: The good news took a moment to sink in.
After another example, the new rule finally sank in.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 사람의 특성이 다른 사람에게도 영향을 주다
glosses.englishDescription: if a quality that someone has rubs off, it starts to affect another person so that they start to have that quality too
glosses.sourceDescription: if a quality that someone has rubs off, it starts to affect another person so that they start to have that quality too
examples: Her calm attitude rubbed off on the whole group.
Mina's love of reading soon rubbed off on Leo.

glosses.meaningKo: 헤어지다; 결별하다
glosses.englishDescription: if two people split up, they end their relationship
glosses.sourceDescription: same as split
examples: Her parents split up a few months ago.
She was due to fly to Barcelona with her mum; their first holiday together since she and Julie's dad split up.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람들과 함께 일을 거들다
glosses.englishDescription: to join with other people in doing a job
glosses.sourceDescription: to join with other people in doing a job
examples: We all pitched in to clean the classroom.
Two neighbors pitched in with the garden work.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일이 걱정되거나 속상하지 않은 듯 넘기다
glosses.englishDescription: to show that something does not worry or upset you
glosses.sourceDescription: to show that something does not worry or upset you
examples: She shrugged off the small spelling mistake.
Leo shrugged the delay off and kept smiling.
