glosses.meaningKo: 특정 사물이나 사람을 찾으려고 노력하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to try to find a particular thing or person
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to find a particular thing or person
examples: I wanted to hunt down Skorpion, take it apart, discover its secret.
Somehow, Stone knew he had to shake this guy, find an interpreter and hunt down Le Borveaux.

glosses.meaningKo: 설득을 받아 갑자기 반대를 그만두다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly stop opposing something, especially because people have persuaded you
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly stop opposing something, especially because people have persuaded you
examples: Dad caved in and let us choose the music.
The group finally caved in after hearing her reasons.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 라디오나 텔레비전 방송을 듣거나 보다
glosses.englishDescription: to listen to or watch a particular broadcast on the radio or television
glosses.sourceDescription: to listen to or watch a particular broadcast on the radio or television
examples: Tune in at six for the science program.
We tuned in to watch the school quiz on local television.

glosses.meaningKo: 좋지 않은 일을 겪은 뒤 다시 건강하거나 행복하거나 성공적인 상태가 되다
glosses.englishDescription: to become healthy, happy, or successful again after something bad has happened to you
glosses.sourceDescription: to become healthy, happy, or successful again after something bad has happened to you
examples: Mina bounced back after a disappointing quiz.
The team bounced back from a slow start.

glosses.meaningKo: 기기나 컴퓨터를 다른 기기나 시스템, 네트워크에 연결하다
glosses.englishDescription: to connect a device or computer to another device, system, or network
glosses.sourceDescription: if you hook up to a place or to the Internet, or if you hook something up, you become connected to it through your computer
examples: He hooked the microphone up to a tape recorder.
I can hook up to the library from my computer.

glosses.meaningKo: 열심히 일하여 자신의 경력이나 직위를 개발하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to develop a career or position for yourself by working hard
glosses.sourceDescription: to develop a career or position for yourself by working hard
examples: By sticking to a few rich women, Emerald had managed to carve out a living.
It can be difficult to carve out a niche in the fashion industry.

glosses.meaningKo: 빡빡하거나 젖은 옷을 제거하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to remove a tight or wet piece of clothing
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove a tight or wet piece of clothing
examples: He crawled into the unmade bed, then reached down to peel off his socks.
The kids peeled off their wet clothes.

glosses.meaningKo: 아주 빨리 먹을 것을 준비하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to prepare something to eat very quickly
glosses.sourceDescription: to prepare something to eat very quickly
examples: If you’re hungry, I can whip us up some lunch.
`But I intend to rescue you from starvation - I'm going to whip up a feast which you'll be quite unable to resist!

glosses.meaningKo: 글 등을 핵심 사실만 남겨 짧게 줄이다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something such as a piece of writing shorter by giving only the basic, most important facts
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something such as a piece of writing shorter by giving only the basic, most important facts
examples: Please boil the report down to three short points.
Mina boiled her long notes down into one clear page.

glosses.meaningKo: 상대가 이해하도록 매우 분명하게 말하거나 설명하다
glosses.englishDescription: to say or explain something very clearly because someone has not understood something
glosses.sourceDescription: to say or explain something very clearly because someone has not understood something
examples: The teacher spelled out each step for us.
Please spell the rule out so everyone understands.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 정확히 파악하거나 설명하다
glosses.englishDescription: to understand or describe something exactly
glosses.sourceDescription: to understand or describe something exactly
examples: We finally pinned down the cause of the wobble.
It is hard to pin that unusual color down.

glosses.meaningKo: 필터로 원하지 않는 것을 걸러 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove something that is not wanted using a filter
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove something that is not wanted using a filter
examples: This cloth can filter out tiny bits from the juice.
The screen filtered the sand out of the water.

glosses.meaningKo: 나중에 바뀔 수 있음을 전제로 일정을 임시로 잡다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange for something to happen or for someone to do something, knowing that it may have to be changed later
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrange for something to happen or for someone to do something, knowing that it may have to be changed later
examples: Let us pencil in the rehearsal for next Tuesday.
I penciled our museum visit in for the morning.

glosses.meaningKo: 집단이나 모음에서 적합하지 않은 것을 골라 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove a person or thing that is not suitable or good enough, especially from a group or collection
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove a person or thing that is not suitable or good enough, especially from a group or collection
examples: We weeded out the duplicate cards from the set.
The editor can weed out unclear examples from the list.

glosses.meaningKo: 심각한 실수를 하거나, 무언가를 망치거나, 특히 상황을 망치는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make a serious mistake, or to spoil something, especially a situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a serious mistake, or to spoil something, especially a situation
examples: He made a bad decision that screwed up his entire life.
I really screwed up this time, didn’t I?

glosses.meaningKo: 작은 용기로 배 안의 물을 퍼내다
glosses.englishDescription: to empty water from a boat using a small container
glosses.sourceDescription: to empty water from a boat using a small container
examples: We bailed out the canoe with a plastic cup.
Dad showed us how to bail the little boat out.

glosses.meaningKo: 예상치 못하게 누군가를 만나기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to meet someone unexpectedly
glosses.sourceDescription: to meet someone unexpectedly
examples: And there's always the chance of bumping into pop celebrities and minor royals.
Given that not all the members will be there all the time, the chance of bumping into many other people is slim.

glosses.meaningKo: 느낌이나 기억과 같은 것을 마음에 심어주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to bring something such as a feeling or memory to your mind
glosses.sourceDescription: to bring something such as a feeling or memory to your mind
examples: Places, periods and people are conjured up in depth and detail.
They conjure up in no time at all a Nordic romanticism ardent, strange and almost mystical.

glosses.meaningKo: 몸을 굽히고 팔다리를 가까이 모은 채 앉거나 눕다
glosses.englishDescription: to sit or lie with your body curved and your arms and legs drawn close
glosses.sourceDescription: to lie with your back curved and your legs and arms close to your chest
examples: We curled up together for warmth.
We sat curled up on the sofa, watching the late film.

glosses.meaningKo: 돈이나 음식 등을 최대한 오래 쓰다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something such as money or food last as long as possible
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something such as money or food last as long as possible
examples: Nia eked out her allowance until Friday.
We eked the picnic snacks out through the afternoon.

glosses.meaningKo: 불쾌한 사실을 무시하거나 피하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to ignore or avoid unpleasant facts
glosses.sourceDescription: to ignore or avoid unpleasant facts
examples: At work, others may gloss over problems, but you solve them.
At work, there is no need to gloss over problems.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가에 많은 돈을 쓰다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend a lot of money on something
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend a lot of money on something
examples: We lashed out on a sturdy new picnic table.
The club lashed out on better art supplies.

glosses.meaningKo: 액체를 닦아 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove liquid using a cloth or another absorbent object
glosses.sourceDescription: same as mop
examples: He mopped up the milk with a tissue.
Then he dropped his eyes to his plate and began to mop up a puddle of syrup with a bit of waffle.

glosses.meaningKo: 지나치게 커지거나 오래 이어진 것을 제한하거나 통제하다
glosses.englishDescription: to limit or control something that has developed too much or has continued for too long
glosses.sourceDescription: to limit or control something that has developed too much or has continued for too long
examples: We reined in the party budget before buying decorations.
The teacher reined the noisy discussion in.

glosses.meaningKo: 처음에 잘못해서 처음부터 다시 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to do something again from the beginning, especially because you did it badly the first time
glosses.sourceDescription: to do something again from the beginning, especially because you did it badly the first time
examples: I did the puzzle over after noticing my mistake.
Please do the last page over more carefully.

glosses.meaningKo: 빨리 가기 위해서, 특히 잘못하고 나서
glosses.englishDescription: to leave quickly, especially after doing something wrong
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave quickly, especially after doing something wrong
examples: Did the thief, or thieves, make off with anything else, or did they come solely to remove my son's ring?
The kids made off when they heard us coming.

glosses.meaningKo: 종종 좋은 이유 없이 누군가를 싫어하기 시작하죠
glosses.englishDescription: to begin to dislike someone, often without having a good reason
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin to dislike someone, often without having a good reason
examples: Martin took against her almost straight away.
Who had taken against amiable Sir Charles?

glosses.meaningKo: 물건을 여러 조각으로 분해하다
glosses.englishDescription: to separate an object into pieces
glosses.sourceDescription: to separate an object into pieces
examples: We took the model apart to see how it worked.
This toy can be taken apart for easy storage.

glosses.meaningKo: 작별 인사를 하려고 역이나 공항 등에 함께 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to go somewhere such as a station or airport with someone in order to say goodbye to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to go somewhere such as a station or airport with someone in order to say goodbye to them
examples: We went to the station to see Grandma off.
Her friends saw her off at the bus stop.

glosses.meaningKo: 용기를 내어 어려운 상황에 맞서다
glosses.englishDescription: to start being brave and dealing with a difficult situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to start being brave and dealing with a difficult situation
examples: Leo chose to man up and admit his mistake.
I had to man up and finish the difficult task.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 잘못했다고 화나게 비판한다는 것은
glosses.englishDescription: to criticize someone angrily for doing something wrong
glosses.sourceDescription: to criticize someone angrily for doing something wrong
examples: 5 Tell off your boss, or a parent, or a spouse: someone you've wanted to tell off for some time but never dared do so.
The teacher told me off for talking again today.

glosses.meaningKo: 누구에 대한 소식을 묻기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to ask for news about someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to ask for news about someone
examples: I met Bob and he asked after you.
`I thought you might be calling to ask after that guy you sent us.

glosses.meaningKo: 나중에 쓰려고 일부를 남겨 두다
glosses.englishDescription: to keep part of something so that you can use it later
glosses.sourceDescription: to keep part of something so that you can use it later

We kept three cookies back for the late guests.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 말하는 것에 빠르고 종종 무례하게 답하기 위해 이 표현은 특히 아이들이 부모에게 무례한 것을 묘사하는 데 사용됩니다
glosses.englishDescription: to reply quickly and often rudely to something that someone says. This expression is used especially to describe children being rude to their parents
glosses.sourceDescription: to reply quickly and often rudely to something that someone says. This expression is used especially to describe children being rude to their parents
examples: Most young children attempt to talk back to parents.
Or maybe you don't like the way your children talk back to you.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려운 일을 성공시키기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in doing something difficult
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in doing something difficult
examples: Now, and again due to Abramov's skills, they were poised to bring off an even bigger coup.
Whatever Maurice Campbell thought, whatever he said to her, she was beginning to feel she might bring off a coup.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 물건을 누군가의 집 등에 데려오거나 가져오다
glosses.englishDescription: to take someone or something somewhere, especially to someone’s house
glosses.sourceDescription: to take someone or something somewhere, especially to someone’s house

Nora brought some craft paper round to my house.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 하거나 말하는 것으로 무언가를 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to begin something by doing or saying something
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin something by doing or saying something

The Prime Minister had invited the President to lead off the press conference.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 집에 올 때까지 잠을 자지 않기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to not go to sleep until someone comes home
glosses.sourceDescription: to not go to sleep until someone comes home
examples: Don’t wait up for me, I’ll be very late tonight.
If he's not there when we get in then you can go to bed and I'll wait up for him.

glosses.meaningKo: 잘못된 행동 때문에 대학에서 퇴학 처분을 받다
glosses.englishDescription: to be ordered to leave a university because you have behaved badly
glosses.sourceDescription: to be ordered to leave a university because you have behaved badly
examples: The university sent the student down for repeated rule breaking.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량이나 운전자가 길가에 차를 세우다

glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls over, they stop by the side of the road

We pulled over to check the map.

glosses.meaningKo: 매우 어려운 상황을 이겨 내거나 누군가가 이겨 내도록 돕다

glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in a very difficult situation, or to help someone to do this

The small shop managed to pull through with careful planning.

glosses.meaningKo: 배고프지 않기 때문에 소량만 먹기 위해

glosses.sourceDescription: to eat only small amounts of a meal because you do not feel hungry

Most of the time he just picks at his food.

glosses.meaningKo: 사용하거나 문지르면서 무언가를 서서히 사라지거나 얇아지도록 만드는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something gradually disappear or become thinner by using or rubbing it
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something gradually disappear or become thinner by using or rubbing it

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 매우 강하게 비판하다
glosses.englishDescription: to criticize someone or something very strongly
glosses.sourceDescription: to criticize someone or something very strongly
examples: The coach hit out at the confusing new schedule.
Parents hit out at the sudden timetable change.

glosses.meaningKo: 빨리 자리를 떠나기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to leave a place quickly
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave a place quickly
examples: Clear off, both of you!
They’ve all cleared off and left me to clean this mess up.

glosses.meaningKo: 용기에 넣어 자라나는 어린 식물을 가지고 땅에 넣어 자라게 하는 것이다

glosses.sourceDescription: to take a young plant that is growing in a container and put it in the ground to grow

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 상황이나 사건이 사람들을 하나로 묶으면, 그들은 서로 만나고 알게 된다

glosses.sourceDescription: if a particular situation or event throws people together, it causes them to meet and get to know one another

When a group has been thrown together this quickly, where is the leader?

glosses.meaningKo: 장소를 떠나다
glosses.englishDescription: to leave a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave a place
examples: We should push off before the museum closes.
The family pushed off soon after breakfast.

glosses.meaningKo: 의견을 큰 소리로, 흔히 무리하게 말하다

glosses.sourceDescription: to express your opinions loudly, especially in an unreasonable way
examples: He sounded off about the new seating plan.
Several students sounded off before hearing all the details.

glosses.meaningKo: 재산이나 권리에 대한 소유권을 이전하는 경우 문서에 자신의 이름을 기재하여 더 이상 자신의 것이 아니라는 것에 동의합니다

glosses.sourceDescription: if you sign away property or a right to something, you agree that it no longer belongs to you by writing your name on a document

glosses.meaningKo: 목록의 항목에 완료 표시를 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to tick off something
glosses.sourceDescription: to tick off something
examples: Check off each item after you pack it.
I checked the last task off my list.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것에 대해 농담하는 것은 그것이 중요하지 않거나 심각한 것이 아니라고 생각하는 것을 보여주기 위해 농담하는 것입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to joke about something in order to show that you think it is not important or serious
glosses.sourceDescription: to joke about something in order to show that you think it is not important or serious
examples: Much as he would have liked to laugh off what Jerry Brahms was saying, his instincts were telling him to be more cautious.
They just laughed off the rumours that they are getting married.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 큰 양에서 특정 양의 무언가를 얻기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to take a particular amount of something from a larger amount
glosses.sourceDescription: to take a particular amount of something from a larger amount

glosses.meaningKo: 이미 노래를 부르고 있는 사람과 함께 노래를 부르기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: to sing a song with someone who is already singing

The best thing is that people are now singing along to the songs.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 큰 목소리로 노래하다
glosses.englishDescription: to sing with a louder voice
glosses.sourceDescription: to sing with a louder voice
examples: The teacher asked the choir to sing out.
Sing out so the people at the back can hear you.

glosses.meaningKo: 장시간 잠을 계속 자야 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to continue sleeping for a long time
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue sleeping for a long time
examples: I CAN'T sleep through the night.
I still find it difficult to sleep through the night.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려운 상황에 처한 누군가를 계속 지원하기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: to continue to support someone who is in a difficult situation
examples: "But I feel like I pushed her away when she needed me to stick by her.
`You can't do your job, and you can't even stick by your own folk.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 남의 눈을 피해 한곳에 머물다
glosses.englishDescription: if you hole up or are holed up somewhere, you stay there, especially because you are hiding
glosses.sourceDescription: if you hole up or are holed up somewhere, you stay there, especially because you are hiding
examples: We holed up in the reading room during the rain.
Mina likes to hole up in her cozy corner with a book.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건이나 사람을 장소에서 멀리 옮기기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: to move goods or people away from a place
examples: The situation looked bad and tourists were shipping out.
Thousands of tons of steel were shipped out from the docks.

glosses.meaningKo: 일부 업무를 회사 밖의 사람들에게 맡기다
glosses.englishDescription: to send part of your work to be done by people outside a company
glosses.sourceDescription: to send part of your work to be done by people outside a company
examples: The studio farmed out the printing to a local shop.
We farmed the binding work out to a specialist.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건을 하나씩 세는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to count things one by one
glosses.sourceDescription: to count things one by one
examples: She counted out £100 in £5 notes.
She opened up the side of her van and began to count out rolls of bread and paper cups.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 결혼할 배우자를 찾아 주다
glosses.englishDescription: to find a husband or wife for someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to find a husband or wife for someone
examples: In the old tale, the queen hoped to marry her son off.
The aunt kept trying to marry her nephew off.

glosses.meaningKo: 방이나 건물에 장비를 넣어 특정 용도로 사용할 수 있도록 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to put equipment into a room or building so that it can be used for a particular purpose
glosses.sourceDescription: to put equipment into a room or building so that it can be used for a particular purpose
examples: The kitchen has been fitted out with pine cupboards.
They are fitting out new offices.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 약속했거나 동의한 행동을 하지 않기로 결정하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to decide not to do something that you had promised or agreed to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to decide not to do something that you had promised or agreed to do
examples: I made half-hearted attempts to cry off, but they both insisted.

glosses.meaningKo: 폭풍이 지나가 끝나다
glosses.englishDescription: if a storm blows over, it ends
glosses.sourceDescription: if a storm blows over, it ends
examples: The brief storm began to blow over before the picnic.

glosses.meaningKo: 이야기, 변명 또는 계획을 발명하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to invent a story, excuse, or plan
glosses.sourceDescription: to invent a story, excuse, or plan
examples: Between them they cooked up some story to tell their parents.

glosses.meaningKo: 평소보다 편안하고 격식 없는 옷을 입다
glosses.englishDescription: to wear clothes that are more informal than the clothes that you usually wear
glosses.sourceDescription: to wear clothes that are more informal than the clothes that you usually wear
examples: We dressed down for the relaxed school picnic.
Staff can dress down on the final Friday of each month.

glosses.meaningKo: 너무 겁이 나서 하려고 했던 일을 하지 않기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: to not do something you were going to do because you are too frightened
examples: He picked up his phone, watching to see if I was going to chicken out.

glosses.meaningKo: 아래쪽으로 밀거나 누르기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to push or press downwards
glosses.sourceDescription: to push or press downwards
examples: I can't have a wobbly surface when I'm trying to bear down.

glosses.meaningKo: 전화를 끝내기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to finish a phone call
glosses.sourceDescription: to finish a phone call
examples: He rang off before she had a chance to reply.
They agreed the details, then he made to ring off, saying `See you later.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 장기간에 걸쳐 분노와 실망과 같은 부정적인 감정을 보이지 않도록, 이러한 감정이 해로운 방식으로 발달하도록 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop yourself from showing negative emotions like anger and disappointment, especially over a long period, so that these feelings develop in a harmful way
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop yourself from showing negative emotions like anger and disappointment, especially over a long period, so that these feelings develop in a harmful way

But the tears just felt like the most amazing release for all the grief, sadness and pain I'd bottled up for years.

glosses.meaningKo: 부주의한 실수를 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make a careless mistake
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a careless mistake
examples: They start asking questions---what if I slip up, say the wrong thing?
When you’re a politician everyone is always watching in case you slip up.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가에 대해 매우 분노적으로 불평하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to complain very angrily about someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to complain very angrily about someone or something
examples: The decision was changed after he kicked up a fuss.
`That's the most worrying thing, him not wanting to kick up a fuss.

glosses.meaningKo: 아름답거나 인상적이거나 뜻밖이어서 크게 놀라게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to surprise someone by being very beautiful, impressive, unexpected etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to surprise someone by being very beautiful, impressive, unexpected etc
examples: The colorful mural bowled us over.
Her confident performance bowled the judges over.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 청소하거나 고치거나 꾸미다
glosses.englishDescription: to clean, repair, or decorate something
glosses.sourceDescription: to clean, repair, or decorate something
examples: We fixed up the old desk with fresh paint.
They are fixing the spare room up for guests.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신을 강요하거나 다른 사람에게 자리를 떠나거나 일을 중단하도록 강요한다
glosses.englishDescription: to force yourself or someone else to leave or to stop doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to force yourself or someone else to leave or to stop doing something
examples: She was unable to tear her eyes away from him.
‘Sorry,’ said Douglas, tearing himself away from the conversation.

glosses.meaningKo: 음식을 덜어 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to serve food
glosses.sourceDescription: to serve food
examples: Mina dished out soup to everyone at the table.
Dad dished the pasta out into four bowls.

glosses.meaningKo: 음식을 요리에 넣어서 먹을 준비가 되도록 하는 것입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to put food into dishes so that it is ready to be eaten
glosses.sourceDescription: to put food into dishes so that it is ready to be eaten
examples: If this is what she dishes up for starters, we await the rest with relish!
The food's not only inedible but is dished up in large portions.

glosses.meaningKo: 아이디어를 격식 없이 자유롭게 이야기하다
glosses.englishDescription: to discuss ideas in an informal way
glosses.sourceDescription: to discuss ideas in an informal way
examples: We knocked about a few ideas for the poster.
The team knocked several names about before choosing one.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 제안을 받아들이지 않고 거절하다
glosses.englishDescription: to refuse to accept someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to refuse to accept someone or something
examples: The committee knocked back our first garden proposal.
The editor knocked the title back and asked for a new one.

glosses.meaningKo: 일을 마치다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop working
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop working
examples: We knock off at four on Fridays.
The painters knocked off when the school bell rang.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 불행하게 하거나 희망적이지 않게 느끼게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone feel unhappy or less hopeful
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone feel unhappy or less hopeful
examples: Don’t let yourself be dragged down to his level.
If you’re not careful he’ll end up dragging you down with him.

glosses.meaningKo: 필요 없을 때 뭔가 이야기를 시작하기 시작하려면, 보통 과거에 있었던 불쾌한 일이고 다른 사람들이 잊고 싶어 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to start talking about something when it is not necessary, usually something unpleasant that happened in the past and that other people want to forget
glosses.sourceDescription: to start talking about something when it is not necessary, usually something unpleasant that happened in the past and that other people want to forget
examples: Must you drag up that old argument?
There's no need to drag up all that old --- ' `No, I can't say I miss it.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 씻어내기 위해 표면 전체를 씻어냅니다
glosses.englishDescription: to wash the whole surface of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to wash the whole surface of something
examples: They wash down the choppers with a hose, but they can't get rid of the stench.
Use hot water and detergent to wash down kitchen worktops.

glosses.meaningKo: 상대가 말할 때 소리쳐 그 말을 들리지 않게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make it difficult to hear what someone says by shouting while they are speaking
glosses.sourceDescription: to make it difficult to hear what someone says by shouting while they are speaking
examples: The noisy class shouted down the student giving the answer.
Several excited voices shouted the guide down.

glosses.meaningKo: 두 사람이 방 같은 것을 함께 쓰다
glosses.englishDescription: if two people double up, they share something, especially a bedroom
glosses.sourceDescription: if two people double up, they share something, especially a bedroom
examples: The cousins doubled up during their short visit.
We doubled up in the guest room for two nights.

glosses.meaningKo: 문을 잠가 누군가가 방이나 건물에 들어오지 못하게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to prevent someone from coming into a room or building by locking the door
glosses.sourceDescription: to prevent someone from coming into a room or building by locking the door
examples: The automatic door locked us out after closing time.
The caretaker locked visitors out after six o'clock.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 친절하게 대해야 그들이 당신을 도와주거나 지원할 수 있습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to be nice to someone so that they will help or support you
glosses.sourceDescription: to be nice to someone so that they will help or support you
examples: How far do you go to butter up shareholders?
I'm suspicious: is this a cheap trick to butter up a member of Her Majesty's press?

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 그것을 알 수 있도록 무언가를 언급하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to mention something so that people know about it
glosses.sourceDescription: to mention something so that people know about it
examples: Some of them had Post-it notes on the cover to flag up pages of interest.
They’ve already flagged up several problems.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 상황이 특정한 방식으로 전개되면, 그것은 그런 방식으로 전개된다
glosses.englishDescription: if a situation pans out in a particular way, it develops in that way
glosses.sourceDescription: if a situation pans out in a particular way, it develops in that way
examples: And look at it this way, if it doesn't pan out, at least you're a skilled car seat finisher.
Let’s see how things pan out before we decide.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 기운 나게 하거나 스스로 기운을 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to make someone happier, or to become happier
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to make someone happier, or to become happier
examples: The funny card bucked her up after a tiring day.
A sunny walk helped us buck up.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 무겁게 만들고 쉽게 움직일 수 없게 만드는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone heavy and unable to move easily
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone heavy and unable to move easily
examples: The waiters were weighed down by huge trays of food.
They were looking for the odd escudo to weigh down the damp pockets creeping up their thighs.

glosses.meaningKo: 기회를 즉시 활용하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to immediately take advantage of an opportunity
glosses.sourceDescription: to immediately take advantage of an opportunity
examples: By 10 o’clock most of the best bargains had been snapped up.
I’d snap up his offer if I were you.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 수나 양에 도달하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to reach a particular number or amount
glosses.sourceDescription: to reach a particular number or amount
examples: The figures are expected to show that it clocked up a profit for the first three months of the year, after tough trading in December.
This app has already clocked up more than 130,000 downloads since its launch three weeks ago.

glosses.meaningKo: 필요 이상으로 오래 끌다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something last for a long time, usually longer than is good or necessary
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something last for a long time, usually longer than is good or necessary
examples: The host chose to spin out the quiz longer than necessary.
Do not spin the meeting out with repeated questions.

glosses.meaningKo: 생각이나 제안에 동의하여 따르다
glosses.englishDescription: to agree with or go along with an idea or suggestion
glosses.sourceDescription: to agree with or go along with an idea or suggestion
examples: Leo decided to string along with our plan for a picnic.
I decided to string along with the group's suggestion.

glosses.meaningKo: 두 사람이 맞붙으면 서로 경쟁하거나 싸우기 시작할 준비를 한다
glosses.englishDescription: if two people square up, they prepare to start competing or fighting with each other
glosses.sourceDescription: if two people square up, they prepare to start competing or fighting with each other
examples: The teenage pair busted one breathtaking move after another as they squared up in a daring dance-off.
The two old rivals square up for one final confrontation.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 어떤 일에 참여하는 것을 방지하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to prevent someone from taking part in something
glosses.sourceDescription: to prevent someone from taking part in something
examples: He was frozen out of official life.
Sergeant," she said, "is it your intention to freeze out Agent Osborne?

glosses.meaningKo: 매우 피곤해 갑자기 잠들다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly start sleeping, usually when you are very tired
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly start sleeping, usually when you are very tired
examples: I crashed out on the sofa after the long school day.
The twins crashed out soon after the evening story.

glosses.meaningKo: 손가락으로 버터 같은 재료를 밀가루 등에 섞다
glosses.englishDescription: to mix something such as butter or fat into another substance such as flour, using your fingers
glosses.sourceDescription: to mix something such as butter or fat into another substance such as flour, using your fingers
examples: Rub in the butter with your fingertips.
Mina rubbed the butter in until the flour looked crumbly.

glosses.meaningKo: 연필로 쓴 글이나 그림을 지우개로 지우다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove with a rubber something that you have written or drawn in pencil, especially because you have made a mistake
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove with a rubber something that you have written or drawn in pencil, especially because you have made a mistake
examples: Rub out the extra line before you color the picture.
I rubbed my spelling mistake out and tried again.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 보고 갑자기 크게 웃다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly laugh a lot at something
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly laugh a lot at something
examples: Everyone will crack up at the silly drawing.
We cracked up when the puppet bowed to the chair.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신에게 불쾌한 행동을 하거나 말한 사람에게 분노하는 반응을 보이는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to react angrily to someone who has done or said something unpleasant to you
glosses.sourceDescription: to react angrily to someone who has done or said something unpleasant to you
examples: It was his instinct to bite back.
The Big Apple is going to bite back.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것이 중요하거나 사실임을 인정하지 않고 무시하다
glosses.englishDescription: to refuse to accept that something is important or true
glosses.sourceDescription: to refuse to accept that something is important or true
examples: Do not brush aside a useful suggestion too quickly.
The group brushed her concern aside without discussion.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가의 말을 듣지 않거나, 무언가가 진실하거나 중요한 것일 수 있다는 것을 받아들이는 것은 거부한다
glosses.englishDescription: to refuse to listen to someone, or to accept that something might be true or important
glosses.sourceDescription: to refuse to listen to someone, or to accept that something might be true or important
examples: I tried to tell him, but he just brushed me off.
The Foreign Secretary brushed off suggestions that he had considered resigning.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것에 대한 기술이나 지식을 실천하고 향상시키기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to practise and improve your skills or knowledge of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to practise and improve your skills or knowledge of something
examples: And you could do with brushing up your knowledge.
You may just want to brush up your English to help the kids with schoolwork.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가에 대한 진실을 배우거나 이해하거나, 누군가에게 무언가에 대한 진실을 말하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to learn or understand the truth about something, or to tell someone the truth about something
glosses.sourceDescription: to learn or understand the truth about something, or to tell someone the truth about something
examples: I'm just saying that you should wise up to yourself a bit more.
Now when are you going to wise up and turn into an old cynic like me?

glosses.meaningKo: 사업이나 프로젝트를 접다
glosses.englishDescription: to close a business or end a project because it cannot continue
glosses.sourceDescription: same as fold
examples: Chris had known if they lost him they might as well fold up the project.
Two months later the company folded up.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 어떤 것에 동의하게 하거나 그들이 무엇을 할 것인지 말하도록 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone agree to something or tell you what they are going to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone agree to something or tell you what they are going to do
examples: I’ll try to nail Jim down about the date.
They’re on the verge of getting the agreement nailed down.

glosses.meaningKo: 주의를 기울이지 않고 흘려듣다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop paying attention
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop paying attention
examples: It is easy to tune out during a long speech.
She tuned out the noise and focused on her book.

glosses.meaningKo: 음악가들이 한 무리를 이루어 조율하면 악기를 조금씩 바꿔서 함께 잘 연주할 수 있도록 한다
glosses.englishDescription: if a group of musicians tune up, they make small changes to their instruments so that they can play well together
glosses.sourceDescription: if a group of musicians tune up, they make small changes to their instruments so that they can play well together
examples: Bending forward, listening closely, he began to tune up the machine heads.
He was in the next room, tuning up his guitar.

glosses.meaningKo: 토지와 같은 것을 다른 사람 또는 국가 간에, 특히 불공정해 보이는 방식으로 분할하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to divide something such as land between different people or countries, especially in a way that seems unfair
glosses.sourceDescription: to divide something such as land between different people or countries, especially in a way that seems unfair
examples: As they had carved up Poland, they might decide to carve up Europe.
They did not want to see a bunch of foreigners carve up their land.

glosses.meaningKo: 찾기 쉽지 않거나 보기 쉽지 않은 곳에 무언가를 넣기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to put something in a place where it is not easy to find or to see
glosses.sourceDescription: to put something in a place where it is not easy to find or to see
examples: But for now it's safely tucked away in a drawer.
Tucked away in a corner perhaps, but still there.

glosses.meaningKo: 옷자락 등을 다른 부분 아래나 뒤에 넣어 단정하게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to put the end of something such as a piece of clothing under or behind another piece in order to make it tidy
glosses.sourceDescription: to put the end of something such as a piece of clothing under or behind another piece in order to make it tidy
examples: Tuck in your shirt before the concert begins.
Leo tucked in the loose end of his scarf neatly.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람들이 당신을 지지하거나 당신에게서 무언가를 사도록 노력하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to try to make people support you or buy something from you
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to make people support you or buy something from you
examples: Advertisements should help to drum up some business.
We should probably see what sort of a deal we can drum up with one of the mags.

glosses.meaningKo: 많은 수나 양을 얻기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to get a large number or amount of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to get a large number or amount of something
examples: It is possible to rack up quite a bit of mileage without-" She paused, not sure of what she wanted to say, how she wanted to phrase it.
Now he was dispatched, she wanted to rack up some tongue miles.

glosses.meaningKo: 액체가 끓어오르거나 끓어오르면 매우 높은 온도에 도달한 후 사라지고 가스로 변합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a liquid boils away, or if you boil it away, it disappears and turns to gas after reaching a very high temperature
glosses.sourceDescription: if a liquid boils away, or if you boil it away, it disappears and turns to gas after reaching a very high temperature
examples: Allow the liquid to boil away until you are left with tender vegetables and little moisture left in the pan.
Remove lid and boil away liquid, pushing veg to the side.

glosses.meaningKo: 액체가 끓어 용기 밖으로 넘치다
glosses.englishDescription: if a liquid boils over, it rises so much when it boils that it flows over the top of the container that it is in
glosses.sourceDescription: if a liquid boils over, it rises so much when it boils that it flows over the top of the container that it is in
examples: The soup boiled over onto the clean stove.
Turn the heat down before the milk boils over.

glosses.meaningKo: 액체나 액체 속의 것을 끓을 때까지 데우다
glosses.englishDescription: to heat liquid, or to heat something in a liquid, until it boils
glosses.sourceDescription: to heat liquid, or to heat something in a liquid, until it boils
examples: Dad boiled up a pot of vegetable soup.
We boiled some water up for the noodles.

glosses.meaningKo: 그림이나 사진을 벽에 핀으로 붙이다
glosses.englishDescription: to fix a picture to a wall
glosses.sourceDescription: to fix a picture to a wall
examples: We pinned up the class photo beside the calendar.
Please pin this bright poster up on the wall.

glosses.meaningKo: 차곡차곡 쌓다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange things in a pile or piles
glosses.sourceDescription: same as stack
examples: She stacked the dishes up on the draining board.
The books had been stacked up in neat piles.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 씹히면 찢어져 파괴됩니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something gets chewed up, it becomes torn apart and destroyed
glosses.sourceDescription: if something gets chewed up, it becomes torn apart and destroyed
examples: He's like a disruptive puppy chewing up the furniture at school and getting himself into trouble.
My new trousers got chewed up in my bike chain.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 친절하게 대해줌으로써 원하는 일을 할 가능성이 높아지도록 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone more likely to do what you want by being nice to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone more likely to do what you want by being nice to them
examples: His strategy was to soften them up with compliments.
She may soften up if asked nicely.

glosses.meaningKo: 차 한 잔 만들기
glosses.englishDescription: to make a drink of tea
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a drink of tea
examples: At the kettle, I brew up.
They spend most weekends on it, brewing up pots of tea.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 수준이나 수치를 달성하다
glosses.englishDescription: to achieve a particular level or number
glosses.sourceDescription: to achieve a particular level or number
examples: She chalked up ten completed books this month.
Our team chalked up its fifth perfect score.

glosses.meaningKo: 한마디씩 하면서 대화에 동참하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to join a conversation by saying something
glosses.sourceDescription: to join a conversation by saying something
examples: Feel free to chime in if you’ve got something to add.
George couldn’t resist chiming in with his ‘helpful hints’ about investments.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 떠나거나 포기하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to leave or give up something
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave or give up something
examples: He dreamt of chucking it all in (=leaving his job, possessions etc) to sail around the world.
She decided to chuck in her job.

glosses.meaningKo: 갑자기 말하거나 설명을 중단하는 것은 당황하거나 불행하거나 비밀을 지키고 싶기 때문입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly stop talking or explaining something, because you are embarrassed, unhappy, or want to keep a secret
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly stop talking or explaining something, because you are embarrassed, unhappy, or want to keep a secret
examples: He clammed up when I asked him who else was involved.
If there were more than two people in a room he'd clam up.

glosses.meaningKo: 나쁘거나 불법적인 행동을 막기 위해 강하게 단속하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a determined attempt to stop people doing something bad or illegal
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a determined attempt to stop people doing something bad or illegal
examples: The school clamped down on noise in the hallways.
The park clamped down on visitors leaving litter.

glosses.meaningKo: 정부나 기업이 돈을 잃어버린 뒤 돈을 환수하면 다시 돌려받는데, 예를 들어 세금을 더 많이 내거나 더 높은 가격을 청구하는 방식이다
glosses.englishDescription: if a government or company claws back money after losing it, it gets it again, for example by making people pay higher taxes or charging higher prices
glosses.sourceDescription: if a government or company claws back money after losing it, it gets it again, for example by making people pay higher taxes or charging higher prices
examples: How will the money be clawed back?
Some of the money can be clawed back by more efficient purchasing.

glosses.meaningKo: 잠자기 위해서, 특히 갑자기
glosses.englishDescription: to go to sleep, especially suddenly
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to sleep, especially suddenly
examples: If you ask me anything, it's a wonder that the poor old boy didn't conk out a great deal sooner than he did.
She had barely gotten to bed at all last night; there hadn't been more than an hour to conk out and shower before work.

glosses.meaningKo: 저녁은 집에서 대신 식당에서 먹기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to eat dinner in a restaurant instead of at home
glosses.sourceDescription: to eat dinner in a restaurant instead of at home
examples: New York is completely relaxed in terms of dining out.
You may go a month without seeing a film or dining out.

glosses.meaningKo: 오래전에 배우거나 알았던 것을 애써 기억해 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to manage to remember something that you learned or knew long ago
glosses.sourceDescription: to manage to remember something that you learned or knew long ago
examples: I dredged up enough French to read the simple sign.
Mina dredged an old song up from memory.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에 진실하거나 완전한 것이 아닌 답변이나 설명을 하기 위해, 질문하거나 불평하는 것을 멈추게 하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to give someone an answer or explanation that is not true or complete, in order to make them stop asking questions or complaining
glosses.sourceDescription: to give someone an answer or explanation that is not true or complete, in order to make them stop asking questions or complaining
examples: Customers complain they’re being fobbed off with an inferior model.
I’m tired of being fobbed off.

glosses.meaningKo: 오랫동안 논의하거나 논쟁한 후 결정이나 합의에 도달하기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: to reach a decision or agreement after discussing it or arguing about it for a long time

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 조용히 하라고 말할 때 쓰다
glosses.englishDescription: used for telling someone to be quiet
glosses.sourceDescription: used for telling someone to be quiet
examples: Hush up for a moment so we can hear the announcement.
The teacher asked the noisy group to hush up.

glosses.meaningKo: 기계가 갑자기 제대로 작동하지 않게 되다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly stop working correctly
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly stop working correctly
examples: The old fan keeled over during the warm afternoon.
Our printer keeled over before the last page.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 일찍 이 일을 해야 할 때 열심히 일하기 시작하세요

glosses.sourceDescription: to start working hard, especially when you should have done this earlier

glosses.meaningKo: 누가 하라는 대로 하기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: to do what someone tells you to do

glosses.sourceDescription: same as ladle

glosses.meaningKo: 무엇을 이루고 싶은지 뚜렷한 생각을 하지 못한 채 계속 살아오거나 무언가를 하는 것은 말이다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue to live or do something without having a clear idea of what you want to achieve
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue to live or do something without having a clear idea of what you want to achieve

You just muddle along, and if an opportunity comes up, it would be silly not to take it.

glosses.meaningKo: 명확한 계획, 방법, 적절한 장비가 없음에도 불구하고 무언가를 성공시키기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in doing something despite having no clear plan, method, or suitable equipment
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in doing something despite having no clear plan, method, or suitable equipment

glosses.meaningKo: 젖은 옷을 빨랫줄에 집게로 고정해 말리다

glosses.sourceDescription: to fasten wet clothes on a line to dry

glosses.meaningKo: 기분이 좋아지고 활기를 되찾다

glosses.sourceDescription: if someone perks up, or if something perks them up, they begin to feel happier or more lively

glosses.meaningKo: 사업이 더 성공적이 되도록 하기 위해 사업에서 얻은 모든 이익을 다시 재투자하는 것입니다

glosses.sourceDescription: to put any profits made by a business back into it in order to make it more successful

glosses.meaningKo: 다듬어 향상시키다

glosses.sourceDescription: same as polish

glosses.meaningKo: 과거에 일어난 불쾌한 일을 언급하고 다른 사람이 그 일에 대해 이야기하고 싶지 않다는 것을 언급하는 것은 불쾌합니다

glosses.meaningKo: 목록을 빠르고 막힘없이 말하다

glosses.sourceDescription: to say a list of things quickly and without much effort

glosses.meaningKo: 찾을 수 있는 모든 것에서 빨리 무언가를 만들기 위해

glosses.sourceDescription: to make something quickly out of whatever you can find

glosses.sourceDescription: to repair something such as a hole in a piece of cloth by sewing it

glosses.meaningKo: 비싼 걸 사기 위해서

glosses.sourceDescription: if an object comes apart, it separates into pieces, either because it has been made that way or because it is very old or in very bad condition

glosses.englishDescription: in sports, to allow an opponent to win because you make a silly mistake
glosses.sourceDescription: in sports, to allow an opponent to win because you make a silly mistake
examples: We gave away two goals and gave ourselves too much to do.
We gave away two very cheap goals.

glosses.meaningKo: 원래 주인이 가지고 있던 것을 돌려주다
glosses.englishDescription: to give someone something that they owned or had before
glosses.sourceDescription: to give someone something that they owned or had before
examples: Please give back the ruler after the lesson.
Mina gave the borrowed book back on Monday.

glosses.meaningKo: 비밀을 간직하지 않기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to not keep a secret
glosses.sourceDescription: to not keep a secret
examples: She threatened to tell on me.
So it's a draw-I don't tell on him and he doesn't tell on me.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 개발하거나 개선하기 위해 열심히 노력하기
glosses.englishDescription: to try hard to develop or improve something
glosses.sourceDescription: to try hard to develop or improve something
examples: If she works at improving her game, she could be a champion.
Successful relationships don’t just happen – you have to work at them.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 가지나 아이디어를 다른 것에 자연스럽게 넣거나 포함하다
glosses.englishDescription: to add one thing or idea to another, or include one thing or idea in another
glosses.sourceDescription: to add one thing or idea to another, or include one thing or idea in another
examples: Can you work this example in before the ending?
Jina worked a short joke in near the end of her speech.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가의 생각이나 결정을 바꾸도록 설득하려고 애쓰다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to influence someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to influence someone
examples: We will work on Mina until she joins the picnic.
Leo worked on his friends and changed their minds.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 떠나라고 요청하는 것은 일반적으로 전화를 걸거나 메시지를 보내는 것으로,
glosses.englishDescription: to ask someone to leave a place, usually by telephoning them or sending them a message
glosses.sourceDescription: to ask someone to leave a place, usually by telephoning them or sending them a message
examples: He was called away unexpectedly today, which is why I came to meet you instead.
The doctor has been called away to deal with an emergency.

glosses.meaningKo: 다시 전화하거나, 이전에 전화한 사람에게 전화하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to telephone someone again, or to telephone someone who telephoned you earlier
glosses.sourceDescription: to telephone someone again, or to telephone someone who telephoned you earlier
examples: I’ll call back later and see how you are.
I’ll call you back when I’ve heard something.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일이 반드시 이루어져야 한다고 공개적으로 요구하다
glosses.englishDescription: to say publicly that something must happen
glosses.sourceDescription: to say publicly that something must happen
examples: Students called for a longer lunch break.
The committee called for clearer signs in the park.

glosses.meaningKo: 이미 일어나고 있는 일을 멈추기로 결정하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to decide to stop something that is already happening
glosses.sourceDescription: to decide to stop something that is already happening
examples: All right, you win – you can call off the dogs now.
I yelled to the man to call off his dog.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 단체에 어떤 일을 하도록 공식적으로 요청하다
glosses.englishDescription: to officially ask a person or organization to do something
glosses.sourceDescription: to officially ask a person or organization to do something
examples: The teacher called on us to keep the room tidy.
The mayor called on residents to save water.

glosses.meaningKo: 옷이 어떻게 생겼는지, 옷이 맞는지 보기 위해 옷을 입습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to put on a piece of clothing in order to see how it looks and whether it fits
glosses.sourceDescription: to put on a piece of clothing in order to see how it looks and whether it fits
examples: 'No, I meant it was the last dress I would try on in this shop.
What a lovely dress! Why don’t you try it on?

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 기간 동안 생존할 수 있도록 관리합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to manage to stay alive for a particular period of time
glosses.sourceDescription: to manage to stay alive for a particular period of time
examples: It doesn’t look like she’ll last out the night.
When we rang off, I said, `Well, Flora and Evelyn, if we can last out a month or so longer, we should be off the hook with Bas.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 사람에게 정보나 조언을 요청하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to ask several people for information or advice
glosses.sourceDescription: to ask several people for information or advice
examples: I'm 17 and have been asking around for plumbing apprenticeships for a good 4 months now.
It may only be known by those already working in your chosen field, so ask around.

glosses.meaningKo: 원하는 것을 받기 위해 말이나 글로 요청하다
glosses.englishDescription: to speak or write to someone because you want them to give you something
glosses.sourceDescription: to speak or write to someone because you want them to give you something
examples: Please ask the librarian for a new card.
Mina wrote to ask for more information.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 나쁜 짓이나 창피한 짓을 했다는 것을 인정하는 것은
glosses.englishDescription: to admit that you have done something bad or embarrassing
glosses.sourceDescription: to admit that you have done something bad or embarrassing
examples: Dan could have made this whole thing go away simply by owning up.
Two local students later owned up to the prank.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 물건을 챙기지 못하고 두고 오다
glosses.englishDescription: to forget to take someone or something with you
glosses.sourceDescription: to forget to take someone or something with you
examples: I left my umbrella behind on the bus.
Do not leave your lunch box behind again.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가 그만하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to stop doing something
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop doing something
examples: And still he kept seeing, and though there were horrors here, to be sure, nothing in him made him want to leave off his seeing.
I wish he’d leave off moaning about everything!

glosses.meaningKo: 과거로부터 여전히 존재하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to still exist from the past
glosses.sourceDescription: to still exist from the past
examples: There was some ham left over from lunch.
These attitudes are left over from the war.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 일을 하는 데 일정한 시간이나 노력을 들이다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend a particular amount of time doing something, or to make a particular amount of effort in order to do something
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend a particular amount of time doing something, or to make a particular amount of effort in order to do something
examples: She put three hours into the art project.
We put great care into the class garden.

glosses.meaningKo: 전화를 원하는 상대에게 연결해 주다
glosses.englishDescription: if you put a person or call through, you connect someone to the person they want to speak to on the telephone
glosses.sourceDescription: if you put a person or call through, you connect someone to the person they want to speak to on the telephone
examples: The receptionist can put my call through to the office.
Could you put me through to the library desk?

glosses.meaningKo: 계획이나 제안을 단체가 논의하고 결정하도록 내놓다
glosses.englishDescription: to explain a plan or suggestion to a group of people so that they can discuss it and decide whether to accept it or not
glosses.sourceDescription: to explain a plan or suggestion to a group of people so that they can discuss it and decide whether to accept it or not
examples: The chair will put the schedule to the committee.
We put our recycling plan to the class for a vote.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 부품을 결합해 무언가를 만들거나 조립하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something by joining all its parts
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something by joining all its parts
examples: Leo put the model plane together after lunch.
Can you put these puzzle pieces together?

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 피하거나, 다른 사람이 이렇게 하도록 하기 위해서요
glosses.englishDescription: to avoid someone or something, or to make someone else do this
glosses.sourceDescription: to avoid someone or something, or to make someone else do this
examples: I’ve told him to keep away, but he won’t listen.
You can’t keep the kids away from the computer.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 장소, 특히 학교에서의 형벌로 머물게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone stay in a place, especially in school as a punishment
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone stay in a place, especially in school as a punishment
examples: If he takes her to hospital, they might keep her in.
They were kept in after school.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 음식이나 음료를 먹거나 마시지 않다
glosses.englishDescription: to avoid a particular type of food or drink
glosses.sourceDescription: to avoid a particular type of food or drink
examples: The doctor asked me to keep off sugary snacks.
I try to keep off fizzy drinks before bedtime.

glosses.meaningKo: 나쁘거나 불쾌한 일이 약해지거나 멈추다
glosses.englishDescription: if something bad or unpleasant lets up, it slows down or stops
glosses.sourceDescription: if something bad or unpleasant lets up, it slows down or stops
examples: The heavy rain began to let up after noon.
The noise outside should let up before bedtime.

glosses.meaningKo: 의견이 다른 사람과 문제를 충분히 대화해 풀다
glosses.englishDescription: to discuss a problem thoroughly with someone who disagrees with you about it
glosses.sourceDescription: to discuss a problem thoroughly with someone who disagrees with you about it
examples: We sat down and talked the problem out calmly.
Mina and Leo talked out their disagreement after class.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 계획을 논의하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to discuss a problem or a plan
glosses.sourceDescription: to discuss a problem or a plan
examples: Each week we'd go home and talk over how our teaching went.
You both need to talk over what happened that day.

glosses.meaningKo: 실제보다 더 중요하거나 좋아 보이도록 치켜세워 말하다
glosses.englishDescription: to talk about someone or something in a way that makes them seem more important or better than they really are
glosses.sourceDescription: to talk about someone or something in a way that makes them seem more important or better than they really are
examples: Jin talked up the school play to his friends.
The guide talked the small museum up to our group.

glosses.meaningKo: 일이나 절차를 정해진 시간 안에 끝내다
glosses.englishDescription: to complete a piece of work, process, or activity within a particular time
glosses.sourceDescription: to complete a piece of work, process, or activity within a particular time
examples: Our shop can turn the order around in one day.
The team turned the report around before Friday.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 이야기를 하거나, 범죄를 저질렀기 때문에 경찰에 데려가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to tell the police about someone, or to take them to the police, because they have committed a crime
glosses.sourceDescription: to tell the police about someone, or to take them to the police, because they have committed a crime
examples: His own brother turned him in.
She turned herself in to local police.

glosses.meaningKo: 마법으로 다른 것으로 변하거나 바꾸다
glosses.englishDescription: to change into something else as a result of magic
glosses.sourceDescription: to change into something else as a result of magic
examples: In the story, the seed turned into a tiny bird.
The wizard turned the paper boat into a fish.

glosses.meaningKo: 버튼의 누름이나 스위치의 이동에 의해 일시적으로 작동되는 장비의 작동을 정지시킨다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop a piece of equipment working temporarily by pressing a button or by moving a switch
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop a piece of equipment working temporarily by pressing a button or by moving a switch
examples: It is now safe to turn off your computer.
Will you turn the television off, please?

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가, 무언가 등을 가지고 있는 것으로 발견될 수 있도록
glosses.englishDescription: to be discovered to be something, have something etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to be discovered to be something, have something etc
examples: It all turned out to be a mistake.
It turns out that I was right all along.

glosses.meaningKo: 학교 등의 수업이 방학이나 휴식 뒤에 다시 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: if school, university etc starts back, classes begin again after a break
glosses.sourceDescription: if school, university etc starts back, classes begin again after a break
examples: School starts back on Monday after the break.
Our music classes start back next week.

glosses.meaningKo: 지루하거나 짜증나는 방식으로 이야기를 시작하기 시작하는데, 보통 누군가나 무언가를 불평하거나 비난합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to begin talking in a boring or annoying way, usually complaining or criticizing someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin talking in a boring or annoying way, usually complaining or criticizing someone or something
examples: She was waiting for me and started in again.
Then she starts in on the dangers of marriage.

glosses.meaningKo: 처음부터 다시 무언가를 하기 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to begin doing something again from the beginning
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin doing something again from the beginning
examples: I’m getting a little bit too old to start over.
She counted all the envelopes, put them back in the box, then started over.

glosses.meaningKo: 사업이나 단체, 프로젝트를 새로 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to bring a business, organization, or project into existence
glosses.sourceDescription: to bring a business, organization, or project into existence
examples: Mina plans to start up a small craft shop.
They started up a neighborhood book club.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 무언가를 돌려주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give something back to someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to give something back to someone
examples: If you decide that you don't want to keep car, you can hand back the keys before you make the payment.
There, former owners often just hand back the keys and with it their liability.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 정보나 조언 같은 것을 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give something such as information or advice to someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to give something such as information or advice to someone
examples: They won’t hand out your phone number without permission.
Would you hand these papers out for me?

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 처음 한 곳을 인도해서 그 곳의 모든 부분을 볼 수 있도록 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to lead someone around a place for the first time, so that they can see all parts of it
glosses.sourceDescription: to lead someone around a place for the first time, so that they can see all parts of it
examples: I’ll get someone to show you around.
They sent someone to show me around the new offices.

glosses.meaningKo: 간직하고 싶지만 마지못해 남에게 내주다
glosses.englishDescription: to give something to someone although you would prefer to keep it
glosses.sourceDescription: to give something to someone although you would prefer to keep it
examples: I could not part with my favorite storybook.
Leo finally parted with the old toy he had saved.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것에 관한 소식이나 정보를 듣다
glosses.englishDescription: to receive information about something
glosses.sourceDescription: to receive information about something
examples: Did you hear about the new reading club?
We heard about the schedule change this morning.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가로부터 소식을 들으면, 그들은 당신에게 편지를 쓰고, 전화를 걸고, 이메일을 보내는 등
glosses.englishDescription: if you hear from someone, they write to you, phone you, email you etc
glosses.sourceDescription: if you hear from someone, they write to you, phone you, email you etc
examples: Next we’ll hear from a listener in Nottingham.
The police would like to hear from anyone who witnessed the accident.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에 관한 소식을 전해 듣다
glosses.englishDescription: to receive news about someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to receive news about someone
examples: We heard little of Maya while she studied abroad.
I was glad to hear of Jina's success at school.

glosses.meaningKo: 아이들이 다른 사람이나 상황을 흉내 내며 놀다
glosses.englishDescription: if children play at something, they pretend to be someone else or to be involved in a particular type of situation
glosses.sourceDescription: if children play at something, they pretend to be someone else or to be involved in a particular type of situation
examples: The children played at running a little café.
We played at being explorers in the garden.

glosses.meaningKo: 녹음된 메시지나 영화를 재생하여 듣거나 보기 위해 녹음된 메시지를 재생합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to play a message or film that has been recorded in order to listen to or watch it
glosses.sourceDescription: to play a message or film that has been recorded in order to listen to or watch it
examples: Transfer your favourite images to the frame and watch them play back.
Watching it played back on a big screen was quite embarrassing.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제나 어려운 상황을 더 중요하지 않게 보이도록 노력하는 것은 그 것보다 덜 중요해 보인다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to make a problem or difficult situation seem less important than it is
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to make a problem or difficult situation seem less important than it is
examples: At first the government played down the threat to public health.
Our own War Office was fighting to play down the whole issue, didn't want the responsibility.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 가지 일을 하느라 몹시 바쁘게 돌아다니다
glosses.englishDescription: to be very busy doing a lot of different things
glosses.sourceDescription: to be very busy doing a lot of different things
examples: I have been running around all morning doing chores.
Dad ran around all day preparing for the party.

glosses.meaningKo: 진행 또는 발전하거나, 무언가 진행 또는 발전시키기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to progress or develop, or to make something progress or develop
glosses.sourceDescription: to progress or develop, or to make something progress or develop
examples: As the process moved along, I learned that other leaders were being considered for the position.
It’s up to the committee to move the process along.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 곳에서 사는 것을 멈추고 다른 곳에서 살기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to stop living in one place and go to live in another
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop living in one place and go to live in another
examples: Her father had moved away from the area.
She was less keen on moving away from her family, but came round to the idea.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람과 같은 장소에서 살기 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to start living in the same place as someone else
glosses.sourceDescription: to start living in the same place as someone else
examples: He’s moving in with his friends from college.
But then I remembered an experience Alexis and Chris had had when they first sold their separate homes to move in together.

glosses.meaningKo: 집에서 생활하거나 사업을 시작하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to start living or operating a business in a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to start living or operating a business in a place
examples: I moved into the shared house in Clapham in south London two years ago.
In 2013 they moved into a shared house in east London.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 좋은 직책이나 더 높은 단계로 올라가다
glosses.englishDescription: to go to a better job, higher level etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to a better job, higher level etc
examples: Mina moved up to a senior role at the library.
After one year, Leo moved up to the next class level.

glosses.meaningKo: 살아갈 이유나 목표가 있다
glosses.englishDescription: to have a reason to want to stay alive
glosses.sourceDescription: to have a reason to want to stay alive
examples: We all need friends and dreams to live for.
Her garden and family gave her much to live for.

glosses.meaningKo: 생활에 필요한 것을 사며 일정한 금액으로 살아가다
glosses.englishDescription: to have a particular amount of money to buy the things that you need to live
glosses.sourceDescription: to have a particular amount of money to buy the things that you need to live
examples: Rina lives on a small weekly budget.
The student learned to live on twenty dollars a day.

glosses.meaningKo: 남은 삶이나 삶의 일부를 특정 장소나 상황에서 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend the rest or part of your life in a particular place or situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend the rest or part of your life in a particular place or situation
examples: She hopes to live out her later years near the sea.
He lived out the rest of his life in a quiet village.

glosses.meaningKo: 위험하거나 불쾌한 상황을 경험하고 그 후에도 여전히 생존하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to experience a dangerous or unpleasant situation and still be alive after it
glosses.sourceDescription: to experience a dangerous or unpleasant situation and still be alive after it
examples: These are people who have lived through two world wars.
Those who reached 100 this year have lived through two world wars.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 기억이나 생각이 오래 마음에 남다
glosses.englishDescription: if something lives with you, you keep remembering it or thinking about it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something lives with you, you keep remembering it or thinking about it
examples: The memory of our first concert will live with me.
That kind lesson lived with her for many years.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신이 생각하고 있는 것, 느끼는 것을 보여주지 않도록 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to not show what you are thinking or feeling
glosses.sourceDescription: to not show what you are thinking or feeling
examples: It can feel safer to hold back some of your feelings, but now you're ready to show how deep love goes.
It can feel safer to hold back some of your love but it is time to put your whole heart into the relationship.

glosses.meaningKo: 직장을 잃지 않고 계속 유지하다
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in keeping a job
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in keeping a job
examples: Mina has held down the same library job for years.
He works hard to hold down his weekend job.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 믿음이나 기준을 계속 지키다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue having a particular belief or standard
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue having a particular belief or standard
examples: She held to her belief that practice brings progress.
We still hold to the same classroom rule.

glosses.meaningKo: 어디 갈 때 누구나 뭐 가지고 가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to take someone or something with you when you go somewhere
glosses.sourceDescription: to take someone or something with you when you go somewhere
examples: In this sort of environment, those of a nervous disposition may want to bring along some garlic and a crucifix.
They are expected to bring along enough school work to keep themselves busy.

glosses.meaningKo: 생각이나 감정, 기억을 다시 떠올리게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to cause ideas, feelings, or memories to be in your mind again
glosses.sourceDescription: to cause ideas, feelings, or memories to be in your mind again
examples: This song brings back happy school memories.
The old photo brought our first trip back to mind.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 나쁜 일을 일으키려고
glosses.englishDescription: to make something bad happen to someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something bad happen to someone
examples: Elaine had regretted instantly what she had done to bring on his daring flattery.
He accused her of bringing shame and disgrace on the family.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가가 자신이 가진 품질을 보여주도록 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone or something show a quality that they have
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone or something show a quality that they have
examples: A man of late middle age, altogether unremarkable in appearance, was not the stuff to bring out any special response in her.
I hoped I'd be able to bring out the best in her along the way.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 한 장소에서 다른 사람이 있는 곳, 특히 그들의 집으로 데려가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to take someone or something from one place to the place where someone else is, especially their home
glosses.sourceDescription: to take someone or something from one place to the place where someone else is, especially their home
examples: He’s bringing his new girlfriend over to our house tonight.
I’ll bring my holiday photos over when I come.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신에게 무슨 일이 생기면 당신에게 영향을 미치는 사건이나 행동이 일어난다
glosses.englishDescription: if something happens to you, an event or action takes place which affects you
glosses.sourceDescription: if something happens to you, an event or action takes place which affects you
examples: I’d never forgive myself if anything has happened to her because I didn’t go to meet her.
This is the best thing that’s ever happened to me.

glosses.meaningKo: 계약서와 같은 공문서에 특정 특징을 포함하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to include a particular feature in an official document such as a contract
glosses.sourceDescription: to include a particular feature in an official document such as a contract
examples: Measures to protect journalists' sources will also be written into the new law.
Only last week was it finally written into law.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 곳을 떠나거나 출발하다
glosses.englishDescription: to leave
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave
examples: We should head off before the buses get busy.
Mina headed off after saying goodbye.

glosses.meaningKo: 검게 가려서 내용이 보이거나 읽히지 않게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to prevent someone from reading or seeing something by covering it with something dark
glosses.sourceDescription: to prevent someone from reading or seeing something by covering it with something dark
examples: Please black out your address before sharing the form.
The editor will black out the private phone number.

glosses.meaningKo: 필요한 것을 살 돈을 벌어 누군가를 부양하다
glosses.englishDescription: to look after someone by making money in order to buy the things that they need
glosses.sourceDescription: to look after someone by making money in order to buy the things that they need
examples: She works hard to provide for her family.
The new job lets him provide for his children.

glosses.meaningKo: 아무것도 하지 않고 시간을 보내기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to spend time doing nothing
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend time doing nothing
examples: Most of the time we just sit around bored.
No one just sits around wasting time.

glosses.meaningKo: 의자에 편안하게 앉기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a chair
glosses.sourceDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a chair
examples: Please, sit down and make yourselves comfortable.
Why don’t you sit yourself down? We’ll do the washing up.

glosses.meaningKo: 아이를 대신 돌봐 주다
glosses.englishDescription: to babysit
glosses.sourceDescription: to babysit
examples: I will sit for our neighbors on Friday evening.
Mina sits for the Park family after school.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 여러분이 그것을 즐기지 않는다면, 무언가를 끝까지 유지하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to stay until the end of something, especially if you are not enjoying it
glosses.sourceDescription: to stay until the end of something, especially if you are not enjoying it
examples: If I have to sit through one more boring meeting, I think I’ll scream.
You sit through a boring meeting.

glosses.meaningKo: 평소보다 늦게까지 자지 않고 있다
glosses.englishDescription: to go to bed later than usual
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to bed later than usual
examples: We sat up late talking about the school play.
Leo sat up past midnight to finish his model.

glosses.meaningKo: 최종 결과물로 무언가를 갖기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to have something as a final result
glosses.sourceDescription: to have something as a final result
examples: His attempt to persuade the boy ended in failure.
The game ended in a draw.

glosses.meaningKo: 마지막 부분으로 무언가를 갖기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to have something as the final part
glosses.sourceDescription: to have something as the final part
examples: The festival ended with fireworks.
Why did you end your essay with a quotation from Shakespeare?

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가에 대해 특히 용감하거나 단호한 방식으로 반대하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to oppose someone or something, especially in a brave or determined way
glosses.sourceDescription: to oppose someone or something, especially in a brave or determined way
examples: He had stood against her in the party elections of 1977.
We must stand against the evil forces that are threatening our country.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 당신을 지나가게 하기 위해 한쪽으로 이동해야 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to move to one side in order to let someone go past you
glosses.sourceDescription: to move to one side in order to let someone go past you
examples: He stood aside to let me pass.
They quickly stood aside to let me pass.

glosses.meaningKo: 상황에 대한 감정으로부터 영향을 받지 않도록 하여, 상황에 대해 더 명확하게 생각할 수 있도록 한다
glosses.englishDescription: to not let yourself be influenced by your feelings about a situation so that you can think about it more clearly
glosses.sourceDescription: to not let yourself be influenced by your feelings about a situation so that you can think about it more clearly
examples: I forced myself to stand back and assess the situation.
Taking time to stand back and think is a priority.

glosses.meaningKo: 행동해야 할 때 아무 조치도 하지 않고 지켜보다
glosses.englishDescription: to not take action when you should
glosses.sourceDescription: to not take action when you should
examples: Do not stand by while others do all the work.
He stood by even though the plants needed water.

glosses.meaningKo: 앉거나 누운 자세에서 몸을 일으켜 서다
glosses.englishDescription: to put your body into an upright position from a sitting or lying position
glosses.sourceDescription: to put your body into an upright position from a sitting or lying position
examples: Please stand up when your name is called.
Jina stood up and opened the window.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 사기 위해 돈을 주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to give money in order to buy something
glosses.sourceDescription: to give money in order to buy something
examples: Can I pay you for this?
Let me pay for dinner.

glosses.meaningKo: 계좌나 기금, 납입 제도에 돈을 넣다
glosses.englishDescription: to put money into an account, fund, or payment scheme
glosses.sourceDescription: to put money into your bank account
examples: She pays into the employees’ pension scheme.
You can pay cash into any one of our three hundred branches.

glosses.meaningKo: 도로, 거리 등이 만나면 서로 합류하거나 교차한다
glosses.englishDescription: if roads, streets etc meet up, they join or cross each other
glosses.sourceDescription: if roads, streets etc meet up, they join or cross each other
examples: The streets meet up at the next intersection.
The track meets up with the main road ahead.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가와 공식적인 회의를 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to have a formal meeting with someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to have a formal meeting with someone
examples: The principal met with the student council.
Our team will meet with the park manager tomorrow.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 결심하거나 열정적인 방식으로 무언가를 시작하기 시작하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to begin doing something, especially in a determined or enthusiastic way
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin doing something, especially in a determined or enthusiastic way
examples: Donaghue set about resolving the problem of rehousing the victims.
She set about the problem with her usual energy.

glosses.meaningKo: 종이에 무언가를 적어서 잊히지 않고 나중에 볼 수 있도록 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to write something on a piece of paper so that it will not be forgotten and can be looked at later
glosses.sourceDescription: to write something on a piece of paper so that it will not be forgotten and can be looked at later
examples: How many words have I set down on paper or vellum, thinking to trap the truth thereby?
She set all these events down in her diary.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 길거나 힘든 여행을 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start a journey, especially one that is long or difficult
glosses.sourceDescription: to start a journey, especially one that is long or difficult
examples: We set forth at sunrise for the hilltop.
The hikers set forth on a short forest trail.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 실수로 장치 등이 작동하게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to cause something to operate, especially by accident
glosses.sourceDescription: to cause something to operate, especially by accident
examples: Opening the door set off the bell.
The bouncing ball accidentally set the sensor off.

glosses.meaningKo: 텐트를 똑바로 세우거나 어딘가에 쉼터를 만들기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to put a tent in an upright position, or to build a shelter somewhere
