glosses.sourceDescription: to put a tent in an upright position, or to build a shelter somewhere
examples: She set up camp in the kitchen while they painted the bedroom.
We set up camp for the night near the river.

glosses.meaningKo: 바뀐 것이 다시 바뀌면 원래대로 돌아간다
glosses.englishDescription: if something that has changed changes back, it returns to how it was originally
glosses.sourceDescription: if something that has changed changes back, it returns to how it was originally
examples: Do you think things will ever change back to the way they were?
She changed back into her painting clothes.

glosses.meaningKo: 도착하거나 무슨 일이 생겼을 때 뭔가를 볼 수 있도록 주의를 기울이는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to pay attention so that you will see something when it arrives or happens
glosses.sourceDescription: to pay attention so that you will see something when it arrives or happens
examples: Watch for Ryan. He’s here somewhere.
We watched for dolphins jumping on the horizon.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 또는 무언가의 보호, 보호 또는 담당하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to guard, protect, or be in charge of someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to guard, protect, or be in charge of someone or something
examples: I watched over her to make sure she was safe.
I will be watching over you and making sure you make the right choices.

glosses.meaningKo: 스포츠에서 공을 치거나, 차거나, 던진 후 팔이나 다리의 움직임을 계속하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to continue the movement of your arm or leg after you have hit, kicked, or thrown a ball in a sport
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue the movement of your arm or leg after you have hit, kicked, or thrown a ball in a sport
examples: Cattermole slid in and touched the ball, but followed through high on the Croatia player.
The keeper got a faint touch on the ball but followed through on the French winger.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람 또는 단체가 맞붙으면 서로 경쟁하거나 싸우게 된다
glosses.englishDescription: if people or groups face off, they compete or fight with each other
glosses.sourceDescription: if people or groups face off, they compete or fight with each other
examples: Soldiers and protesters faced off during riots.
The teams face off at 3 o’clock.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 가능하다는 것을 보여주기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to show that something is possible
glosses.sourceDescription: to show that something is possible
examples: The evidence allows of no other interpretation.
The possibility must be allowed of concepts which are not concepts of any actual thing, and of names which express a sense but have no denotation.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 양이나 수를 더하여 양이나 수를 더 크게 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make an amount or number greater by adding another amount or number
glosses.sourceDescription: to make an amount or number greater by adding another amount or number
examples: All her many expenses were added to my bill.
The arrival of five more guests only added to the confusion.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 품질이 더 많이 생기기 시작하세요
glosses.englishDescription: to begin to have more of a particular quality
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin to have more of a particular quality
examples: In recent years cycling has grown in popularity.
The area has gradually grown in importance.

glosses.meaningKo: 식물이나 나무가 자라면 발달하여 키가 커지거나 커집니다
glosses.englishDescription: if plants or trees grow, they develop and get larger or taller
glosses.sourceDescription: if plants or trees grow, they develop and get larger or taller
examples: The trees grew almost to the water’s edge.
We left some of the better trees and let them grow to maturity.

glosses.meaningKo: 접힌 것을 펼쳐 전체 모양이 보이게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: if something opens out, or if you open it out, it opens from a folded position so that you can see its shape
glosses.sourceDescription: if something opens out, or if you open it out, it opens from a folded position so that you can see its shape
examples: Mina opened the paper map out on the table.
The folded fan opened out into a wide circle.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 공공장소에서 특정한 방식으로 옷을 입거나 행동하기 위해, 특히 이것이 당신을 바보처럼 보이게 하거나 바보처럼 보이게 할 때
glosses.englishDescription: to dress or behave in public in a particular way, especially when this makes you look or seem silly
glosses.sourceDescription: to dress or behave in public in a particular way, especially when this makes you look or seem silly
examples: I can’t walk around with my hair like this.
You’re not walking around in that hat?

glosses.meaningKo: 장소나 상황, 사람을 떠나다
glosses.englishDescription: to leave a place, situation, or person
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave a place, situation, or person
examples: She smiled, waved, and walked away.
Leo walked away from the noisy game.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신을 필요로 하는 사람이나 상황을 갑자기 떠나다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly leave a person who needs you or a situation that depends on you
glosses.sourceDescription: to suddenly leave a person who needs you or a situation that depends on you
examples: Do not walk out on your team before the project ends.
The lead singer walked out on the group without warning.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 나쁘게 대하고, 그들의 감정에 대한 존중 없이 원하는 일을 하도록 만드는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to treat someone badly and to make them do what you want without respect for their feelings
glosses.sourceDescription: to treat someone badly and to make them do what you want without respect for their feelings
examples: Do you let people walk over you?
I’m not about to let them walk all over me.

glosses.meaningKo: 천천히 연습하거나 누군가에게 차근차근 방법을 보여 주다
glosses.englishDescription: to practise or learn something in a slow patient way, or to show someone how to do something
glosses.sourceDescription: to practise or learn something in a slow patient way, or to show someone how to do something
examples: The coach walked us through the new warm-up.
Could you walk me through this math problem?

glosses.meaningKo: 잃어버린 것을 되찾기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to get back something that you have lost
glosses.sourceDescription: to get back something that you have lost
examples: She admits: 'We know we have to work hard to win back support.
We know we have to work hard to win back their support.

glosses.meaningKo: 수치나 가격 등을 억지로 낮추다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something become lower
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something become lower
examples: Extra supply can force apple prices down.
The new process may force printing costs down.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신에게 오거나 당신에게 배달될 무언가를 준비하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange for something to come to you or be delivered to you
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrange for something to come to you or be delivered to you
examples: I think we should send for a doctor.
In the end we had to send for an ambulance.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 어떤 곳으로 가도록 준비해 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange for someone to go somewhere
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrange for someone to go somewhere
examples: We sent Mina off to summer camp with a warm goodbye.
The coach sent the players off to their next activity.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 목적을 위해 누군가를 어떤 곳으로 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to send someone to a place for a particular purpose
glosses.sourceDescription: to send someone to a place for a particular purpose
examples: The school sent two guides out to welcome families.
The manager sent a helper out to check the signs.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 잘 먹게 해 몸을 더 크고 건강하며 튼튼하게 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone bigger, healthier, and stronger, especially by making them eat more
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone bigger, healthier, and stronger, especially by making them eat more
examples: Nutritious meals helped build the young runner up.
The trainer built her up with rest and healthy food.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가에 접근하지 않도록
glosses.englishDescription: to not approach someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to not approach someone or something
examples: So far, customers have stayed away.
Stay away! Don’t come any closer!

glosses.meaningKo: 먹은 음식이 탈 없이 위에 남아 있다
glosses.englishDescription: if food that you have eaten stays down, it stays in your stomach and you are not sick
glosses.sourceDescription: if food that you have eaten stays down, it stays in your stomach and you are not sick
examples: The toast stayed down after my stomach felt better.
Only the plain rice would stay down that morning.

glosses.meaningKo: 줄어든 체중이 다시 늘지 않고 유지되다
glosses.englishDescription: if weight that you have lost from your body stays off, you do not become heavier again
glosses.sourceDescription: if weight that you have lost from your body stays off, you do not become heavier again
examples: The weight she lost has stayed off for a year.
Daily walks helped those extra pounds stay off.

glosses.meaningKo: 몹시 크게 웃거나 웃음을 참지 못하다
glosses.englishDescription: if you fall about or fall about laughing, you laugh a lot at something
glosses.sourceDescription: if you fall about or fall about laughing, you laugh a lot at something
examples: We all fell about laughing at the silly puppet.
The children fell about when the clown dropped his hat.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 집단이나 범주에 속하거나 그 일부로 분류되다
glosses.englishDescription: to belong to or be classified as part of a particular group or category
glosses.sourceDescription: to refer to a certain group, category, part, etc.
examples: These books fall into three broad groups.
Her questions fall into the beginner category.

glosses.meaningKo: 의견 충돌로 누군가와 사이가 틀어지다
glosses.englishDescription: to stop being friendly with someone because you have had a disagreement with them
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop being friendly with someone because you have had a disagreement with them
examples: Mina and Leo fell out over the team name.
The two friends fell out but soon made up.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 일이나 의무가 누군가의 책임이 되다
glosses.englishDescription: if a particular job or duty falls to someone, it is their responsibility
glosses.sourceDescription: if a particular job or duty falls to someone, it is their responsibility
examples: The final decision will fall to the committee.
The task of greeting guests fell to our class.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 하려는 의도, 또는 무언가가 일어날 것을 기대하는 의도
glosses.englishDescription: to intend to do something, or to expect something to happen
glosses.sourceDescription: to intend to do something, or to expect something to happen
examples: We are planning on going to Australia this year.
We hadn’t planned on so many people coming.

glosses.meaningKo: 절단하여 어떤 것을 통과하는 길을 만드는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make a path through something by cutting
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a path through something by cutting
examples: He cut his way through the jungle with a machete.
She tried to cut through the undergrowth.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 여러 조각으로 자르다
glosses.englishDescription: to cut something into several pieces
glosses.sourceDescription: to cut something into several pieces
examples: Please cut the paper up into four squares.
Mina cut up the fruit for our picnic.

glosses.meaningKo: 도움이나 보호가 필요한 사람을 돌보다
glosses.englishDescription: to do the necessary things for someone who needs help or protection
glosses.sourceDescription: to do the necessary things for someone who needs help or protection
examples: Leo cares for his little brother after school.
Mina cared for her grandmother during the visit.

glosses.meaningKo: 비용을 물건을 사는 사람에게 전가하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone who is buying something from you pay for the cost of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone who is buying something from you pay for the cost of something
examples: The shop passed the delivery cost on to buyers.
The company will not pass the extra fee on to customers.

glosses.meaningKo: 더 좋은 자리에 뽑지 않고 다른 사람을 선택하다
glosses.englishDescription: to not give someone a better job, choosing instead someone who is younger or has less experience
glosses.sourceDescription: to not give someone a better job, choosing instead someone who is younger or has less experience
examples: She was passed over for the team leader role.
Leo felt disappointed when he was passed over for promotion.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 사람의 소유 또는 지배를 멈추고 다른 사람의 소유 또는 지배를 시작하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to stop being owned or controlled by one person and start being owned or controlled by another
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop being owned or controlled by one person and start being owned or controlled by another
examples: The estate has passed from father to son for generations.
Under the will, ownership of the business will pass to my daughter.

glosses.meaningKo: 빨리 싸게 팔기 위해서, 보통 돈이 필요하니까
glosses.englishDescription: to sell something quickly and for a low price, usually because you need money
glosses.sourceDescription: to sell something quickly and for a low price, usually because you need money
examples: Most deans don't try to sell off their Cathedral treasures!
The monk who took me round made it clear that the Order had fallen on hard times, and the brothers needed to sell off what they could.

glosses.meaningKo: 출석했거나 다시 일할 준비가 되었음을 알리러 돌아오다
glosses.englishDescription: to return to a place in order to say that you are present or ready to start working again
glosses.sourceDescription: to return to a place in order to say that you are present or ready to start working again
examples: Please report back to the office after lunch.
The helpers reported back at nine to start work.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 가지 가능한 선택 중에서 누군가 또는 무언가를 선택하기
glosses.englishDescription: to choose someone or something from a number of possible choices
glosses.sourceDescription: to choose someone or something from a number of possible choices
examples: When it came to deciding on a career, I originally wanted to act.
When the time came to decide on a career, he made the obvious choice.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량이나 운전자가 움직이기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls away, they start to move
glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls away, they start to move
examples: The bus pulled away from the stop at noon.
Our train pulled away slowly after the doors closed.

glosses.meaningKo: 나쁜 결과가 예상되는 일을 하지 않기로 물러서다
glosses.englishDescription: to decide not to do something that will probably have bad effects
glosses.sourceDescription: to decide not to do something that will probably have bad effects
examples: The school pulled back from changing the lunch schedule.
Mina pulled back from a plan that seemed too costly.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량이 어떤 곳에 들어와 멈추다
glosses.englishDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls in somewhere, they stop there
glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls in somewhere, they stop there
examples: The bus pulled in beside the library at noon.
Our taxi pulled in near the front gate.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량이 어떤 장소로 들어와 멈추다
glosses.englishDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls into a place, they stop there
glosses.sourceDescription: if a vehicle or driver pulls into a place, they stop there
examples: The train pulled into the station on time.
Our bus pulled into a quiet roadside stop.

glosses.meaningKo: 이전의 상태나 행동 방식으로 돌아가다
glosses.englishDescription: to go back to a previous state or way of behaving
glosses.sourceDescription: to go back to a previous state or way of behaving
examples: After resting, the classroom returned to its usual calm.
The garden returned to normal after the rain.

glosses.meaningKo: 자금이나 자원에 여유를 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make time, money, or another resource available for use
glosses.sourceDescription: same as free
examples: I'm sorry, Donald, but that's the most slack I can free up.
We can probably free up £20,000 for new computer equipment.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 무언가를 원하지 않게 하거나 누군가와 함께하고 싶은 마음을 멈추게 하기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone stop wanting something or stop wanting to be with someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone stop wanting something or stop wanting to be with someone
examples: Increasing prices will only drive customers away.
Promise We will not be driven away by such people.

glosses.meaningKo: 가격이나 수량을 더 높은 수준으로 올리다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a price or amount rise to a higher level
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a price or amount rise to a higher level
examples: High demand drove ticket prices up this week.
Extra packaging can drive shipping costs up.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것의 일부가 나머지에서 떨어져 나가다
glosses.englishDescription: if a part of something breaks away from the rest, it becomes separated from it
glosses.sourceDescription: if a part of something breaks away from the rest, it becomes separated from it
examples: A small piece broke away from the clay model.
One corner of the label broke away easily.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 말을 걸 때 방해하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to interrupt when someone is talking
glosses.sourceDescription: to interrupt when someone is talking
examples: At one's own parties, she pointed out, one was entitled to break in on any conversation.
‘Hilary,’ he broke in gently, ‘I’m just trying to help.’

glosses.meaningKo: 반점 같은 게 생기거나, 반점에 생기거나 하면 피부에 반점이 나타나기 시작합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as spots break out, or if you break out in spots, spots start to appear on your skin
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as spots break out, or if you break out in spots, spots start to appear on your skin
examples: Sweat was beginning to break out on his forehead.
The skin on my arms was breaking out in a rash.

glosses.meaningKo: 회의나 다른 행사가 결렬되거나, 헤어지면 끝이 나고 사람들이 떠나갑니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a meeting or other event breaks up, or if you break it up, it ends and people leave
glosses.sourceDescription: if a meeting or other event breaks up, or if you break it up, it ends and people leave
examples: Sorry to break up the party, but I have to go.
We shall be leaving soon, and we wouldn't want to break up your party for you.

glosses.meaningKo: 군대의 일원이 되기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to become a member of the armed forces
glosses.sourceDescription: to become a member of the armed forces
examples: He joined up right after leaving school.
Since he was a farmer, his was a reserved occupation and he had not been permitted to join up.

glosses.meaningKo: 환경이나 생활 방식이 몸과 마음에 잘 맞다
glosses.englishDescription: if a situation or way of living agrees with you, you enjoy it and feel happy and relaxed
glosses.sourceDescription: if a situation or way of living agrees with you, you enjoy it and feel happy and relaxed
examples: The quiet country air agrees with Mina.
Early morning walks agree with my grandfather.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 물건을 자세히 살펴 원하는 것을 고르다
glosses.englishDescription: to examine a collection of things carefully so that you can decide which ones you want
glosses.sourceDescription: to examine a collection of things carefully so that you can decide which ones you want
examples: We picked over the apples and chose the firm ones.
Mina carefully picked over the buttons for her craft.

glosses.meaningKo: 많이 쓰거나 문질러서 사라지거나, 아니면 사라지게 하기 위해서요
glosses.englishDescription: to disappear, or to make something disappear, because it has been used or rubbed a lot
glosses.sourceDescription: to disappear, or to make something disappear, because it has been used or rubbed a lot
examples: The grass has been worn away by cars.
The inscription on the ring had almost worn away.

glosses.meaningKo: 우연히 생각해 내거나 찾아내다
glosses.englishDescription: to suddenly think of or discover an idea or answer
glosses.sourceDescription: same as hit on
examples: I think he’s hit upon the crucial question.
She hit upon a clever scheme.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 불쾌하게 하거나 불쾌한 일을 경험하게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone do something or experience something that is unpleasant
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone do something or experience something that is unpleasant
examples: Come on, hit me with it – what happened?
They may decide to hit him with a lawsuit.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 아이디어나 사실을 사용하여 결정을 내리거나 계산하거나 이론을 개발하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to use particular ideas or facts to make a decision, do a calculation, or develop a theory
glosses.sourceDescription: to use particular ideas or facts to make a decision, do a calculation, or develop a theory
examples: Prices are based on two people sharing a room.
The prosecution’s case is based largely on evidence from ex-members of the gang.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 점차 파괴하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to gradually destroy something
glosses.sourceDescription: to gradually destroy something
examples: After nearly three years of exhaustion and emotional numbness, I decide to confront the thing eating away at me and the family.
That sort of thing eats away at your belief.

glosses.meaningKo: 다시 전화하거나, 당신이 자리를 비웠을 때, 혹은 너무 바쁠 때 전화를 걸었던 사람에게 전화를 걸어 전화하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to phone someone again, or to phone someone who phoned you earlier when you were away or were too busy to speak to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to phone someone again, or to phone someone who phoned you earlier when you were away or were too busy to speak to them
examples: I’ve got someone at the door. I’ll phone you back.
She’s not in at the moment. Can you phone back later?

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 사람 또는 회사에 전화를 걸어 무언가를 준비하거나 정보를 얻습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to phone several people or companies in order to arrange something or to get information
glosses.sourceDescription: to phone several people or companies in order to arrange something or to get information
examples: I knew I could get a better deal if I phoned round a bit.
It’s normal for companies to phone round their big customers and try to persuade them to invest.

glosses.meaningKo: 그들이 없거나 아픈 동안 누군가의 일을 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to do someone’s work while they are away or ill
glosses.sourceDescription: to do someone’s work while they are away or ill
examples: If Pauline asks where I am, will you cover for me?
I’m just covering for Mrs Tyler, so please bear with me.

glosses.meaningKo: 장소를 빠르고 자주 영구적으로 떠나기
glosses.englishDescription: to leave a place quickly and often permanently
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave a place quickly and often permanently
examples: I sometimes feel like clearing out of here altogether.
Just clear out!

glosses.meaningKo: 비행기나 배를 타고 어떤 곳에 도착하다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive at a place by plane or boat
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive at a place by plane or boat
examples: We landed in Jeju after a short flight.
The travelers landed in Busan by ferry.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 고려하기 위해 잠시 멈추는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to stop for a moment in order to consider something
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop for a moment in order to consider something
examples: Step back and think this all through.
This is the moment to step back and think for a while.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 장소에서 멀어지기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to move away from a person or place
glosses.sourceDescription: to move away from a person or place
examples: Ann suddenly drew away from me.
People started waving as the train drew away.

glosses.meaningKo: 커튼 같은 것을 당겨 열린 상태로 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to pull something such as a curtain into an open position
glosses.sourceDescription: to pull something such as a curtain into an open position
examples: Mina drew back the curtains to let in sunlight.
He drew the curtain back and looked outside.

glosses.meaningKo: 차량 등이 어떤 장소에 도착하다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrive in a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrive in a place
examples: The train drew into the station just before noon.
Our bus drew into the terminal a few minutes early.

glosses.meaningKo: 특별한 주의를 위해 그룹에서 한 사람을 선택합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to choose one person from a group for special attention
glosses.sourceDescription: to choose one person from a group for special attention
examples: Katie was often singled out for punishment.
Who would you single out as the most promising student of the year?

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 사물 사이의 거리나 차이를 좁히다
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce the distance or difference between people or things
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce the distance or difference between people or things
examples: Our runner closed on the leader during the final lap.
The blue boat slowly closed on the red one.

glosses.meaningKo: 짧은 시간 동안 또는 영구적으로 활동을 중단하거나 사업을 중단하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to stop an activity or close a business, either for a short time or permanently
glosses.sourceDescription: to stop an activity or close a business, either for a short time or permanently
examples: All the shops had closed up for the night.
As the storm approached, everyone began closing up their businesses.

glosses.meaningKo: 메시지나 지시를 빠르게 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to quickly send a message or give instructions
glosses.sourceDescription: to quickly send a message or give instructions
examples: Mina fired off a quick email to the office.
The coach fired off three short instructions.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 더미로 만들기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make something into a pile
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something into a pile
examples: Before going to bed, she banked up the fire.
Soil was banked up against the wall.

glosses.meaningKo: 결정이나 책임이 누군가에게 있는 경우, 그들은 그 결정이나 책임을 져야 할 의무나 권한을 갖는다
glosses.englishDescription: if a decision or responsibility rests with someone, they have the duty or authority to take that decision or responsibility
glosses.sourceDescription: if a decision or responsibility rests with someone, they have the duty or authority to take that decision or responsibility
examples: Responsibility for child care rests with social services.
The matter now rests with the medical committee.

glosses.meaningKo: 예를 들어 더 이상 원하지 않는 것을 제거하기 위해 먼지통에 넣어 제거합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to get rid of something that you no longer want, for example by putting it in a dustbin
glosses.sourceDescription: to get rid of something that you no longer want, for example by putting it in a dustbin
examples: Don't throw away anything else until told to.
Throw away anything you no longer need or haven't used in a couple of years.

glosses.meaningKo: 침대에서 일어나기 전에 이불을 재빨리 젖히다
glosses.englishDescription: to push the covers on a bed away from you quickly, for example before you get out of bed
glosses.sourceDescription: to push the covers on a bed away from you quickly, for example before you get out of bed
examples: Jina threw back the covers and sat up.
Leo threw the blanket back before getting out of bed.

glosses.meaningKo: 원하는 수준 또는 필요한 수준으로 높이기 위해 무언가에 더 추가하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to add more to something in order to increase it to the level that you want or need
glosses.sourceDescription: to add more to something in order to increase it to the level that you want or need
examples: Can I top you up?
Would you like me to top up your drink?

glosses.meaningKo: 누우거나, 다른 사람을 침대나 다른 장소에 넣어 잠을 자게 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to lie down, or to put someone else into a bed or another place to sleep
glosses.sourceDescription: to lie down, or to put someone else into a bed or another place to sleep
examples: Extra guests can bed down in neighbouring barns that sleep up to six.
John and Steve can bed down in the living room.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 채우거나 채워주면 더 이상 배고픔을 느끼지 않도록 음식을 충분히 먹는다
glosses.englishDescription: if you fill someone up, or if they fill up, they eat enough food so that they no longer feel hungry
glosses.sourceDescription: if you fill someone up, or if they fill up, they eat enough food so that they no longer feel hungry
examples: Fill up on lots of vegetables and salads.
If you’re hungry, fill up on pasta or rice.

glosses.meaningKo: 지면이 갑자기 아래로 낮아지다
glosses.englishDescription: if the ground drops away, it slopes steeply downwards
glosses.sourceDescription: same as drop
examples: As we round the first rock face and the ground drops away to the pass far below, adrenalin surges into my veins.
Then, without warning, the ground drops away and your jaw drops with it.

glosses.meaningKo: 뒤로 처지다
glosses.englishDescription: to move back into a position behind other people
glosses.sourceDescription: same as drop
examples: Alex dropped back to let me pass.
He dropped back and finished in sixth place.

glosses.meaningKo: 뒤처지다
glosses.englishDescription: to move more slowly and end up behind other people
glosses.sourceDescription: same as drop back
examples: Jensen has dropped behind into last place.
Mary dropped behind to walk with Sam.

glosses.meaningKo: 활동이나 학교 등을 마치기 전에 그만두다
glosses.englishDescription: to leave something such as an activity, school, or competition before you have finished what you intended to do
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave something such as an activity, school, or competition before you have finished what you intended to do
examples: Mina dropped out of the club before the term ended.
The student dropped out of the art course in May.

glosses.meaningKo: 반대나 어려움에도 불구하고 무언가를 성취하기 위해 계속 노력하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to continue trying to achieve something despite opposition or difficulties
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue trying to achieve something despite opposition or difficulties
examples: Government pushes ahead with plan.
He wants to push ahead with his reform agenda.

glosses.meaningKo: 불쾌하거나 걱정되는 일을 생각하지 않으려 밀어 두다
glosses.englishDescription: to refuse to think about something unpleasant
glosses.sourceDescription: to refuse to think about something unpleasant
examples: She pushed aside her worries and started the presentation.
Leo pushed his doubts aside and tried again.

glosses.meaningKo: 예정된 일을 더 늦은 시간으로 미루다
glosses.englishDescription: to arrange a later time for something
glosses.sourceDescription: to arrange a later time for something
examples: We pushed the meeting back to Friday afternoon.
The school pushed back the concert by one week.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 얻거나 성취하기 위해 열심히 노력하기
glosses.englishDescription: to try hard to get or achieve something
glosses.sourceDescription: to try hard to get or achieve something
examples: He’s pushing us for a decision by tomorrow.
We are pushing for a ban on nuclear testing.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 장소를 향해 더 나아가기 위해, 혹은 반대나 어려움에도 불구하고, 정해진 방식으로, 또는 반대나 어려움에도 불구하고
glosses.englishDescription: to move further towards a place in a determined way, or in spite of opposition or difficulties
glosses.sourceDescription: to move further towards a place in a determined way, or in spite of opposition or difficulties
examples: John pushed forward into the dark entrance of the cave.
They were urged to push forward with their reforms.

glosses.meaningKo: 먼저 기다린 사람들 앞에 부당하게 끼어들다
glosses.englishDescription: to stand in front of people who have been waiting longer than you, in a way that is unfair
glosses.sourceDescription: to stand in front of people who have been waiting longer than you, in a way that is unfair
examples: Please do not push in while others are waiting.
A boy tried to push in at the lunch line.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 세게 밀어서 자신이 있는 위치에서 떨어지게 하는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to push someone or something hard so that they fall from the position that they are in
glosses.sourceDescription: to push someone or something hard so that they fall from the position that they are in
examples: He pushed over the lamp.
She pushed me over in the playground.

glosses.meaningKo: 많은 사람들이 반대하지만 법을 통과시키고 합의 등을 빨리 받아들이는 데 성공하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in getting a law, agreement etc accepted quickly although a lot of people oppose it
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in getting a law, agreement etc accepted quickly although a lot of people oppose it
examples: He had been instrumental in pushing through the law.
He helped push through the law.

glosses.meaningKo: 부수거나 으깨서 다른 형태로 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something change into a different form by damaging it or crushing it
glosses.sourceDescription: to make something change into a different form by damaging it or crushing it
examples: We reduced the crackers to crumbs for the recipe.
The blender reduced the oats to a fine powder.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 이야기함으로써 누군가의 의견, 아이디어, 느낌 등을 알아내려고 노력한다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to find out someone’s opinions, ideas, feelings etc by talking to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to find out someone’s opinions, ideas, feelings etc by talking to them
examples: When you come back from your honeymoon, Fred, I'd like you to sound out your men in St Padarn's about the idea of a men's organization.
Without knowing it, the Ambassador's wife had zeroed in on the very man Control was anxious to sound out after dinner.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 원하는 방식으로, 특히 화가 나게 함으로써 무언가에 반응하도록 한다
glosses.englishDescription: to react to something in the way that someone wants you to, especially by becoming angry
glosses.sourceDescription: to react to something in the way that someone wants you to, especially by becoming angry
examples: He’s just trying to provoke you. Don’t rise to it.
I was too tired to rise to the bait so I said nothing.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 사용하지 않기 위해, 또는 덜 사용하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to avoid using something, or to use less of it
glosses.sourceDescription: to avoid using something, or to use less of it
examples: Keep your showers short to save on water.
Using eco-friendly light bulbs will help you save on electricity bills.

glosses.meaningKo: 돈을 모으다
glosses.englishDescription: to keep money over time so that you can use it later
glosses.sourceDescription: same as save
examples: I’m saving up for a new car.
She spent all the money I had saved up for our trip.

glosses.meaningKo: 제자리에 두지 않고 아무 데나 놓여 있다
glosses.englishDescription: to have been left somewhere instead of being put in the correct place
glosses.sourceDescription: to have been left somewhere instead of being put in the correct place
examples: Art supplies were lying around the classroom after lunch.
Please put away the books lying around your room.

glosses.meaningKo: 앉은 자세에서 평평하게 누운 자세로 이동하기 위해, 표면에 평평하게 누운 자세
glosses.englishDescription: to move from a sitting position into a position in which you are lying flat on a surface
glosses.sourceDescription: to move from a sitting position into a position in which you are lying flat on a surface
examples: Lie back and relax for thirty minutes.
The doctor asked me to lie back on the couch.

glosses.meaningKo: 결정이나 조치의 진정한 이유가 되기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to be the real reason for a decision or action
glosses.sourceDescription: to be the real reason for a decision or action
examples: But more profound reasons lie behind the need for lying in the initial stages of courtship.
There can be all sorts of reasons lying behind favouritism.

glosses.meaningKo: 책임이나 비난, 권한, 결정권이 누군가에게 있다
glosses.englishDescription: if responsibility, blame, power, or a decision lies with someone, they have that responsibility or authority
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as responsibility or blame for something lies with someone, they are responsible for it or they should be blamed for it
examples: There is evidence to suggest that some blame lies with the police.
Unfortunately, the decision doesn’t lie with our department.

glosses.meaningKo: 생각이나 생각이 생기면 갑자기 예상치 못한 생각이 들기 시작한다
glosses.englishDescription: if a thought or idea occurs to you, you suddenly and unexpectedly start to think about it
glosses.sourceDescription: if a thought or idea occurs to you, you suddenly and unexpectedly start to think about it
examples: It didn’t occur to her to ask how he’d found her.
It suddenly occurred to her that Joe was afraid of being alone.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건이나 차량을 빌렸다는 표시로 공식 명단에 이름을 쓰다
glosses.englishDescription: if you sign out an object or a vehicle, you write your name on an official list to show that you have borrowed or hired it
glosses.sourceDescription: if you sign out an object or a vehicle, you write your name on an official list to show that you have borrowed or hired it
examples: Please sign out the tablet before taking it home.
Mina signed the camera out at the front desk.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가에 대한 책임을 지는 것에 동의하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to agree to be responsible for something
glosses.sourceDescription: to agree to be responsible for something
examples: He will have to answer for the detailed handling of the operation.
You have to answer for any problems that happen during the show.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람의 감정을 이해하고 공감하다
glosses.englishDescription: to feel that you can understand and share someone else’s feelings
glosses.sourceDescription: to feel that you can understand and share someone else’s feelings
examples: Young readers identify with the shy hero in this book.
Mina identified with the character who felt left out.

glosses.meaningKo: 다 썼거나 나중에 쓰려고 물건을 한쪽에 내려놓다
glosses.englishDescription: to put something down and to one side because you have finished with it or want to save it until another time
glosses.sourceDescription: to put something down and to one side because you have finished with it or want to save it until another time
examples: Mina laid the book aside when dinner was ready.
He laid aside the puzzle until the next morning.

glosses.meaningKo: 문제에 대한 결과, 결정 또는 해결책에 도달하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to reach a result, decision, or solution to a problem
glosses.sourceDescription: to reach a result, decision, or solution to a problem
examples: How did they arrive at that figure?
The two studies arrive at very different conclusions.

glosses.meaningKo: 정보나 조언이나 지시를 받았기 때문에 무언가를 하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to do something because you have been given information, advice, or orders
glosses.sourceDescription: to do something because you have been given information, advice, or orders
examples: I’m acting on the advice of my lawyers.
They were acting on the instructions of senior managers.

glosses.meaningKo: 몸의 일부가 아프거나 장비가 말썽을 일으키기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: if a part of your body or a piece of equipment acts up, it starts to become painful or to develop problems
glosses.sourceDescription: if a part of your body or a piece of equipment acts up, it starts to become painful or to develop problems
examples: The classroom printer may act up on very humid days.
My old tablet acted up during the lesson.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 보고 그들이 안전하고 만족스럽다고 확신하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to look at someone or something so that you are certain they are safe, satisfactory etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to look at someone or something so that you are certain they are safe, satisfactory etc
examples: I sent Michael to check on the kids.
The boss arrived to check on our progress.

glosses.meaningKo: 꼼꼼히 점검하다
glosses.englishDescription: to examine someone or something carefully to find any problems
glosses.sourceDescription: same as check
examples: All written work should be checked over for spelling mistakes.
The nurse began checking him over.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려움이나 두려움을 대수롭지 않게 여기다
glosses.englishDescription: to behave in a way that shows you are not worried or frightened by something
glosses.sourceDescription: to behave in a way that shows you are not worried or frightened by something
examples: Mina laughed at the challenge and tried again.
We learned to laugh at small setbacks instead of worrying.

glosses.meaningKo: 대기하거나 아무것도 하지 않는 곳에서 시간을 보내기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to spend time in a place waiting or doing nothing
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend time in a place waiting or doing nothing
examples: I hung around outside, waiting for the others.
Let’s not hang around or we’ll be late!

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가가 당신에게 걸려 있으면, 당신은 그것에 대해 걱정하거나 화를 냅니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something hangs over you, you worry about it or feel upset about it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something hangs over you, you worry about it or feel upset about it
examples: A sense of doom hung over the town.
The threat of homelessness hangs over hundreds of families.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정 장소, 가족 또는 상황에서 오는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to come from a particular place, family, or situation
glosses.sourceDescription: to come from a particular place, family, or situation
examples: Hugh’s interest in languages sprang from his upbringing in Spain.
Is that Ricky? Where did he spring from?

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 더 강하게 하거나 더 확실하게 정하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make something stronger or more definite
glosses.sourceDescription: to give someone or something what they need in order to be stronger
examples: Negotiators will meet later this week to firm up the deal.
They’ve agreed to firm up their peacekeeping force.

glosses.meaningKo: 남은 것을 마저 끝내다
glosses.englishDescription: to complete the last part of something or consume what remains
glosses.sourceDescription: same as finish
examples: Do you want to finish off these sandwiches?
I just need to finish off a few things first.

glosses.meaningKo: 회사 조직 방식을 바꾸어 더 효율적이거나 성공적으로 만들다
glosses.englishDescription: to make changes in the way that a company is organized so that it is more effective or successful
glosses.sourceDescription: to make changes in the way that a company is organized so that it is more effective or successful
examples: The director plans to shake up how the company is organized.
A new manager shook up the office to make it more efficient.

glosses.meaningKo: 비행기를 타고 어떤 곳으로 가다
glosses.englishDescription: to travel by plane
glosses.sourceDescription: to travel by plane
examples: We flew into Seoul on an early morning flight.
Mina will fly into Jeju before the holiday.

glosses.meaningKo: 그물이나 낚싯대 등으로 물고기를 잡으려 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to catch fish, for example using a net or a fishing rod
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to catch fish, for example using a net or a fishing rod
examples: The children fished for minnows with small nets.
We fish for trout at the lake each summer.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 나쁜 일이 일어날 수도 있고, 누군가에게 일어난 일이 있을 수도 있다고 생각하기 때문에 누군가나 무언가에 대해 걱정하게 되는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to feel worried about someone or something because you think something bad may happen to them or has happened to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to feel worried about someone or something because you think something bad may happen to them or has happened to them
examples: Hundreds of innocent civilians fear for their lives.
I fear greatly for their safety.

glosses.meaningKo: 새로운 아이디어나 계획, 특히 어리석거나 특이한 것을 떠올리는 것은 매우 중요한 일이다
glosses.englishDescription: to think of a new idea or plan, especially one that is silly or unusual
glosses.sourceDescription: to think of a new idea or plan, especially one that is silly or unusual
examples: Before the end, the leaders dreamed up more and more fantastical punishments for those who exhibited doubts.
He was continually dreaming up schemes to expand his business.

glosses.meaningKo: 경쟁자를 이기고 원하는 것을 얻는 데 성공하다
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in winning or gaining something from an opponent
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in winning or gaining something from an opponent
examples: The bakery managed to beat off local competition and win the award.
Our class could beat off three rivals in the science quiz.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 사람도 원하는 것을 경쟁에서 이겨 차지하다
glosses.englishDescription: to succeed in winning or gaining something that someone else wants
glosses.sourceDescription: to succeed in winning or gaining something that someone else wants
examples: Mina beat out twenty applicants for the school role.
Our poster managed to beat out five others for first place.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 원하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to want something
glosses.sourceDescription: to want something
examples: He could not have wished for a more pleasant holiday.
You couldn’t wish for a better friend.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것에 관한 것이거나 그것과 관련되다
glosses.englishDescription: to be about something, or to be connected with something
glosses.sourceDescription: to be about something, or to be connected with something
examples: This chapter relates to life in the ocean.
The new rule relates to borrowing library books.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 성과가 누군가의 공이라고 말하거나 믿다
glosses.englishDescription: to say or believe that someone is responsible for a particular achievement
glosses.sourceDescription: to say or believe that someone is responsible for a particular achievement
examples: Teachers credit Mina with improving the school garden.
We credit Leo with creating the winning design.

glosses.meaningKo: 손이나 발, 스포츠 도구로 공 등을 치거나 차려고 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to hit or kick something such as a ball with your hand, foot, or a piece of sports equipment
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to hit or kick something such as a ball with your hand, foot, or a piece of sports equipment
examples: Mina struck at the ball with her tennis racket.
Leo struck at the practice ball but missed.

glosses.meaningKo: 뜻밖에 또는 우연히 무언가를 찾아내거나 생각해 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to find or think of something suddenly, unexpectedly, or by accident
glosses.sourceDescription: to find or think of something suddenly, unexpectedly, or by accident
examples: Mina struck on a clever solution during lunch.
We struck on the answer while checking the diagram.

glosses.meaningKo: 음악 한 곡이 틀어지면 누군가 그것을 연주하기 시작합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if a piece of music strikes up, someone starts playing it
glosses.sourceDescription: if a piece of music strikes up, someone starts playing it
examples: The announcer called out, ‘Strike up the band!’
The musicians struck up and people began to dance.

glosses.meaningKo: 항공기나 우주선이 착륙하다
glosses.englishDescription: if an aircraft or space vehicle touches down, it lands
glosses.sourceDescription: if an aircraft or space vehicle touches down, it lands
examples: Our plane touched down just before sunset.
The small aircraft touched down on the island runway.

glosses.meaningKo: 상점, 레스토랑 등에서 손님을 모시기
glosses.englishDescription: to serve a customer in a shop, restaurant etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to serve a customer in a shop, restaurant etc
examples: Are you being attended to?
Please take a seat and I’ll ask someone to attend to you.

glosses.meaningKo: 일정한 시간을 잠을 자며 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: to spend a period of time in sleeping
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend a period of time in sleeping
examples: Leo slept away most of the rainy afternoon.
The tired puppy slept the morning away by the window.

glosses.meaningKo: 휴식하고 생각할 시간을 더 가진 다음 날까지 결정을 내리기 위해 기다리는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to wait to make a decision until the next day, after you have rested and had more time to think
glosses.sourceDescription: to wait to make a decision until the next day, after you have rested and had more time to think
examples: I will have to sleep on it and see where we are.
Let me sleep on it and give you an answer tomorrow.

glosses.meaningKo: 어려움, 반대 또는 중단에도 불구하고, 어떤 일을 결심한 방식으로 계속 수행하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to continue doing something in a determined way, despite difficulties, opposition, or interruptions
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue doing something in a determined way, despite difficulties, opposition, or interruptions
examples: They pressed ahead regardless of objections.
We shall press ahead with our plans for reform.

glosses.meaningKo: 한 무리의 사람들이 앞으로 나아가며 일렬로 퍼지다
glosses.englishDescription: if a group of people fan out, they move forwards and apart in a straight line
glosses.sourceDescription: if a group of people fan out, they move forwards and apart in a straight line
examples: The students fanned out across the field to collect litter.
Our helpers fanned out along the path to place signs.

glosses.meaningKo: 특히 무슨 일이 일어나기를 기다리기 위해 원래 의도했던 것보다 더 오래 장소에 남아 있어야 합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to remain in a place for longer than you originally intended, especially in order to wait for something to happen
glosses.sourceDescription: to remain in a place for longer than you originally intended, especially in order to wait for something to happen
examples: Lee challenged her to a demonstration but she said it was too early for that and he'd better stick around.
Well, yes, she saw me and I saw her, but she didn't stick around.

glosses.meaningKo: 위쪽으로 무언가를 올리기 위해서, 특히 팔이나 손을 올리려면
glosses.englishDescription: to raise something upwards, especially your arm or hand
glosses.sourceDescription: to raise something upwards, especially your arm or hand
examples: Maggie stuck up her hand to answer the question.
You’ve got a bit of hair sticking up at the back.

glosses.meaningKo: 얼음으로 덮이기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to become covered with ice
glosses.sourceDescription: to become covered with ice
examples: Drivers faced a new danger as roads iced over when floodwater froze.
The pond was iced over for most of the winter.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가의 건강이나 행복, 성공을 빌며 잔을 들어 마시다
glosses.englishDescription: to wish for health, happiness, or success for someone or something, then lift your glass and drink from it
glosses.sourceDescription: to wish for health, happiness, or success for someone or something, then lift your glass and drink from it
examples: Let us drink to her success with apple juice.
We gathered to drink to the new school year.

glosses.meaningKo: 음료를 다 마시기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to drink all of your drink
glosses.sourceDescription: to drink all of your drink
examples: Drink up, everyone, it’s time to go.
I gave the cat some milk and she drank it all up.

glosses.meaningKo: 소매나 바짓단을 여러 번 접어 짧게 올리다
glosses.englishDescription: if you roll your sleeves or the legs of your trousers up, you fold the cloth several times until they are shorter
glosses.sourceDescription: if you roll your sleeves or the legs of your trousers up, you fold the cloth several times until they are shorter
examples: Mina rolled up her sleeves before washing the brushes.
Leo rolled his trouser legs up to cross the shallow stream.

glosses.meaningKo: 혼자 있고 싶어 아무도 못 찾는 곳에 가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to go to a place where no one can find you because you want to be alone
glosses.sourceDescription: to go to a place where no one can find you because you want to be alone
examples: Kate’s experiences would have made most people want to hide away.
When he gets depressed, he hides himself away and we never see him.

glosses.meaningKo: 여럿이 돈을 조금씩 모아 함께 물건을 사다
glosses.englishDescription: if people club together, each of them gives some money so that all the money collected can be used to buy something
glosses.sourceDescription: if people club together, each of them gives some money so that all the money collected can be used to buy something
examples: We clubbed together to buy our teacher a plant.
The neighbors decided to club together for a new park bench.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 그룹보다 강하거나 더 성공하여 실패하거나 더 이상 당신과 경쟁할 수 없도록 하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to become stronger or more successful than another group so that they fail or can no longer compete with you
glosses.sourceDescription: to become stronger or more successful than another group so that they fail or can no longer compete with you
examples: The old inhabitants are being crowded out by rich young professionals.
Traditional industries were crowded out with the growth of mass tourism.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 이루기 위해 한데 뭉치다
glosses.englishDescription: to come together as a group in order to achieve something
glosses.sourceDescription: to come together as a group in order to achieve something
examples: The students banded together to clean the school garden.
Local families banded together to open a reading room.

glosses.meaningKo: 옷이 몸 위쪽으로 점차 말려 올라가다
glosses.englishDescription: if a piece of clothing rides up, it gradually moves upwards on your body
glosses.sourceDescription: if a piece of clothing rides up, it gradually moves upwards on your body
examples: Her coat can ride up when she reaches for the shelf.
This shirt tends to ride up when I stretch.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 일어나지 않도록 하기 위해 노력합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to try to prevent something from happening
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to prevent something from happening
examples: The element of surprise is difficult to guard against.
We need to guard against the possibility of people losing interest.

glosses.meaningKo: 막아 버리다
glosses.englishDescription: to fill or cover an opening so that nothing can pass through
glosses.sourceDescription: same as block
examples: One end had been blocked up with piled stones.
We had continual problems with leaves blocking up the gutters.

glosses.meaningKo: 오래 머물기 때문에 편안한 곳에서 지내기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a place because you are going to stay there for a long time
glosses.sourceDescription: to make yourself comfortable in a place because you are going to stay there for a long time
examples: How are you settling into your new home?
We settled into our tent.

glosses.meaningKo: 각 개인 또는 그룹이 얼마를 지불해야 하는지 동의하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to agree how much each person or group should pay
glosses.sourceDescription: to agree how much each person or group should pay
examples: I’ll pay – we can settle up later.
Let’s settle up with the waiter and get out of here.

glosses.meaningKo: 두 가지를 서로 맞거나 일치시키거나, 이렇게 맞거나 일치시키기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make two things fit or match each other, or to fit or match in this way
glosses.sourceDescription: to make two things fit or match each other, or to fit or match in this way
examples: I was convinced that a way needed to be found to marry up the two groups.
Our approach is to marry up the business problem with the technology.

glosses.meaningKo: 들어 올리거나 높이다
glosses.englishDescription: to raise someone or something to a higher position or level
glosses.sourceDescription: same as lift
examples: He lifted up the heavy bags.
We could hear the gospel groups lift up their voices.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 곳에서 물건을 주워서 모아두기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to pick up things from several different places and put them together
glosses.sourceDescription: to pick up things from several different places and put them together
examples: Janet quickly gathered up her books and left the classroom.
You have ten minutes to get below and gather up your kits and get back up here.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 물건을 넣을 만큼 공간이 충분하다
glosses.englishDescription: if you can fit a person or thing somewhere, there is enough space for you to put them there
glosses.sourceDescription: if you can fit a person or thing somewhere, there is enough space for you to put them there
examples: This small desk should fit into the reading corner.
We fit the extra chair into the narrow space.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건을 같이 맞추면, 맞는 방법으로 함께해서 무언가를 만들어 낸다
glosses.englishDescription: if you fit things together, you join them in the right way to make something
glosses.sourceDescription: if you fit things together, you join them in the right way to make something
examples: I’ve got all the pieces; now I just have to fit them together.
We have all the evidence but we don’t know yet how it fits together.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가나 무언가를 좋아하기 시작하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to begin to like someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to begin to like someone or something
examples: It might take them a while to warm to the idea.
She’s the kind of person you warm to immediately.

glosses.meaningKo: 따뜻해지다
glosses.englishDescription: to become warm
glosses.sourceDescription: to become warm
examples: The soup warmed up slowly on the stove.
The room will warm up when the sun appears.

glosses.meaningKo: 목록에 있는 무언가를 통해 선을 그어 당신이 그것을 처리했음을 보여주는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to draw a line through something on a list to show that you have dealt with it
glosses.sourceDescription: to draw a line through something on a list to show that you have dealt with it
examples: "" Most likely she'll be between the ages of twenty and forty, but knowing Richie, don't cross off anyone under seventy-five.
The children say their names, and you cross them off.

glosses.meaningKo: 이전과 다른 집단이나 유형에 속하기 시작하다
glosses.englishDescription: to start to belong to a different group or type from before
glosses.sourceDescription: to start to belong to a different group or type from before
examples: The artist crossed over from painting to digital design.
The band crossed over into a wider pop audience.

glosses.meaningKo: 손짓으로 사람이나 차량이 입구를 지나가도 된다고 알리다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a signal with your hand that shows you are allowing a person or vehicle to go through a gate or other entrance
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a signal with your hand that shows you are allowing a person or vehicle to go through a gate or other entrance
examples: A helper waved the families through the entrance.
The crossing guide waved our bus through the gate.

glosses.meaningKo: 바람 때문에 무언가가 넘어지다
glosses.englishDescription: if something blows down or is blown down, the wind makes it fall
glosses.sourceDescription: if something blows down or is blown down, the wind makes it fall
examples: Strong wind can blow our cardboard sign down.
A gust may blow the chair down.

glosses.meaningKo: 바람 때문에 무언가가 떨어져 나가다
glosses.englishDescription: if something blows off or is blown off, the wind makes it come off
glosses.sourceDescription: if something blows off or is blown off, the wind makes it come off
examples: The wind can blow my hat off near the playground.
A breeze may blow the paper cover off the box.

glosses.meaningKo: 불어서 불을 끄다
glosses.englishDescription: to put out a flame by blowing on it
glosses.sourceDescription: same as blow
examples: He blew out all 60 candles on his birthday cake.
We had to blow out the candles first, and when we'd done so I heard myself say, `There go twenty-one wasted years of our married life.

glosses.meaningKo: 시험 준비나 회의 등을 위해 열심히 공부하거나 무언가를 배우기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to study hard or learn about something in order to prepare for a test, meeting etc
glosses.sourceDescription: to study hard or learn about something in order to prepare for a test, meeting etc
examples: He’s boning up for his final exams.
She boned up on the company before the interview.

glosses.meaningKo: 매우 더웠을 때 더 시원해지기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to become cooler after being very hot
glosses.sourceDescription: to become cooler after being very hot
examples: Unable to sleep, she decided to run a tepid tub, something she did when she needed to cool off.
We went for a swim to cool ourselves off.

glosses.meaningKo: 자신과 매우 비슷해서 누군가 누군가를 떠올리게 하거나 다른 것을 떠올리게 하는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone think of someone or something else because of being very similar to them
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone think of someone or something else because of being very similar to them
examples: It’s a strange taste – it reminds me of melons.
She was tall and dark, and reminded me of my cousin Sarah.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 만나 연애를 시작하거나, 두 사람이 서로 관계를 맺기를 원하기 때문에 두 사람을 하나로 묶는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to start a romantic relationship with someone, or to bring two people together because you want them to have a relationship with each other
glosses.sourceDescription: to start a romantic relationship with someone, or to bring two people together because you want them to have a relationship with each other
examples: All our friends seem to be pairing off.
They paired me off with a gorgeous man.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 의지하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to depend on someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to depend on someone
examples: Everybody needs someone to lean on in times of trouble.
Rosie Quantock sensed his annoyance for she said at once,'I'm here for Delia to lean on.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 다른 사람들과 떨어진 곳에 있게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to put someone in a place where they are kept apart from other people
glosses.sourceDescription: to put someone in a place where they are kept apart from other people
examples: Mina shut herself away in the study for a quiet hour.
The artist shut himself away to finish the mural.

glosses.meaningKo: 기계가 꺼지거나 기계를 꺼서 작동을 멈추게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: if a machine shuts off, or if someone shuts it off, it stops working
glosses.sourceDescription: if a machine shuts off, or if someone shuts it off, it stops working
examples: The fan shuts off automatically after one hour.
Please shut the projector off when class ends.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 닫아놓으면, 그것을 보고, 듣고, 생각하지 못하게 된다
glosses.englishDescription: if you shut something out, you stop yourself from seeing it, hearing it, or thinking about it
glosses.sourceDescription: if you shut something out, you stop yourself from seeing it, hearing it, or thinking about it
examples: He closed the door to shut out the noise.
I tried to shut the incident out of my mind.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가가 말을 끊거나 소리를 지르는 것을 멈추게 하기 위해서입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone stop talking or making a noise
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone stop talking or making a noise
examples: He wishes us to enjoy ourselves, which means I must shut up immediately.
I wish he’d shut up about his holiday.

glosses.meaningKo: 비처럼 위에서 많이 쏟아지다
glosses.englishDescription: to fall from above in large quantities
glosses.sourceDescription: same as rain
examples: Colorful paper petals rained down after the school show.
Golden leaves rained down from the trees in the wind.

glosses.meaningKo: 무엇이 마르거나, 말리면 물이 다 마르거나 표면에서 닦아집니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something dries off, or if you dry it off, all the water dries or is wiped from its surface
glosses.sourceDescription: if something dries off, or if you dry it off, all the water dries or is wiped from its surface
examples: He got out of the shower and dried himself off.
Wash the salad and leave it to dry off.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가의 소유이다
glosses.englishDescription: to be owned by someone
glosses.sourceDescription: to be owned by someone
examples: This notebook might belong to her.
These books belong to the school library.

glosses.meaningKo: 내용물을 완전히 비우다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove everything from inside a container or place
glosses.sourceDescription: same as empty
examples: He emptied his clothes out of the drawers.
He was told to empty out his desk and leave.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가와 다시 전화하기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to phone someone again
glosses.sourceDescription: to phone someone again
examples: Either ring back or ask callers to ring back at a specified time - and make sure you do it.
I’ll ring back later.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 사람 또는 회사 등과 전화하여 무언가를 정리하거나 정보를 얻습니다
glosses.englishDescription: to phone several people or companies etc in order to arrange something or to get information
glosses.sourceDescription: to phone several people or companies etc in order to arrange something or to get information
examples: I’ll ring round some of my friends and see if they can help.
Ring round a few people who offer clipping.

glosses.meaningKo: 특정한 유형으로 표시하다
glosses.englishDescription: to identify or classify someone as a particular type
glosses.sourceDescription: same as mark
examples: She immediately marked him as a troublemaker.
The glasses and the books marked him as a student.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건의 가격을 낮추다
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce the price of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce the price of something
examples: The shop marked all winter hats down today.
They marked down the notebooks before the new term.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 다른 사람들과 구별되게 하거나 특정 역할에 적합함을 보여주다
glosses.englishDescription: to distinguish someone from others or show that they are suited for a particular role
glosses.sourceDescription: to show that someone or something will do something in the future
examples: His talent has marked him out as one of the greatest runners ever.
It was the kind of singing voice that marks someone out for a professional career.

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것에서 이익을 얻다
glosses.englishDescription: to make a profit from something
glosses.sourceDescription: to make a profit from something
examples: Local farmers profit from the weekend market.
The small shop profited from its popular new design.

glosses.meaningKo: 전자 메시지를 주고받도록 컴퓨터나 시스템을 연결하다
glosses.englishDescription: to connect computers or computer systems so that electronic messages can be sent between them
glosses.sourceDescription: to connect computers or computer systems so that electronic messages can be sent between them
examples: We linked the classroom computers up to share files.
The library will link up its two computer systems.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에 대한 정보를 찾으려고 노력하거나
glosses.englishDescription: to try to find out information about someone or something
glosses.sourceDescription: to try to find out information about someone or something
examples: A few kids were nosing around.
I found two men nosing around the boat.

glosses.meaningKo: 기회나 힘 등을 놓쳐 더 이상 가지지 못하게 되다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as power or an opportunity slips away, you stop having it
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as power or an opportunity slips away, you stop having it
examples: The chance to join the trip slipped away.
This helpful opportunity could slip away soon.

glosses.meaningKo: 대화나 연설에 말을 눈에 띄지 않게 슬쩍 넣다
glosses.englishDescription: if you slip a remark into a conversation, speech etc, you make sure that you say it in a way that is not too obvious
glosses.sourceDescription: if you slip a remark into a conversation, speech etc, you make sure that you say it in a way that is not too obvious
examples: Mina slipped a kind remark into the conversation.
He slipped the reminder into his short speech.

glosses.meaningKo: 뭔가의 주요 부분을 남기기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to leave the main part of something
glosses.sourceDescription: to leave the main part of something
examples: A small group of soldiers branched off into the jungle.
Lanes branch off the main road, leading to the coast.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 좋아하지 않지만 바꿀 수 없는 사람 또는 무언가에 대해 반응하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to react against someone or something that you do not like but cannot change
glosses.sourceDescription: to react against someone or something that you do not like but cannot change
examples: How can you kick against that?
Katherine has an instinct for kicking against the establishment.

glosses.meaningKo: 뚜렷한 계획 없이 어떤 곳에서 시간을 보내다
glosses.englishDescription: if people are kicking around, or kicking around a place, they are in that place without any definite plans
glosses.sourceDescription: if people are kicking around, or kicking around a place, they are in that place without any definite plans
examples: We kicked around the park until it was time for lunch.
The friends kicked around town with no fixed plan.

glosses.meaningKo: 긴장을 풀기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to relax
glosses.sourceDescription: to relax
examples: At 5:00 we can kick back and forget about work.
With such responsibility on his shoulders during the week, where does he go to kick back on his day off?

glosses.meaningKo: 어떤 것을 성취하는 데 도움이 되는 행운이나 우연과 같은 것에 의존하기 위해, 일반적으로 다른 선택의 여지가 없기 때문입니다
glosses.englishDescription: to depend on something such as luck or chance to help you to achieve something, usually because you have no other choice
glosses.sourceDescription: to depend on something such as luck or chance to help you to achieve something, usually because you have no other choice
examples: Again, trusting to instinct normally does the job just fine.
You can be as prepared as you want, but at some point you have to trust to instinct.

glosses.meaningKo: 눈이나 시선을 누군가나 무언가에 고정시키면, 그 사람을 똑바로 바라보고 다른 것은 아무것도 안 한다
glosses.englishDescription: if you fix your eyes or your attention on someone or something, you look straight at them and at nothing else
glosses.sourceDescription: if you fix your eyes or your attention on someone or something, you look straight at them and at nothing else
examples: I kept my eyes fixed on the horizon.
She fixed her gaze on Jeff.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 당신이 느끼는 모든 것을 말해주는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to tell someone everything that you are feeling
glosses.sourceDescription: to tell someone everything that you are feeling
examples: She began pouring out her fears about the future.
She wrote him a long letter, pouring her heart out.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 조각조각 뜯어 완전히 망가뜨리다
glosses.englishDescription: to damage or destroy something completely by breaking it into pieces
glosses.sourceDescription: to damage or destroy something completely by breaking it into pieces
examples: The puppy may tear the cardboard box apart during playtime.
We can tear the model apart for recycling.

glosses.meaningKo: 빠르고 부주의하게 옷을 벗기세요
glosses.englishDescription: to remove your clothes quickly and carelessly
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove your clothes quickly and carelessly
examples: The boys tore off their clothes and jumped into the water.
The gorilla had to run for its life, tangled in the sheet, while trying to tear off the mask.

glosses.meaningKo: 종이나 천 등을 잡아당겨 여러 조각으로 찢다
glosses.englishDescription: to destroy something such as a piece of paper or cloth by pulling it into pieces
glosses.sourceDescription: to destroy something such as a piece of paper or cloth by pulling it into pieces
examples: Mina tore up the scrap paper for the collage.
We tore the old fabric up into narrow strips.

glosses.meaningKo: 얼굴이나 눈빛이 흐려지며 부정적인 감정을 드러내다
glosses.englishDescription: if your face or eyes cloud over, they show a negative emotion
glosses.sourceDescription: if your face or eyes cloud over, they show a negative emotion
examples: His face clouded over when the trip was delayed.
Mina's eyes clouded over at the disappointing news.

glosses.meaningKo: 당겨져 더 길거나 넓어지다
glosses.englishDescription: to become longer or wider by pulling
glosses.sourceDescription: to become longer or wider by pulling
examples: This soft band can stretch to twice its usual length.
The fabric can stretch to twice its width.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가가 넘어지거나 누군가나 무언가가 넘어지면 옆으로 넘어집니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something tips over, or if someone or something tips it over, it falls onto its side
glosses.sourceDescription: if something tips over, or if someone or something tips it over, it falls onto its side
examples: He just tipped over lightly on a carpeted floor.
He tipped his drink over.

glosses.meaningKo: 여러 몫이나 집단으로 나누다
glosses.englishDescription: to separate people or things into groups or parts
glosses.sourceDescription: same as divide
examples: Divide the children up into groups of four.
Let’s divide up into groups now.

glosses.meaningKo: 먼저 신중하게 생각하지 않고 무언가를 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to do something without first thinking carefully about it
glosses.sourceDescription: to do something without first thinking carefully about it
examples: I swore to myself I wouldn’t rush headlong into another romance.
Try not to rush into a decision you may later regret.

glosses.meaningKo: 공식 또는 법률 업무를 평소보다 더 신속하게 처리하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to deal with official or legal business more quickly than usual
glosses.sourceDescription: to deal with official or legal business more quickly than usual
examples: The legislation had been rushed through parliament.
When something is rushed through, they tend to make bad laws.

glosses.meaningKo: 둘이 같거나 비슷한 특성을 지녀 서로 들어맞다
glosses.englishDescription: if one thing matches up with another, or if they match up, they are the same or have similar qualities
glosses.sourceDescription: if one thing matches up with another, or if they match up, they are the same or have similar qualities
examples: The two lists match up in every detail.
Your answers match up with the answer key.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 개선하거나 더 성공적으로 만들기 위해 돈을 쓰는 것
glosses.englishDescription: to spend money on something in order to improve it or make it more successful
glosses.sourceDescription: to spend money on something in order to improve it or make it more successful
examples: I think it’s time I invested in a new computer.
This government believes in investing in education.

glosses.meaningKo: 가능성 또는 선택의 수를 줄이기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to reduce the number of possibilities or choices
glosses.sourceDescription: to reduce the number of possibilities or choices
examples: That narrowed it down to just two possibilities.
We’re working to narrow down the list of possible suspects.

glosses.meaningKo: 땅의 한 구역을 잔디로 덮다
glosses.englishDescription: to cover an area of ground with grass
glosses.sourceDescription: to cover an area of ground with grass
examples: The workers grassed over the bare patch beside the path.
We plan to grass over the empty corner of the yard.

glosses.meaningKo: 사람이나 무언가를 어떤 곳에서 내쫓다
glosses.englishDescription: to force someone or something to leave a place
glosses.sourceDescription: to force someone or something to leave a place
examples: The group decided to cast out a member who kept breaking its rules.
In the tale, the council chose to cast the giant out of town.

glosses.meaningKo: 아이디어를 격식 없이 이리저리 이야기하다
glosses.englishDescription: to discuss ideas in an informal way
glosses.sourceDescription: to discuss ideas in an informal way
examples: We knocked around a few ideas for the class picnic.
The team knocked the poster ideas around after lunch.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가에게 매우 강한 인상을 주다
glosses.englishDescription: to impress someone very much
glosses.sourceDescription: to impress someone very much
examples: Mina's piano performance knocked the audience out.
The bright mural will knock visitors out.

glosses.meaningKo: 방이나 건물을 분리하는 벽을 없애 두 개의 방을 하나의 방이나 건물로 만드는 것이다
glosses.englishDescription: to make two rooms or buildings into one room or building by removing a wall that separates them
glosses.sourceDescription: to make two rooms or buildings into one room or building by removing a wall that separates them
examples: The six-bedroom property is made up of two Victorian terraced houses knocked together to make a large home for an extended family.
The two cottages had been knocked together.

glosses.meaningKo: 급히 만들어 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to make or prepare something quickly
glosses.sourceDescription: same as knock
examples: It doesn’t take long to knock up some pasta.
You can't just knock up a few tons of maraging steel in the back streets of Cairo, it's not that easy.

glosses.meaningKo: 다른 것에 무언가를 놓기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to put something around something else
glosses.sourceDescription: to put something around something else
examples: Each cake has a bright red ribbon wrapped round it.
We see couples with their arms wrapped round each other.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가 원하지 않을 때 상황에 휘말리게 하기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone become involved in a situation when they do not want to
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone become involved in a situation when they do not want to
examples: Friends will be dragged into the argument.
My friend went mad about being dragged into our rows.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 원하거나 생각하는 것보다 더 오래 지속하는 것이 필요하다고 생각하는 것보다 더 오래 지속하는 것이 필요하다
glosses.englishDescription: to continue for longer than you want or think is necessary
glosses.sourceDescription: to continue for longer than you want or think is necessary
examples: This has been dragging on for months now.
This has dragged on for months.

glosses.meaningKo: 비나 강 같은 것이 무언가를 씻으면 그것을 운반합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if something such as rain or a river washes something away, it carries it away
glosses.sourceDescription: if something such as rain or a river washes something away, it carries it away
examples: Forecasters said the snow would be washed away quickly by rain - but that prospect sparked flood warnings.
Heavy rains have washed away the bridge.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건을 씻거나, 더러워진 물건이 있으면 세탁하여 제거합니다
glosses.englishDescription: if you wash dirt off something, or if dirt washes off, you remove it by washing
glosses.sourceDescription: if you wash dirt off something, or if dirt washes off, you remove it by washing
examples: Don’t worry about the dirty marks. They’ll wash off easily.
Wash all the soil off before you cook the potatoes.

glosses.meaningKo: 무언가를 갑자기 아주 큰 소리로 외치다
glosses.englishDescription: to say something suddenly in a very loud voice
glosses.sourceDescription: to say something suddenly in a very loud voice
examples: Mina shouted out the answer when she remembered it.
Please shout the number out so everyone can hear.

glosses.meaningKo: 단단한 물체에서 작은 조각을 도구에 쳐서 제거합니다
glosses.englishDescription: to remove small pieces from something hard by hitting it with a tool
glosses.sourceDescription: to remove small pieces from something hard by hitting it with a tool
examples: She was chipping away at the ground with a trowel.
Use a hammer to chip away the edge.

glosses.meaningKo: 당신이 온 방향으로 돌아가서 돌아가기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to turn and go back in the direction that you have come from
glosses.sourceDescription: to turn and go back in the direction that you have come from
examples: One frequently sees them flying alongside a hedge, just keeping ahead of one, then doubling back.
When you get to the roundabout, you need to double back on yourself.

glosses.meaningKo: 물건을 잠금장치가 있는 곳이나 용기에 넣어 두다
glosses.englishDescription: to put something in a place or container which you fasten with a lock
glosses.sourceDescription: to put something in a place or container which you fasten with a lock
examples: Please lock the art supplies away after class.
Mina locked her passport away in a small safe.

glosses.meaningKo: 시스템에서 누군가나 무언가를 관여시키기 위해, 시스템에서 쉽게 벗어날 수 없는 방식으로 계획 등을 한다
glosses.englishDescription: to involve someone or something in a system, plan etc in such a way that they cannot easily escape from it
glosses.sourceDescription: to involve someone or something in a system, plan etc in such a way that they cannot easily escape from it
examples: The currency is now locked into the European Monetary System.
Their strategy is to lock subscribers into long-term contracts.

glosses.meaningKo: 옷에 묻은 먼지나 흙을 털어 내다
glosses.englishDescription: to wipe dust or dirt off your clothes
glosses.sourceDescription: to wipe dust or dirt off your clothes
examples: Leo dusted his jacket off before entering the room.
Mina dusted off her coat after sitting on the bench.

glosses.meaningKo: 코나 입을 통해 폐로 공기를 들이마시기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to take air into your lungs through your nose or mouth
glosses.sourceDescription: to take air into your lungs through your nose or mouth
examples: It hurts when I breathe in.
They needed medical treatment after breathing in toxic fumes.

glosses.meaningKo: 코나 입을 통해 폐에서 공기를 내보내기 위해
glosses.englishDescription: to send air out of your lungs through your nose or mouth
glosses.sourceDescription: to send air out of your lungs through your nose or mouth
examples: Now breathe out slowly.
We breathe in air and breathe out carbon dioxide.

glosses.meaningKo: 많은 사람 또는 물건을 많은 수 또는 양으로 장소에 넣기 위해서
glosses.englishDescription: to fit a lot of people or things into a place in large numbers or quantities
glosses.sourceDescription: to fit a lot of people or things into a place in large numbers or quantities
examples: More than 120 people are packed into a small wood-panelled room in the roof.
There are about 45 people packed into the room with me.

glosses.meaningKo: 누군가를 장소나 일, 참여하던 것에서 나가게 하다
glosses.englishDescription: to make someone leave a place, their job, or something that they are involved in
glosses.sourceDescription: to make someone leave a place, their job, or something that they are involved in
examples: A login error booted Mina out of the class website.
The game booted us out when the session ended.

glosses.meaningKo: 대개 긴장해서 손가락으로 물건을 계속 만지작거리다
glosses.englishDescription: to keep touching or moving something with your fingers, usually because you are nervous
glosses.sourceDescription: to keep touching or moving something with your fingers, usually because you are nervous
examples: Mina toyed with a pencil while waiting for her turn.
He toyed with the button on his sleeve during the talk.
